articles.title: This Filipino couple has one of the biggest private collections of Yayoi Kusama’s art
articles.summary: Lito and Kim Camacho have over 100 works of the late Japanese avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama in various mediums

items: Filipino couple Lito and Kim Camacho are passionate collectors of Yayoi Kusama's art, having built a collection of over 100 pieces since their first encounter with her work in 2004.

Their collection has been showcased internationally, including a significant exhibition at the National Gallery Victoria in Melbourne, where they loaned nine pieces, attracting over half a million visitors.
The couple's admiration for Kusama extends beyond collecting; they have met her in person and expressed their desire to hold a major retrospective of her works in the future.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Filipino couple Lito and Kim Camacho are among the world’s ardent collectors of the late Japanese avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama (who died on August 14), with dozens of pieces in their home in an exclusive village in Makati City.

Lito was a former finance secretary during the early years of the Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo administration. When Newsbreak magazine interviewed his wife Kim in 2002, she was then the country manager and representative for Sotheby’s, one of the world’s biggest auction houses for art and real estate. At the time, they were not yet collectors of Kusama’s works.

The Camachos have such a wide collection that they’ve been invited to display some of Kusama’s works in special exhibits abroad. For instance, they loaned nine of their pieces for the Yayoi Kusama exhibition held at the National Gallery Victoria (NGV) in Melbourne, Australia, more than a year ago. The exhibit, which displayed nearly 200 of Kusama’s artworks, ran from December 15, 2024 to April 21, 2025, and was attended by over half a million visitors.

Among the pieces displayed from the Camacho collection were Kusama’s Sex Obsession painting and her Statue of Venus Obliterated by Infinity Nets sculpture. Sex Obsession can be viewed at 1:27 into this Yayoi Kusama overview video below published by NGV Melbourne, while Statue of Venus Obliterated is shown at 1:31.

blocks.caption: This Filipino couple has one of the biggest private collections of Yayoi Kusama’s art

blocks.text: The Camachos first encountered Kusama artworks during the couple’s visit to Japan in 2004, or 22 years ago, when Kusama’s popularity was starting to peak. Upon the invitation of the Japanese government, they visited Tokyo, where there was a retrospective on Kusama at the National Museum of Modern Art.
Kim had not heard of Kusama prior to that, but she was wowed by her works of art.

“I was immediately attracted to her works because they were so different. There was something very original and fresh about them, and the retrospective showed how adept she was at different mediums: she started with very small watercolors, moving to acrylic on canvas and sculptural pieces, and eventually entire room installations. Her versatility, sense of fun, originality and uniqueness were just outstanding!” she said in an interview with Art Outreach, a Singapore-based nonprofit visual arts organization, published in 2021.

Upon his wife’s insistence, Lito said he made sure to also include in his itinerary a visit to the museum, spent an hour looking at Kusama’s work, and was “awed by Kusama’s art as Kim was,” he said in the same interview with Art Outreach.

blocks.caption: This Filipino couple has one of the biggest private collections of Yayoi Kusama’s art

blocks.text: “You have to consider that she started her art back in the ’50s as a Japanese woman who had moved to New York, so she was an outsider, and yet she persisted. I also got a sense of her courage and strong conviction because she was not very successful in the early days. Even her works from the ’50s and ’60s remain as contemporary today, and that shows how significant and important her art is in history. I guess we just fell in love, and that was the start of our love affair with Kusama,” he said.

In 2005, when the Camachos moved to Singapore after Lito’s three-year stint in the Arroyo administration, they went to a Kusama exhibition in an art gallery, where they bought their first Kusama pieces. At that time, Lito said the “fairly small works” were still reasonably priced.

Kim did more research on Kusama, and the couple decided to “buy as many pieces” as they could given the still reasonable prices. “They were about 10% of what her prices are now. In some cases, even 1%,” she said.
Lito said they “were buying Kusama works wherever we could find them,” and within five years, they “had built enough of a collection to hold our own exhibition.”

“Our Kusama collection continues to grow as we have decided we’d like to hold a major retrospective one day that covers the full spectrum of her works from early to late, small to very large, and all the different mediums, so we still try to fill any gaps we have,” he added.
The couple now has over 100 pieces of Kusama’s works.

Among the popular Kusama works the Camachos purchased were a polka-dotted 300-kilo yellow pumpkin called Great Gigantic Pumpkin, installed in their home in Makati, and a Ladder to Home installation, purchased in 2006, which had amazed Kim when she first saw it in 2004.

“It is mind-boggling when you look up and down and see the ladder going endlessly into infinity. At the Singapore Biennale in 2006, which was the first biennale of Singapore, the work was displayed inside a Hindu temple. I went to see it and was still so impressed, so I persisted in enquiring when one became available, and that is the one we have now,” Kim told Art Outreach.
The ladder is installed in the Camachos’ main living room.
Lito, in an interview with ICON Magazine Singapore, described their Kusama collection as “very studied” and “very deliberate.”
“It’s the whole perspective of Kusama, from the earliest to the latest, in all the medium that she has done,” he said.
“So, from her early drawings and watercolors to works of acrylic on canvas…we have the longest work of Kusama, which is 100 meters long in soft sculpture,” Kim added in the same interview.

In an interview in 2017 with CoBo, a content platform for art enthusiasts, the Camachos said they got to meet Kusama in her studio and spent two hours — instead of an expected 15-minute encounter — with the artist when she was 84 years old.

blocks.caption: This Filipino couple has one of the biggest private collections of Yayoi Kusama’s art

blocks.text: “It was quite an experience; she’s almost childlike. You can tell there’s something very special about her,” Lito said. “We were warned before the visit that if we were able to get 10 or 15 minutes of her time, we’re doing very, very well…. So, we had expected to have a couple of photos, shake her hands, maybe have something signed, and that’s it.”

“I was so delighted with how warm she was to us. I thought she would be forbidding and like standoffish and impossible to touch. [But] no, she was so warm, allowed me to touch her hand,” Kim said. “She was very excited to be with us. She’s so nice.”
With Japan rising in popularity for Filipino tourists, the best place to see Kusama’s works is in her own five-story Yayoi Kusama Museum in 107 Bentencho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo, Japan.

blocks.caption: DOTS. White polka dots dominate the façade of the Yayoi Kusama Museum in Tokyo, Japan, in this photo taken in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

blocks.text: I got a chance to visit the museum in November 2019, when one could visit even without a booking in advance and without a specified and limited time slot.

blocks.caption: BALLOON. The lobby of the Yayoi Kusama Museum has bright red and white colors, with a small souvenir stand in this photo taken in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

blocks.text: There was a multi-color polka-dotted giant silver pumpkin on the top floor of the building.

blocks.caption: RAINBOW. A multi-colored, polka-dotted giant silver pumpkin installed at the top floor of the Yayoi Kusama Museum in Tokyo, Japan, in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

blocks.text: It also had a Ladder to Heaven installation with the warning, “For the protection of the artwork and your own safety, make sure not to step on the circular mirror at the bottom of the artwork.”

blocks.caption: INFINITY. A peek into Yayoi Kusama’s Ladder to Heaven art installation in her museum in Tokyo, Japan, in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

blocks.text: On what she aspired for in putting up the museum, Kusama said:
“I infused my eternal soul into this museum. I want you to be guided by my sincere desire: I wish for everyone to realize all the inspirations in my art.

blocks.caption: RED. A portrait of Yayoi Kusama with red hair hangs in her Tokyo museum in this photo taken in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

blocks.text: “The Museum will be a testament to my truth, that I have been living my life. Perhaps the museum can deliver love for all humanity, accompanying both life and death, seeking to attain the world’s supreme peace, having revealed out of all the love a hymn for humanity’s eternal life.
“This is my great hope in founding this museum.”

blocks.caption: FREE. No need to pay entrance fees to get a selfie with Yayoi Kusama’s giant pumpkin in Yokohama Art Museum in Odori Park. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

blocks.text: For those traveling to Fukuoka, there’s a Great Gigantic Pumpkin installed outside the Fukuoka Art Museum at the popular tourist spot, Odori Park. It is a cheap and quick way to get a photo with Kusama’s iconic art piece. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Tornado touched down near Elkhorn, Man., on Sunday: Environment Canada
articles.summary: A tornado touched down near a community in southwestern Manitoba on Sunday, Environment and Climate Change Canada has confirmed.

image.caption: Sunday's storms damaged this barn on Kelvin and Pat Siemen's farm near Kola, Man. (Submitted by Pat Siemens)

blocks.text: Manitoba
A tornado touched down near a community in southwestern Manitoba on Sunday, Environment and Climate Change Canada has confirmed.
1 confirmed, 1 possible tornado also reported in eastern Saskatchewan
A tornado was observed near Elkhorn, Man., 300 kilometres west of Winnipeg, around 6:30 p.m. Sunday, Environment Canada said. Reports of the tornado were made via the RCMP and social media.
The weather agency is collaborating with the Northern Tornadoes Project to investigate further and will provide more information once a preliminary assessment is done.
Storm damage was reported in the Manitoba community of Kola, just south of Elkhorn, Environment Canada meteorologist Shannon Moodie told CBC News on Monday.
The Northern Tornadoes Project said it's possible the tornado near Elkhorn began near Kola, Moodie said.
"So we're not sure if it's two tornadoes [or] if it's one. There could be more."
'Lost almost all our buildings'
A farmer near Kola said his family will be deciding Monday whether to rebuild, after the storms damaged most of their buildings, including a hay shed that "blew away."
It was raining "like crazy" when Kelvin Siemens said he heard a roar outside the farm on Sunday.
"We lost almost all our buildings," but their house was spared, Siemens said Monday.
He's going to speak with his insurance company before a family meeting to discuss next steps, he said.
"I'm not a young man anymore, and how much do we, or will we, rebuild?"
Siemens said he's certain they will rebuild to some extent.
"I'm not quite ready to give up."
It's been a summer of wet weather in the area, with parts of southwestern Manitoba were previously walloped by torrential rains earlier this summer.
Kola received about 74 millimetres of rain on Sunday, while St-Lazare got about 41 mm and Duck Mountain Provincial Park got 37.8 mm, Moodie said.

Another confirmed tornado was seen near Maryfield, Sask., around 4 p.m. Sunday, the weather agency said. A possible tornado was also reported near Kelso, Sask., on Sunday, but there's insufficient evidence to prove that so far.

Parts of Manitoba will see some showers and non-severe, isolated thunderstorms on Monday, as the "pretty big" system over the Prairies that produced Sunday's storms has begun to settle down, she said.

items: Tornado confirmed, warnings issued as south and central Sask. walloped by extreme weather

blocks.text: Kurt Fuchs, who lives in Fleming, Sask., said he was driving home from his job in Virden, Man., when heavy rains forced him off the highway and into Elkhorn around 6:30 p.m. Sunday.
He took images of the town after the storm ripped the roof off a store's shed, which littered the streets alongside broken tree branches.
"It was really, really shocking," Fuchs told CBC News on Monday.
Dwayne Hohmann, division manager of the Twin Valley Co-op on the west side of Elkhorn, which is near where Fuchs took photos, said part of the roof of the store's lumber shed ripped off in the storm.
"It was a positive that nobody was injured, so that's what we're taking out of it," he said.
"We'll band together as a community and move forward."
With files from Alana Cole and Cory Funk

articles.title: In Saxony-Anhalt, Sven Schulze takes on far-right AfD
articles.summary: The AfD is way ahead in the polls in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt. But the young incumbent state premier insists he can stop the far right from leading a government for the first time…

image.caption: Saxony-Anhalt's State Premier Sven Schulze, of the right-wing CDU, hopes to be able to stay in office after the state election on Sept. 6Image: Peter Gercke/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: "It's far from decided." State Premier Sven Schulze likes to repeat his big campaign message over and over again ahead of the impending election in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on September 6. His audience, however, rarely responds with enthusiasm.

The German public and international media alike are watching this election closely. Never before has the Alternative for Germany (AfD) — classified by the domestic intelligence agency as "confirmed right-wing extremist" — had a better chance to take over a state government. The party is polling at over 40% compared to Schulze's center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) at around 23%.

Schulze is hoping the AfD will stay below 50% and so be unable to secure a majority in the state parliament — and, with no other party willing to join it in a coalition, the AfD would be unable to form a government. That would leave it up to Schulze to form a coalition, perhaps with as many as three partners, and remain in office.
"We are fighting for every single voter right now," he told DW on August 7.
CDU's Saxony-Anhalt candidate warns against AfD taking power
Young, family man, engineer, cyclist
Schulze was just 11 years old at the time of German reunification. Now, at 47, the qualified industrial engineer and father of three is the youngest of Germany's 16 state premiers.

He only took over leadership of the state at the end of January, when his predecessor, Reiner Haseloff — then 71 — retired after nearly 15 years in office. The early handover to Schulze was supposed to improve the younger man's prospects in the state election. After all, a sitting premier is said to enjoy an "incumbency bonus."

Schulze is now touring the state of 2 million inhabitants. On some days, he has been seen out and about on his bicycle, complete with cycling jersey and helmet, handing out ice cream on hot summer days, and engaging in small group discussions.

Aware that his party leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz, is not exactly popular in Germany right now, one of his recurring messages has been that he is not there "to sell the Berlin government's ideas to Saxony-Anhalt." Instead, he said, his task is "to bring issues from Saxony-Anhalt to Berlin." Not everyone in Merz's government is necessarily pleased about this message.
Celebrities welcome, chancellor not so much

This became particularly evident when Schulze appeared at campaign events in the state's larger cities alongside Dieter Hallervorden — an actor and comedian who is a household name in Germany, and who was born in Dessau in Saxony-Anhalt nearly 91 years ago.

Hallervorden, not previously known as a CDU supporter, has now joined Schulze on stage during the election campaign four times. The venues were packed, and the events easily ranked among the best-attended of Schulze's campaign.

The comedian showed no compunctions about criticizing the federal government's defense and arms export policies. During one of his musical performances, an image of protesters bearing a banner with the slogan "Stop the genocide in Gaza" was briefly visible in the background.

Schulze calmly rejected sharp criticism of Hallervorden's involvement from his party's headquarters in Berlin. He maintained that he did not share, and even rejected some of Hallervorden's views, but had shared the stage with him to demonstrate his commitment to freedom of speech. The AfD, Schulze noted, seeks to abolish freedom of speech, while he does not.
AfD a threat to German culture, says Schulze

Dessau is known around the world as being one of the homes of the Bauhaus movement, which propelled art and architecture into the modern era starting in 1919. The Nazis sought to stifle the movement when they took power in 1933.

Now, more than 90 years later, some members of the AfD have again been directly echoing the Nazis' language about the famous movement. In a speech to the state parliament last year, AfD representative Hans-Thomas Tillschneider described Bauhaus as a "wrong track of modernism" — a direct quote from the 1928 book "Art and Race" by architecture critic Paul Schultze-Naumburg, who influenced Nazi thought.
Schulze has accused the AfD of wanting to return to Germany's past eras of oppression, and sought to tie the far-right party to East Germany's communist dictatorship.

"When the AfD sings the GDR anthem at the end of its party events, it shows exactly what it wants: a return to the days of the GDR," Schulze told DW. "And I do not want us to wall ourselves in again, as happened here before. That is not what the people want."
What if Germany's far-right AfD party wins in Saxony-Anhalt?
Running a local campaign

At campaign events, Schulze has attempted to shift the focus away from federal or global political issues and toward the situation within his home state. He often cites local businesses that rely on foreign employees and on exports to worldwide markets.

Regarding healthcare and care for the elderly, he warns against simply adopting, without debate, the recommendations of a commission appointed by the federal government. That again has directly contravened Merz's message, who said that those recommendations, which some say contain several cuts to public services, should and would be followed to the letter.

But Schulze remains undeterred, and has vowed to keep discussing the issues that matter to the people of Saxony-Anhalt. "I trust the people here," he said. He added that he is counting on the people of Saxony-Anhalt to stand up against having their state "turned upside down."
At times, he gets straight to the point: this election, he says, boils down to "Sven Schulze or the AfD."
This article was originally written in German.

blocks.text: PAMPANGA — Flooding continued to affect several communities in Pampanga as intermittent rains and water flowing from upstream areas push water levels higher in rivers, waterways, drainage systems, and low-lying areas across the province.
According to the Pampanga Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council, 327 barangays in 20 local government units were affected by the flooding.
More than 17,000 individuals have been evacuated as rescue and evacuation operations continue in communities affected by rising floodwaters.

blocks.caption:
Floodwaters are currently below knee-deep around the Cathedral and City Hall areas in San Fernando, Pampanga as of August 31, 2026.

Amid the worsening situation, Governor Lilia Pineda and Vice Governor Dennis Pineda led an emergency inter-agency meeting with representatives from the Office of Civil Defense, Department of National Defense, Department of Social Welfare and Development, Department of Health, water and electric cooperatives, and several mayors.

The meeting focused on sustaining food supplies in evacuation centers, ensuring safe water supply particularly in Macabebe, providing additional medicines and medical assistance, augmenting relief goods in hard-to-reach areas, and deploying additional rescue personnel.

articles.title: Putin-Modi meeting at SCO: Can Russia-India ties hold?
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Modi and Russian President Putin are at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Kyrgyzstan as Moscow and New Delhi face rising tensions with Washington.

image.caption: Modi and Putin last met in December 2025, when Putin visited India for the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit [FILE: December 5, 2025]Image: Alexander Kazakov/Sputnik/REUTERS

blocks.text: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to meet in Kyrgyzstan's capital, Bishkek, on Monday on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit — a bloc often seen as a counterweight to US influence.
The meeting comes against the backdrop of the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran, which has disrupted global energy markets, and Russia's war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year.
India has remained engaged with the SCO while resisting efforts to turn it into an anti-Western bloc. Its position reflects a broader effort to maintain relationships with competing powers.

That approach is under greater pressure. Russia remains under Western sanctions over the war in Ukraine. Meanwhile, India has faced US pressure over its purchases of Russian oil, alongside wider trade tensions.
A former Indian ambassador to the US, Meera Shankar, told DW that India's relationship with Russia should not be seen as directed against the US.
"India has a long-standing strategic relationship with Russia. This is not directed against any country but intended to help India meet its national goals," said Shankar.
Energy ties deepen between India, Russia
Energy has become the most visible change in the India-Russia relationship.

Before 2022, when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, it supplied only a small share of India's crude imports. Discounted Russian oil rapidly changed that, making Moscow one of India's biggest suppliers.

It has also become the most contentious part of India's relationship with the US, which has pressed New Delhi to reduce its purchases from Russia. India maintains that securing affordable and reliable energy is a national interest.

The disruption to traditional energy supplies has made that calculation more complicated. This year's US-Israel war on Iran and disruption of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz have affected India's purchases from the Gulf and pushed up prices.
Shankar said India is responding by diversifying its sources of supply, including both Russia and the US.
"In the long run, a transition to a non-fossil fuel economy would strengthen India's energy independence. But this will not happen overnight," she added.
Until then, Shankar said, India will take steps it considers necessary to stabilize supplies and protect its people.
Future of India-Russia defense cooperation
Defense remains the other major pillar, but here the direction of travel is clearer: India's dependence on Russian equipment has been declining.
The Ukraine war has raised questions over Russia's production capacity, delivery schedules and ability to supply spare parts after decades as a major supplier of India's military hardware.
Why is India pivoting away from Russian weapons?

"India remains one of Russia's oldest and largest arms buyers, and perhaps the last major one," Aravind Yelery, an associate professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in the Indian capital, New Delhi, told DW.

"New Delhi is increasingly reluctant to commit to Russia's fifth-generation fighter program and has little appetite for new Russian hardware unless it can be incorporated into India's indigenous production plans," he added.
While India has diversified its purchases, that does not mean the defense relationship is disappearing.
However, the terms are changing, with India looking for a relationship that contributes to its own defense production, so that it can move away from simply buying finished systems.
The China question
Russia's growing dependence on China has also become an unavoidable part of the India-Russia equation.

Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in early 2022, China has become indispensable to Russia as a market, supplier and economic partner. That has reduced Moscow's ability to serve as a counterweight to Beijing.
Yelery sees an important distinction in the two relationships.
"Strategically, Russia's relationship with China remains structurally transactional, a dependence it can ill afford to compromise, whereas its relationship with India rests on partnership," he said.
Russia needs China trade more than ever
India still has reasons to keep Moscow close: energy, defense, access to the Russian market and a longstanding political relationship across Eurasia. But the strategic calculation has changed.
India's 'America plus' strategy
Strategic affairs expert C Raja Mohan said that Russia's growing dependence on China has changed its strategic value for India.
"Russia is no longer in a position to help India balance China," Mohan, a professor of American studies at Jindal Global University, told DW.
This changes India's expectations from the relationship with Russia.

The emphasis is increasingly on specific interests — energy security, defense supplies, trade and access to technology — while India's larger strategic weight increasingly rests on relationships with the US and its allies.
India has expanded defense and technology cooperation with Washington, while deepening ties with partners such as France and Israel.
Mohan describes this approach as an "America plus" strategy, whereby India maintains its partnership with the US while widening its engagement with other major powers.
"India is trying to reduce its exposure to American volatility, but it still recognizes that Washington is its most important partner," he said.
India's double bind: Trying to mollify Russia, US
What do Modi and Putin want?
Rajan Kumar, a professor of Russian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, said Putin wants reassurance that India will remain engaged with Moscow despite pressure from Washington.
"President Putin needs an assurance from Prime Minister Modi that India will not ditch Russia when the latter is facing the worst possible crisis after the 1990s," Kumar told DW.
He expects continuity rather than a dramatic reset. "I think it is more about continuation of existing ties amid US pressure," he added.

Energy trade and payment mechanisms, ways to increase Indian exports to Russia, defense cooperation and the two countries' assessments of the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran are likely to remain important.
The bigger test will come in Delhi in September, when Putin is expected to return for the BRICS summit.
The Bishkek meeting can keep the political relationship on track, but the Delhi talks will show whether that political continuity can produce progress on trade, energy, defense and technology.

The relationship is no longer what it was before the Ukraine war. Energy has become far more important, India's defense dependence is being recalibrated, and Russia's closeness to China has altered the strategic equation.

"The relationship has a value that goes beyond individual deals. Putin appears well aware that India carries an independent strategic weight that China's structural leverage cannot substitute," said Yelery.

articles.title: Mt. Apo Unesco Global Geopark bid advances after expert evaluation
articles.summary: KIDAPAWAN CITY — The bid of Mt. Apo, the country’s tallest peak, to be declared a United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (Unesco) Global Geopark has moved forward after…

blocks.text: KIDAPAWAN CITY — The bid of Mt. Apo, the country’s tallest peak, to be declared a United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (Unesco) Global Geopark has moved forward after experts conducted an evaluation, with supporters expressing optimism for a positive outcome.

Cynthia Fortin, Mount Apo Foundation Inc. (MAFI) program manager, said they showcased the foundation’s flagship initiatives, including safeguarding environmental resources and preserving the rich cultural traditions of the Indigenous Peoples (IPs) living within the Mount Apo Natural Park, to Unesco evaluators.
Fortin particularly emphasized the foundation’s grassroots environmental stewardship through the local Bantay Bukid (forest guards) initiative.
“These dedicated community members patrol ancestral lands to preserve sacred cultural sites and protect local biodiversity,” she said in a statement.
MAFI has been actively involved in Mt. Apo’s Geopark bid since initial preparations began in 2022, working alongside the Department of Environment and Natural Resources in Regions 11 and 12.
Unesco evaluators Dr. Guy Martin Martini of France and Chenggong Zhang of China conducted a five-day field evaluation mission from Aug. 17 to 21.

They visited Lake Agco hot springs and the Mount Apo Geothermal Production Field in this city; the newly opened museum managed by the Mt. Apo Geopark and the Protected Area Management Office (PAMO) in Barangay Kapatagan, Digos City; and the Bagobo Tagabawa Cultural Village in Sta. Cruz, Davao del Sur.

The PAMO museum highlights geo-heritage, geoconservation efforts, geosites, biodiversity and cultural heritage within Mt. Apo Natural Park. It also features rock specimens found in Mt. Apo and textiles showcasing the traditional clothing and practices of the IPs in the area.
“While Mt. Apo is famed for its ecological and geological significance, it is your culture that gives life to it,” Chinese Unesco evaluator Zhang said during their visit to the museum.
For his part, Martini stressed “that the indigenous community and their cultural heritage are the true keepers of Mt. Apo’s territory.”
Jimmy Mantawil, chairperson of Barangay Ilomavis here, which is at the foot of Mt. Apo, expressed optimism that Mt. Apo’s bid for Unesco Global Geopark recognition will be successful.

“This is not only about recognizing the mountain but also an opportunity to show to the world the beauty and significance of Mount Apo, while doing our best to preserve it for future generations,” he said on social media.
Mantawil said a Unesco Global Geopark inscription will help boost tourism and the local economy with the arrival of more visitors and other opportunities the recognition brings.
If its bid is successful, it will become the second Unesco Global Geopark in the country, after Bohol in the Visayas, which is famous for its Chocolate Hills.

Unesco Global Geoparks are single, unified geographical areas where sites and landscapes of international geological significance are managed with a holistic concept of protection, education and sustainable development.
There are currently 241 Unesco Global Geoparks in 51 countries.
So far, Mt. Apo, a declared protected area in the Philippines, was recognized as an ASEAN Heritage Park during the 2nd Asean Ministerial Meeting in Bangkok, Thailand, on Nov. 29, 1984. /mcm

articles.title: Two remaining living WWII veterans honored in Nueva Vizcaya
articles.summary: SOLANO Nueva Vizcaya -- Two remaining World War II veterans, both centenarians, were honored during the commemoration of National Heroes Day Held the Heritage Memorial Park here,on August 31. The…

blocks.text: SOLANO Nueva Vizcaya -- Two remaining World War II veterans, both centenarians, were honored during the commemoration of National Heroes Day
Held the Heritage Memorial Park here,on August 31.
The provincial government also paid tribute to a fallen member of the Philippine National Police Special Action Force ot SAF 44.
Governor Jose Gambito led the ceremony, joined by Rep.Timothy Joseph Cayton and Vice Governor Eufemia Ang-Dacayo.
The memorial park is the resting place of some Novo Vizcayano veterans who fought in World War II.
Private Alberto Ruizo and Private First Class Maximo Santiago, the province’s last living World War II veterans, each received P25,000 in financial assistance from the provincial government.

Provincial Social Welfare and Development Officer Flordelina Granada said the annual aid is provided under the Northern Valor Ordinance, authored by former Board Member Patricio “Patpat” Dumlao Jr. The ordinance grants P25,000 every year to living World War II veterans in Nueva Vizcaya.
Gambito said the freedoms enjoyed by Filipinos today were earned through the courage and sacrifice of the country’s heroes and veterans.

“Our heroes made sacrifices so that we could live in freedom. We can never fully repay what we owe them, but we can honor their legacy by protecting the democracy they fought for and by exercising our rights with responsibility,” Gambito said.
“Freedom must never be abused or taken for granted—it was won through the courage and sacrifice of those who came before us,” he added.
The provincial government also honored SPO2 Joel Bumidang Dulnuan of Barangay Ocapon, Villaverde, one of the 44 police commandos killed during the Mamasapano operation in Maguindanao in January 2015.
Dulnuan was among members of the PNP Special Action Force who died in the operation, now widely remembered as the Mamasapano clash.
Cayton said the bravery and patriotism of World War II veterans and fallen uniformed personnel would remain etched in the nation’s memory.
“To every veteran who offered strength and life for the country, we extend our heartfelt gratitude,” Cayton said.
The congressman also pledged to help secure funding for the purchase of a larger property that would serve as a burial ground for Novo Vizcayano heroes.

articles.title: Countries legally obliged to consider slavery reparations, says UN committee
articles.summary:
Guidance says states must implement ‘comprehensive measures’ to address legacy of racial discrimination

A UN committee has said countries are legally obliged to consider reparations for the…

blocks.text: A UN committee has said countries are legally obliged to consider reparations for the transatlantic slave trade and take other ⁠measures to address the enduring ⁠legacy of racial ​discrimination.

Guidance published on Monday by the committee on the elimination of racial discrimination (CERD) said the obligations arose from ⁠a legally binding 1965 convention on racial discrimination, not from the legal standards that existed when the slave trade took place.
The committee described the approach as a “paradigm ⁠shift” away from debates over historical responsibility that have often been used by governments to resist reparations ​claims.
“States parties must implement comprehensive reparatory measures for ‌people of African descent, ‌covering all aspects of remedies,” said the UN document, which may be cited in courtrooms.
At least 12.5 ‌million Africans were taken and sold between the 15th and 19th centuries in what CERD called the largest forced displacement in history.

Calls for reparations – ranging from official apologies to financial compensation – have gained momentum internationally, though opponents argue states and institutions should not be held responsible for historical crimes. The EU and Britain abstained from a UN resolution ‌on slavery in March.
Some states have sought to dodge claims for justice in courtrooms by arguing that there were no international laws outlawing the slave trade ​at the time – the so-called intertemporality principle.

But the UN document argues that, regardless of whether slavery and the slave trade were illegal under the laws of the day, countries remain responsible under current international obligations to tackle their continuing effects.

“Irrespective of the legal characterisation of the original historical acts, states parties remain bound ⁠by their present obligations under the convention to address structural inequalities,” the UN document ​says.
Financial compensation alone is ​not sufficient, it adds, urging “transformative” measures including ​opening archives, revising public memorials and establishing independent truth commissions.
after newsletter promotion
Pela Boker Wilson, a committee expert ​from Liberia who helped draft ‌the document, said ​she expected states ​to move beyond broad expressions of regret and review policies and laws.

“We are calling on state parties to take concrete and meaningful action,” she told Reuters. “We want to affirm the dignity of those whose suffering was denied, whose suffering was minimised or forgotten.”

articles.title: Drug personality resists arrest, is killed in gun raid in Negros
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - A 43-year-old suspected drug personality was killed after allegedly resisting arrest by the police in a gun raid in Barangay Inolingan, Moises Padilla, Negros Occidental on Sunday,…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY - A 43-year-old suspected drug personality was killed after allegedly resisting arrest by the police in a gun raid in Barangay Inolingan, Moises Padilla, Negros Occidental on Sunday, August 30.

Police tried to enforce a search warrant issued by a Regional Trial Court in La Carlota City, Negros Occidental on August 20 for illegal possession of firearms and ammunition against the suspect named Reynan, following reports of alleged threat and illegal discharge of firearm in the area.
Police Major Ryan Villasario, Moises Padilla police chief, said the suspect fled his home towards a mountainous area after sensing the presence of policemen.
While escaping, he reportedly fired several shots towards the operating team, prompting the latter to return fire due to imminent threat, leading to a one minute armed encounter.
Villasario said that a 12-gauge shotgun, an ammunition, and a .45 caliber colt pistol were recovered.
Villasario said they previously subjected the suspect to a buy-bust operation but he managed to escape. He was classified as a street level individual.
The suspect, considered by police as armed and dangerous, reportedly threatened his customers in the alleged illegal drug trade, according to Villasario.
Villasario said that operatives did not expect that it would lead to a shootout, but they also have to defend themselves.
If there is a complaint related to the incident, Villasario said that police operatives are willing to face it.

TARLAC - Gov. Christian Yap, together with Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials, conducted another inspection of two major bridges that collapsed and disrupted access between western Tarlac and the provincial capital on Monday, August 31.
Yap, accompanied by Tarlac City Mayor Susan Yap, discussed urgent measures to repair the damaged structures .
Likewise, identify alternative routes to ensure the continued movement of people, goods, and economic activities.
DPWH materials needed to construct a temporary bridge have already been delivered to Tarlac, with construction set to begin.
The inspection, conducted with the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO), also focused on assessing infrastructure damage and ensuring the safety of nearby residents.

articles.title: Italy extends Schengen suspension with Spain
articles.summary: Italy's far-right government announced that it will continue to exclude Spanish nationals from the free movement agreement for another 15 days.

image.caption: Many of the refugees left in Ceuta are minorsImage: Violeta Santos Moura/REUTERS

blocks.text: The government of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni will extend its suspension of the Schengen free movement agreement with Spain for another 15 days at least, Italian media reported on Monday.
Rome had already suspended the arrangement with Madrid for a month beginning on July 31, in response to an influx of migrants who crossed into the Spanish territory of Ceuta.
The incident, in which dozens of migrants died, triggered a massive European Union migration emergency and brought Spain's leftist government much criticism, including from Italy.
Spain's Ceuta grapples with aftermath of border chaos
What else do we know about Italy's extension?

Italy's Interior Ministry said the decision to extend the suspension was taken "due to the persistence of the factors that had led to the reintroduction of the measures on Aug. 1," without clarifying.
The ministry added that Italy was aware of "the steps already undertaken ⁠by ​Spain, together with the European Union, to ​help bring the situation in the area back to normal in the ​near future."
The announcement came despite the fact that nearly all of the some 70,000 people who had broken through the barrier returned to Morocco in the days after the incident.

Spain had responded to Italy's suspension by introducing its own border controls for passengers arriving from Italy and on Monday reportedly said it was extending this measure by 15 days, in an apparent tit-for-tat move.
Sanchez says Ceuta incident traced to Russian, Israeli agents

Socialist Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Monday that an "international far-right movement" with "links to Russia and Israel" had created a disinformation campaign on social media that led to the incident at the border fence in Ceuta.
Both Rabat and Madrid had earlier said that the crisis was exacerbated by incorrect information circulating on social media regarding a recent Supreme Court ruling.

"What we know so far is that a ruling by the Supreme Court of July 8 was distorted, which was spread on social networks through fake news, disinformation and also by criminal organizations that traffic in people," Sanchez told broadcaster SER on Monday.
He said there had been a concerted effort "to attack and divide not only Spain but also Europe," without providing further details.
Sanchez added that there was no evidence that Moroccan authorities had been responsible.
Some 5,000 migrants remain in Ceuta, Sanchez said, with at least 1,200 being minors.
Unaccompanied minors at risk of sexual assault in Ceuta

On Friday, Spain asked for help from the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) in processing the remaining migrants, amid rising protests against their presence by residents of the exclave.

Ceuta is bordered by Morocco on one side and the sea on the other, with no direct access to the mainland of the European Union, making it difficult for any asylum seekers to access the bloc from there.

articles.title: Laguna prov’l gov’t intensifies relief drive to help displaced families affected by flooding
articles.summary: CALAMBA CITY, Laguna — Governor Sol Aragones continue lead the delivery of direct assistance to families displaced by recent rains and flooding, reaching out to evacuation centers across Calamba City…

blocks.text: Laguna government conducted relief operations to families in Calamba and Cabuyao Cities affected by floods. (Photo via Danny Estacio)

CALAMBA CITY, Laguna — Governor Sol Aragones continue lead the delivery of direct assistance to families displaced by recent rains and flooding, reaching out to evacuation centers across Calamba City and Cabuyao City on Friday, August 29 .

According to the Provincial Public Affairs Office, relief missions were undertaken in five evacuation sites — three in Calamba City and two in Cabuyao City — distributing aid and checking on the condition of families temporarily sheltered away from their homes.
Aragones reiterated that her administration’s core directive to ensure every displaced Lagunense family receives the support they need.
“Our goal is clear — to reach all of you. No matter which barangay, no matter how far, we will make sure that every family affected by this calamity is reached and assisted,” the Arogones said.

The relief missions were carried out in close coordination with local barangay officials, ensuring that aid is delivered directly to the intended beneficiaries and that gaps in assistance are immediately identified and addressed .

Aragones emphasized that the relief operations are continuous, not one-off distributions. Assessment teams remain deployed across Laguna’s various districts to identify families still in need, whether in formal evacuation centers or staying with relatives .
The lady chief executive assured that the provincial government will sustain its presence and assistance in the affected communities until families can safely return to their homes and livelihoods.

articles.summary: LUCENA CITY, Quezon- Due to mistaken identity, a barangay watchman responding to an arrest was stabbed by the father of a female victim of acts of lasciviousness at the police station on Sunday…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY, Quezon- Due to mistaken identity, a barangay watchman responding to an arrest was stabbed by the father of a female victim of acts of lasciviousness at the police station on Sunday afternoon, Aug. 30, in this city.

The barangay tanod identified as Juan, 51, a businessman and a resident of PCA, Barangay Isabang, was stabbed by the suspect Mark, 38, a resident of Purok Ipil 3, Brgy. 9, and was arrested immediately.
Police did not mention if Juan was hurt or not.

At about 1:30 p.m., Juan, along with two other village watchmen of Brgy. Isabang and Angel, the victim proceeded to the Lucena City police station to turn over the suspect identified as Son after he was arrested for the crime of acts of lasciviousness.

While at the police station, the victim’s father, Mark, suddenly drew a bladed weapon (balisong) and stabbed Juan, allegedly after mistakenly identifying him as the suspect who had groped his daughter’s private part.
Police confiscated the bladed weapon, and the suspect is now in Lucena City Police custody and facing a charge of attempted homicide.

articles.title: Search continues for 18 passengers after ferry capsized in northern Cyprus
articles.summary: Eight people have died after the ferry started taking on water shortly after setting off for Turkey.

blocks.text: Rescuers are continuing their search for 18 passengers of a ferry which capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday.
The vessel, which was carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members, began taking on water soon after departing the coastal town of Kyrenia in the self-proclaimed Turkish republic on Cyprus.
Eight people have been confirmed to have died in the incident, while 19 are currently being treated at hospitals in northern Cyprus, local authorities say.
The ship's captain, seven crew members, and another man were arrested on Monday, while warrants have been issued for a further seven people.
Ünal Üstel, Prime Minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), which is only recognised by Turkey, announced a three-day period of national mourning.
The boat has completely sunk and is lying at a depth of 514m (1,686ft), officials say.
Debris remains scattered across the water, including a black wheelie suitcase bobbing on the surface and a sheet of steel that appeared to have broken away from the ferry.
Authorities are attempting to recover the vessel's black box recorder to establish what happened.
The privately owned ferry left the popular holiday resort of Kyrenia at about 12:30 (09:30 GMT), en route to the town of Tasucu in Turkey.
It had been scheduled to travel to Turkey on Saturday but its journey was delayed due to poor weather conditions.
Üstel told local media the boat was hit by two waves before it capsized.
While the captain of the vessel was trying to recover from the first wave, a second wave hit and it began taking on water, he said.
Among the missing are Ayten Bicer's two children - her 12-year-old daughter Miray and six-year-old son Mehmet Asaf.
She told local media she felt Miray slip out of her hands and disappear as they tried to cling on to the overturned boat.
"She was saying, 'Don't let go'. And I didn't let go of my daughter. I swear, I didn't let her go," Bicer said.

She said a suitcase fell on top of her which forced her daughter from her grip. She managed to grab hold of her daughter's foot, but her shoes were coated in engine oil from the overturned vessel and she slipped through her hands.
She and her husband, Hayri, are by the port in Kyrenia with other families as they await news of their loved ones.
The ferry - a high-speed 40m long, 10m wide Filo Jet vessel - sails under the flag of Turkey, according to Marine Traffic.
Filo Denizcilik, the company which operates the capsized passenger boat, said it was "deeply saddened by the tragic accident".
The TRNC controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, which has been divided since 1974.

articles.title: Cops seize P4.83-M shabu in Iloilo City
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY—An anti-drug operation seized more than P4.82 million worth of suspected shabu (crystal meth) in Iloilo City early Monday, August 31. Drug suspects with the aliases of "Jerome" and…

blocks.text: (Photo via Tara Yap)
ILOILO CITY—An anti-drug operation seized more than P4.82 million worth of suspected shabu (crystal meth) in Iloilo City early Monday, August 31.

Drug suspects with the aliases of "Jerome" and "Garry" yielded around 710 grams of shabu in a buy-bust operation conducted by the Iloilo City Police Office – Station 2 Drug Enforcement Team and in coordination with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA).
The police conducted a series of surveillance, validation and profiling before successfully arresting Jerome, who is classified as a high-value individual (HVI).
Brigadier General Randulf T. Tuaño, regional director of Police Regional Office (PRO-6), lauded the operation that would cut back the proliferation of illegal drugs in Iloilo City.

“This operation represents drugs that will no longer reach our communities to harm our youth and families. This proves that through effective intelligence, validation, coordination, and vital information provided by our fellow citizens, we are achieving concrete results against the illegal drug trade,” said Tuaño in a statement on Monday, August 31.
The duo is facing charges for violating Republic Act No 9165 or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act.

articles.title: Romualdez: Guteza's accounts unreliable even before recantation
articles.summary: The accounts of Orly Guteza, the former bodyguard of ex-Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, have long been unreliable before his recantation, the camp of former Speaker Martin Romualdez said Monday.

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 7:34pm
The accounts of Orly Guteza, the former bodyguard of ex-Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, have long been unreliable before his recantation, the camp of former Speaker Martin Romualdez said Monday.

Romualdez said that Guteza’s affidavit, which was submitted before the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee flood control probe, was found forged by the Manila Regional Trial Court in October 2025 because the signature on the supposed notarized affidavit was falsified and did not belong to the notary public stated in the document.
“Orly Guteza’s first affidavit was already under a cloud before he took it back,” the Romualdez camp said in a statement.

Likewise, the Leyte lawmaker's camp invoked the September 2025 denials of Co’s aides and bodyguards Mark Bunagan and Allan Colesio, whom Guteza identified as the ones who can corroborate his statements in his Senate blue ribbon panel affidavit.

“The document’s supposed notary denied signing it, a Manila court treated it as falsified, and the people Guteza named as possible corroborators rejected the alleged cash deliveries. This is why the Office of the Ombudsman cannot presume that Guteza’s first version is true and treat his recantation as the only disputed statement,” the Romualdez camp added, referring to Guteza’s recantation, which only happened this month.
The Romualdez camp also argued that Guteza’s allegations that certain individuals made him link Romualdez to the flood control mess should not be taken lightly by the Ombudsman.

“At the very least, these sworn statements materially impair the credibility and reliability of the principal witness pool of the complainant [Ombudsman] Special Panel of Investigators, taint the admissibility of the Affidavits attached to the Complaints, and prevent the Complaints from meeting the threshold of prima facie evidence with reasonable certainty of conviction,” Romualdez said in his counter-affidavit.
The Office of the Ombudsman is investigating Romualdez for plunder, graft, bribery and money laundering in connection with Guteza's allegations and the supposed defrauding of the national budget.

Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano earlier assured the public that the recantation of Guteza and three other previous accusers of Romualdez does not mean that the Ombudsman does not have evidence against Romualdez.

“Hindi po tama na dahil lang po may recantation, nabura na yung dati nilang sinasabi. Ang legal effect po niyan ay itatabi po yung dating affidavit doon sa bagong affidavit,” Clavano said in a press conference last week.
(To say that a recantation is an erasure of account is wrong. The legal effect of that recantation is that the new affidavit will be compared with the initial affidavit.)
“Dagdag ebidensya po yan. Hindi siya nakabawas sa ebidensya ng investigators natin,” Clavano added.
(That is additional evidence. The recantation did not reduce the evidence that our investigators already have.) —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Nepal floods test PM Balen's young government
articles.summary: A year after Gen Z-led protests swept Prime Minister Balendra "Balen" Shah to power, deadly floods are testing his government's ability to manage a national crisis.

image.caption: Rescue efforts continue to aid the tens of thousands impacted by the devastating floods, with roads smashed and bridges destroyedImage: Arun Sankar/AFP

blocks.text: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah, an ex-rapper popularly known as "Balen," is facing the enormous task of rebuilding communities and critical infrastructure following last week's deadly flash floods.
The floods, carrying rock, ice, mud and debris, swept through areas near the Chinese border, ravaging entire towns and damaging hydropower plants.
More than 900 people have been killed and nearly 4,800 remain missing, authorities said Monday, as rescue efforts entered a sixth day.

The devastating floods struck the Himalayan nation just days before the anniversary of the Gen-Z-led anti-corruption protests of September 8-9 last year that toppled the previous government and swept Shah to power.
Now, the 36-year-old prime minister and his largely inexperienced cabinet face their first major national crisis in what is shaping up to be the country's worst disaster in a decade.
Anxious relatives await news from flood zone
Rescuers, including Chinese and Indian experts, believe hundreds of workers are trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites under construction that were buried in mud by the catastrophic flooding.

blocks.caption: The death toll continued to rise on Monday as increasingly desperate families searched for their loved onesImage: Dar Yasin/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Sushila Giri was waiting for news of her son, Sishir, a Kathmandu University student completing an internship at one of the hydropower projects.
"I came to know that my son, along with others, was at the quarter of the hydro project when the disaster happened," she told DW. "Please help me find his whereabouts."
Gen Z activist Raksha Bam expressed concern about delays in rescuing workers trapped at hydropower projects and urged the government to seek specialized assistance from the international community.
Across affected districts, family members gathered in hospitals and temporary aid centers hoping for news of missing loved ones.

Indra Adhikari lost her home and paddy fields in the floods. Four of her relatives remain missing. She said rescue and relief efforts appeared concentrated in areas accessible by road and where media were present, particularly along one side of the Trishuli River.
"Most of those who have come to Trishuli Bazar are not rescuers but onlookers," she told DW. "Remote settlements farther upstream and across the river remain difficult to reach."
Nepal: Rapper-turned-politician set to become next PM
How is the new government handling the crisis?

The administration itself has acknowledged that it was not fully prepared for a disaster of such scale, which is the deadliest for Nepal since a 2015 earthquake killed thousands and injured many more.

"On the very first day, we got a bit confused as to how to deal with the crisis," Minister for Information and Communication Bikram Timilsina told DW after visiting the flood-hit area. "[From the] second day onwards, we have been putting all our efforts into swift search, rescue and relief works."

Security agencies have received praise for their response, particularly their efforts to reach people in inaccessible areas via helicopters. But the disaster has also exposed questions about the government's crisis-management capacity and its relationship with Nepal's provincial and local governments.

"Given the scale of devastation, the government's efforts and promptness to deal with the crisis are commendable," Madhu Raman Acharya, a former foreign secretary of Nepal, told DW. "The preliminary search and rescue efforts, especially coordination among security agencies, are commendable."
Govinda Pokharel, a former chief executive officer of the National Reconstruction Authority, which oversaw post-earthquake reconstruction, however, has a different take.

blocks.caption: Rescuers have been working to reach hundreds of workers trapped in tunnels of damaged hydropower projectsImage: Prime Minister Secretariat, Nepal/AFP

blocks.text: He said that the federal government had attempted to manage the crisis largely on its own, without adequately involving local and provincial governments. This is particularly significant because Shah's ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party has no presence in local or provincial governments.
Pokharel also questioned whether the government's lack of experience had affected its ability to gauge the scale of the response required.

"Our neighboring countries like China and India were willing to lend help for rescue, especially for tunnel-rescue from the very outset," he told DW, adding that the government failed to decide in time whether to allow them to deploy, costing three crucial days.
Can Balen's government deliver?
Nepal initially maintained that its own rescue teams were capable of handling the operation.

But by Friday, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal told the media that the government had decided to seek international expertise, including from China and India, for tunnel rescues, DNA testing and forensic examinations.
The shift highlighted one of the central challenges facing the new administration: whether the government can act quickly and effectively during a rapidly evolving national emergency.
Pokharel said the government's decision to raise substantial funds domestically for disaster relief demonstrated public confidence.
Nepal starts mass burials of hundreds ⁠of flood victims

"One good thing is that the government is collecting a huge sum of public money domestically on the Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund," he said. "It shows the public trust in the government that doesn't misuse its funds collected in the name of relief."

By Saturday, over 5 billion Nepali rupees ($34.7 million, €29.9 million) had been collected in a government-run disaster relief fund for flood victims, according to the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.

Prabha Bogati, deputy mayor of Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot, said local authorities had limited scope to act during the crisis because the federal government adopted a centralized "one-door" approach, requiring relief activities to be coordinated through a single command structure.
"In previous crises, local communities and volunteers used to be mobilized in search, rescue and relief efforts," she told DW.
Bogati added that helicopter rescues have been effective, but local stakeholders have not been brought into the response and have not been allowed to recover bodies or perform final rites.
Government spokesperson and Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel defended the administration's response, saying all available resources were being mobilized for rescue, relief and rehabilitation.

"In the first phase, our priority was to save citizens' lives by using the available human resources and means," Pokharel told reporters. "A process has also been initiated to better organize the mobilization of volunteers."
In Nepal, families cling to hope as thousands still missing

articles.title: Niger's failed coup exposes cracks in the military — and Russia's influence
articles.summary: The failed coup in Niger has brought deep divisions within the military to light. As Russia's support highlights the junta's fading influence, soldiers continue to face jihadi attacks, poor equipment…

image.caption: Niamey, Niger: Following the attempted coup, military units have moved into key positions across the capitalImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: What does it mean to be a soldier in Niger today? It means fighting jihadi groups under difficult conditions and at considerable personal risk for little pay, said Sahel expert Abdoulaye Sounaye, a professor at the Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient research institution in Berlin.

In an exclusive interview with DW, he described the hard conditions facing Nigerien soldiers: "The vast majority earn less than €150 [about $170] a month, and many have to support six, seven or more family members on that monthly salary."
"This naturally contributes to discontent within Niger's armed forces," he added, hinting at some of the motivation behind the increasing levels of discontent among soldiers.
At the same time, military personnel are expected to follow a strict military leadership which only came to power through a coup.
Junta vs. Islamists
At the top of this junta sits General Abdourahamane Tchiani, the erstwhile commander of the presidential guard prior to the military takeover in 2023.

Tiani ousted democratically elected President Mohamed Bazoum, with his junta largely justifying its rule by invoking the ongoing fight against jihadist violence in the country, which it claims the Bazoum administration had failed to sufficiently address.
But the failed uprising in Niamey puts that claim to the test amid growing frustration within the military over the unending battle against Islamist insurgencies.
On the weekend, parts of the army temporarily took control of Air Base 101 at Niamey's international airport, and attempted to advance toward the Presidential Palace and Niger's state broadcaster.
The government has described the incident as a mutiny.

But Senegalese governance expert Pape Ibrahima Kane told DW in an exclusive interview that "this was not just a mutiny, but an attempted coup. If this is not an attempted coup, then what does an attempted coup look like?"

blocks.caption: From left to right: Mali's Assimi Goita, Niger's Abdourahamane Tiani and Burkina Faso's Ibrahim Traore pose for photographs during the first ordinary summit of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) in Niamey, Niger, in July 2024Image: Mahamadou Hamidou/REUTERS

blocks.text: Growing frustration within the army
Niger's military has been fighting jihadist groups for years without managing to contain the violence.
The capital Niamey itself has come under attack several times this year alone.
For soldiers, this means that they're exposed to high risks daily, compounded by serious problems with equipment, supplies and logistics.

Kane describes an army struggling to move its troops and equipment across the country's vast territory. Whether the government has the financial resources to address these shortcomings meanwhile remains an open question.
There also appears to be growing frustration over military pay and work conditions.
Sahel expert Mamadou Mouth Bane sees the possible preferential treatment of the presidential guard over frontline units as one factor behind the discontent that resulted in the uprising.

"The men who are at the front are being neglected. They feel forgotten and treated worse" than the presidential units, Bane explained in a DW interview, highlighting that the junta cannot afford to alienate these soldiers.

The military uprising also highlights the junta's chief dilemma: The loyalty of its forces remain key to the current military rulers' ongoing grip on power, which in the light of the latest developments might just be slipping.
What's driving Russia's ambitious push into Africa?
Russia: Niger's security guarantor
The role of Russia's Africa Corps is also particularly significant in this context.
The force has taken over large parts of the former activities of Wagner mercenaries in Africa.

Following the failed mutiny against the Kremlin of Wagner Group chief Yevgeny Prigozhin and his mysterious death in a plane crash in August 2023, Russia quickly reorganized its operations in Africa, placing them more firmly under the control of its defense ministry.

In Niger, the Africa Corps has become an important security partner of the junta. During the latest uprising, Russian forces actively helped retake Air Base 101, according to a statement by Russia's ambassador — at the direct behest of the country's military rulers.

blocks.caption: Russia has engaged in under-the-radar military operations in several countries in AfricaImage: French Army/AP/picture alliance

blocks.text: By helping the Nigerien army put down an attack from within its own ranks, it is becoming evident that the role of the Africa Corps now reaches well beyond their stated objective of assisting with the military government's counterterrorism strategy.
Kane described Niger's reliance on the Africa Corps as a "strategic dependency" in his exclusive interview with DW, claiming that the junta would have fallen without Russian assistance.
"Without the Russian army, we would have a new government in Niger today," he stressed.
Is Tiani playing Russian roulette?
But there are further factors to take into consideration, which could challenge Kane's statement.
According to DW information gathered on the ground, the presidential guard and other forces loyal to the regime were also heavily involved in the response to the coup attempt.
Algeria — Niger's neighbor to the northwest — meanwhile also backed Niamey, deploying four Su-30 fighter jets to Niger.

The involvement of the Africa Corps was probably a decisive factor in the rapid suppression of the uprising, but not the only one, although it appears to have exposed Tiani's dependence on a foreign armed partner to ensure his grip on power.

blocks.caption: Fighting jihadist groups under difficult conditions: Soldiers stand guard during a military ceremony at the Martyr Quarter in NiameyImage: Ludovic Marin/AFP

blocks.text: A risk for the Sahel at large

It is evident that the Africa Corps alone cannot defeat the ongoing insurgency of jihadist groups; otherwise it would have solved the crisis by now after years of involvement in the region. Neither can it solve the Nigerien army's structural problems.
This makes Niger a test case for the strength of this security model pursued by the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), which is comprised of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso.
All three military juntas have increasingly been turning to Russia while distancing themselves from Western partners.

But Russian support can only help stabilize the juntas in the short term. As long as foreign forces have to take over critical security tasks, the underlying causes of the military crisis remain unresolved.

The failed coup attempt was ultimately a victory for Tiani's junta — but equally a warning sign about the state of Niger's armed forces, as in the face of mounting challenges, their loyalty to the regime can clearly no longer be taken for granted.
Can new AES Unified Force stamp out terror in the Sahel?
Correction, August 31, 2026: An earlier version of this article misspelled the name of Abdoulaye Sounaye. DW apologizes for the error.

articles.title: US Embassy alerts Philippine authorities on visa applicant's fake documents, warns vs. visa fraud
articles.summary: An applicant for a US visa was recently arrested after presenting fake documents, the US Embassy has said. In a social media post, the embassy said US consular officers inform Philippine authorities…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 7:30pm
An applicant for a US visa was recently arrested after presenting fake documents, the US Embassy has said.
In a social media post, the embassy said US consular officers inform Philippine authorities whenever they discover fraudulent Philippine documents in the visa application process.

“We take visa fraud seriously. Recently, the US embassy notified Philippine law enforcement about visa fraud, resulting in the arrest of an applicant using fake documents, ” the US Embassy video said.
“Here is what you need to know. When our consular officers discover fraudulent Philippine documents, we notify the Philippine government authorities,” it added.
The embassy said using fake documents or misrepresenting facts would result in a lifetime ban on entering the United States, as well as criminal prosecution and arrest.
“No secrets, no exceptions, no tolerance for fraud. Report visa scams and fraud to FBI Manila at state.gov,” the embassy said. –Mariel Celine Serquiña/NB, GMA News

articles.title: OCD: 330 barangays in Pampanga still flooded
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — More than 300 villages in Pampanga remain flooded, with some areas experiencing flooding for the first time, Office of Civil Defense (OCD) Assistant Secretary Raffy Alejandro IV…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — More than 300 villages in Pampanga remain flooded, with some areas experiencing flooding for the first time, Office of Civil Defense (OCD) Assistant Secretary Raffy Alejandro IV said on Monday.
“What we saw along the way is that the waters are still high in most parts of Pampanga,” Alejandro said in a press conference, partly in Filipino.
In total, Alejandro said 330 villages in 20 local government units (LGUs) in the province remain flooded. Pampanga has more than 500 villages.
“There are some areas which only experienced this (flooding) for the first time,” he also said, noting that the area had seen bouts of rain for almost a month.
Alejandro noted that the OCD is also concerned about water runoff not only from Mount Pinatubo but also from the Sierra Mountain Range, which will flow toward the province.
Asked if Pampanga is the most affected by the rains, Alejandro said: “So far, it’s Pampanga, which had a bit of a grave [impact] for this season.”
Alejandro said this initial assessment was based on their aerial inspection of the province on Monday morning.
So far, 21 LGUs have declared a state of calamity in Pampanga.
Since Aug. 1, the OCD said 33 people have died due to the southwest monsoon, while Alejandro said it is still verifying 14 newly reported deaths. /mcm

articles.title: Man arrested in Bukidnon over killing of 20-year-old
articles.summary: MALAYBALAY CITY, Bukidnon — A man with an alleged domestic problem with his live-in partner killed another person for no apparent reason in Zone 1, Barangay Kalasungay here on Sunday evening, police…

blocks.text: MALAYBALAY CITY, Bukidnon — A man with an alleged domestic problem with his live-in partner killed another person for no apparent reason in Zone 1, Barangay Kalasungay here on Sunday evening, police said.
Lt. Col. Joepet Paglinawan, Malaybalay police chief, said they arrested the 28-year-old suspect hours after he punched and stabbed the victim who was just buying dinner at a store at around 7:40 p.m.

With the help of Barangay Public Safety Officers, police launched a hot pursuit operation and arrested the suspect at his residence, where his mother surrendered the knife used in the crime, the official said.
The suspect, who was allegedly under the influence of alcohol, stabbed the victim at the back and left arm.
City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office personnel rushed the victim to Bethel Hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival.The suspect was positively identified by a witness.
Investigators believe the suspect’s anger may have triggered the attack due to domestic trouble with his live-in partner.
He is now in police custody facing appropriate charges. /jpv

articles.title: Stranded giant sea turtle rescued in Lebak, Sultan Kudarat
articles.summary: COTABATO CITY – A giant sea turtle, found stranded on the coast of Barangay Tran, Lebak, Sultan Kudarat on Sunday, Aug. 30, is now being secured by local environment workers. The giant turtle,…

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY – A giant sea turtle, found stranded on the coast of Barangay Tran, Lebak, Sultan Kudarat on Sunday, Aug. 30, is now being secured by local environment workers.
The giant turtle, measuring about 105 inches long and 91 inches wide, was found by Febrodin Ambag, a Sangguniang Kabataan council member.
Ambag posted on his Facebook page the discovery of the sea turtle.
The species of the sea turtle was not immediately known.
“I think this giant sea turtle is trying to find a place where to lay her eggs,” Ambag said, adding that the reptile appears to be weak and unable to return to deeper waters.
“Overnight, the pawikan is still in the same site where it was found the day earlier,” he added.
Ambag said that villagers jointly watched the reptile to ensure it is free from predators
He appealed to villagers not to disrupt the sea turtle and other marine life that strands in the coast of Barangay Tran.
The Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office (MENRO) Lebak has yet to issue a statement on the status of the rescued sea turtle. /jpv

articles.title: Civic groups unite to oppose Pax Silica initiative
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Civic groups on Monday launched a coalition to push back against Pax Silica, a US-led initiative facing broad domestic opposition over fears of community displacement and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Civic groups on Monday launched a coalition to push back against Pax Silica, a US-led initiative facing broad domestic opposition over fears of community displacement and environmental, energy, and water risks.

More than 50 organizations have signed up to join the Network Opposed to Pax Silica, a coalition of environmental activists, scientists, and Indigenous groups, according to Teddy Casiño, chairman of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan.
“Pax Silica is not just a simple investment program or industrial strategy,” Casino said. “This is the new field of economic warfare.”
“It’s a battle to see who will have control over the materials, technology and infrastructure that will be the foundation of the economy of the future,” he added.

The Philippines joined Pax Silica in April, and the US plans to build an industrial hub in the country as Washington seeks to cut reliance on Chinese tech and supply chains for AI, semiconductors and critical minerals amid a deepening tech rivalry with Beijing.
Plans for an industrial hub in Central Luzon have drawn opposition from groups warning it could drain water resources, strain the power grid and displace communities if a data center is built there.

Apung Petronila Capiz-Muñoz, chieftain of an Aeta group in Sitio Sapang Kawayan in Tarlac, said she is against any Pax Silica development over fears it would encroach upon their domain and displace them.
“We are against Pax Silica because it is a violation of our rights, especially our community, our livelihood, our church, our burial ground,” she told reporters in Filipino. /jpv

articles.title: Motorcycle theft suspects slain in shootout with cops in Sultan Kudarat
articles.summary: COTABATO CITY — Police in Esperanza, Sultan Kudarat, neutralized two suspected motorcycle thieves who traded shots with lawmen during pursuit operations on Sunday evening, Aug. 30. Maj. Jeffrey…

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY — Police in Esperanza, Sultan Kudarat, neutralized two suspected motorcycle thieves who traded shots with lawmen during pursuit operations on Sunday evening, Aug. 30.

Maj. Jeffrey Lazaro, chief of the Esperanza Municipal Police Station, said police responded to a reported motorcycle theft in Barangay Laguinding, Esperanza, at 11:30 p.m. and chased two men fleeing on separate motorcycles.
“During the chase, the suspects lost control of their motorbikes and crashed in Barangay Salabaca,” Lazaro said in his report.
Lazaro said that as pursuing lawmen approached and identified themselves as police officers, the suspects allegedly opened fire, prompting the officers to return fire in self-defense.
Both suspects sustained gunshot wounds and were transported to a local hospital, where they were declared dead on arrival.
Lazaro said police recovered two .45-caliber pistols loaded with live ammunition, fired cartridge cases and two motorcycles believed to be connected to the incident. /mcm
