articles.title: Nearly a year after Tindig Bulacan, sectoral groups march again vs corruption, reclamation
articles.summary: Protesters demand action a year after a flood corruption scandal put a spotlight on Bulacan

blocks.text: BULACAN, Philippines — Following five weeks of heavy rains, Bulakenyos took to the streets once more on Monday, August 31, demanding accountability and immediate action amid the worsening flooding here.

At the KILOS BULACAN! indignation rally in Malolos, two groups of protesters from student, agricultural, labor, and church organizations marched from the Malolos Crossing and Malolos Digital Amphitheatre before converging at the Bulacan Provincial Capitol Freedom Park. They called for an end to corruption, environmental destruction, and reclamation projects, particularly the New Manila International Airport (NMIA) project in Bulakan.

The Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office reported that 960,821 residents were directly affected by the recent floods, while damage to agriculture, fisheries, livestock, and poultry reached more than P130 million.

Bulacan has been one of the provinces dragged into the flood corruption scandal that blew up last year, with district engineers based in the province eventually getting charged in court for graft and corruption. The Commission on Audit uncovered various ghost and substandard flood control projects here.
A former district engineer had testified that at least 50 ghost flood projects were marked for the province’s first district alone.

From 2021 to 2024, Bulacan was awarded a total of P43.5 billion worth of flood control contracts. Governor Daniel Fernando’s now-viral claim that he had no knowledge of the projects came with an explanation during an August 26 press conference: the funds and projects were handled directly by the national government and agencies.
Fernando’s statement drew criticism among Bulakenyos.

“Hindi rin puwedeng ‘yung gobernador, walang alam. ‘Yung congressman, walang alam. So lahat sila dapat managot kasi kung wala silang alam, dapat magsipag-resign na sila sa puwesto nila. Kasi hindi naman nila pera ‘yan,” said David D’Angelo, environmental advocate and interim spokesperson of KILOS BULACAN! (How can it be that the governor was not aware of this? Even the congressman claims lack of knowledge of these projects. If none of them were aware, then they should just resign.)

blocks.caption: PUNISH THE CORRUPT. A protester delivers a solidarity speech as groups from different sectors converge at the Capitol Freedom Park in Malolos.

blocks.text: The group will also hold consultations with sectors across Bulacan as it continues its campaign, D’Angelo said. “Hindi naman po ito dito matatapos kasi lahat ng organisasyon hihilingan natin na magsama-sama,” he added. The group plans to discuss reclamation, including the NMIA project, as well as nature-based solutions and other approaches to flood mitigation.

He said they have requested documents from the office of Vice Governor Alex Castro, including Bulacan’s comprehensive flood mitigation plan. The group plans to study the documents as it considers filing cases against those it holds accountable for environmental destruction. “‘Yung mga dokumento rin na ‘yon ay pag-aaralan natin para magsampa po tayo ng kaso sa mga dapat sampahan, lalong lalo na sa kalaban ng kalikasan at sa salot ng kalikasan na si P.I. Ramon Ang,” D’Angelo said.

Monday’s rally came nearly a year after the Tindig Bulacan movement began, which sparked a series of mobilizations across towns in the province calling for accountability over flood control projects and the use of public funds. – Rappler.com

Mark David Silencio is an Information Technology student at Bulacan State University in Plaridel, Bulacan. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, he is also the managing editor for Administration of Pacesetter.

articles.title: Swiss police arrest man over deadly rave shooting

blocks.text: Swiss police on Monday arrested a suspect in the weekend shooting at a rave in the Swiss town of Aarau, where an Italian woman was killed and several others were injured.
Local police had said the incident could have been an act of terrorism, but that other motives were also being considered.
Authorities said that the suspect was a Swiss national, and that they believe he acted alone.
What do we know about the arrest made?

"Investigations ‌into the exact ‌circumstances ​of the incident, as well as its ​background and possible motive, are currently ⁠underway. ​At this ​stage, it is ​assumed that ‌a single perpetrator was involved," ​police ⁠in the canton ⁠of ​Aargau said in a statement.
Police added that the suspect was arrested on "strong suspicion" of being behind the attack.
At least five others were injured in the attack, some seriously.
Investigators found two kinds of cartridges at the scene, indicating the presence of a pistol and a large weapon, possibly an assault rifle.
The suspect was apprehended after a major manhunt, which also involved police from neighboring Germany.

articles.title: The jury's options in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial
articles.summary: Jurors have five options before them as they decide the fate of the former nurse charged with killing her three children.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
ByAna Faguy
Reporting fromMassachusetts
Lindsay Clancy's murder trial has gripped the American public for the last five weeks.
The 36-year-old former nurse killed her three small children in the basement of their family home in Massachusetts.
Charged with three counts of first-degree murder, she does not dispute killing her two sons and daughter.
But her lawyer argues she was suffering from postpartum psychosis during the incident in January 2023.
On Monday morning, a jury of nine women and three men will continue to deliberate whether she is criminally responsible for her actions.
The prosecution argues Clancy made a calculated, intentional decision to kill them and knew right from wrong in that moment.
The defence, meanwhile, has said her mental illness prevented her from knowing what she was doing.
The jury is weighing several options:

items: not guilty
not guilty by reason of insanity
first-degree murder
second-degree murder
manslaughter

blocks.text: Not guilty / not guilty by reason of insanity
This hinges on the postpartum psychosis defence - her legal team argued that Clancy hallucinated a voice after giving birth to her youngest child that told her to kill the children.
Expert witnesses told the court how severe this illness can be, and family members testified about Clancy's state of mind.
Under Massachusetts law, there is no burden on Clancy to prove her mental illness and that she lacked criminal responsibility.
Rather, it is on the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that she was criminally responsible when she killed her children, criminal defence lawyer Elyse Hershon told the BBC.

They can do this by either proving beyond reasonable doubt that she didn't suffer from a mental illness at the time or that, while she had a mental illness, she still controlled her actions and knew they were wrong.

A not guilty verdict would mean Clancy went free but that is considered highly unlikely. Much more likely is a not guilty by reason of insanity, which would result in Clancy being detained at a hospital.

"The case really comes down to where she is going to serve the rest of her life; the defence thinks it should be a psychiatric facility, the prosecution thinks it should be in a state prison," Hershon said.
Watch: What is postpartum psychosis and why is it central in the Lindsay Clancy trial?
First-degree murder
This is the most serious potential outcome for Clancy - being found guilty of first-degree murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.
In the state of Massachusetts, this conviction carries a mandatory sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole.

As Heather Cucolo, a New York Law School professor and expert in mental health law, put it to the BBC, Clancy would effectively need to be seen as "a monster in the jury's eyes" if they pick this outcome.
Jurors would have to find there was extreme atrocity or extreme cruelty or both to convict Clancy of this, and it would mean the prosecution had proven there were no mitigating factors.
In this case, mental disease or defect - as the law describes it - could be a mitigating factor.
Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague said during closing arguments there was no dispute Clancy was suffering from mental illness but it was not so severe that she didn't know right from wrong.
Expert witnesses for the prosecution cast doubt on whether Clancy actually heard the voice that she said ordered her to kill her children.
Second-degree murder
This is a catch-all for any murder that is not first-degree, under Massachusetts law.
It applies to unlawful killings committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without prior planning.

"For this verdict, the jurors may not be convinced that the actions leading up to the murder rose to the level of pre-planned [or] premeditated but that instead, Clancy consciously saw an opportunity to commit the killings at the specified time," Cucolo said.
In the case of second-degree murder, Clancy would also face a life sentence - but with the possibility of parole.
Manslaughter
The jury received yet another option when the judge allowed them to find Clancy guilty of manslaughter - previously a point of contention between the defence and the prosecution.
Manslaughter, which is defined as causing death by an unintentional, mistaken or neglectful act, carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison per count.
Intent is an important distinction between a verdict like manslaughter and the two murder verdicts, experts said.
"This option allows the jury to accept that the murders were not planned or calculated but that instead Clancy made a split-second decision to act," Cucolo said.
The prosecution is not obligated to demonstrate that she intended to cause the children's deaths for there to be a manslaughter conviction, she added.

articles.title: With multilateralism in decline, what's next for the world?
articles.summary: The global political architecture is shifting, partly as a result of the actions of US President Donald Trump. As nations search for a new world order, some may gain influence and power, while others…

image.caption: Who will dominate the future world order? Indonesian painter Galam Zulkifl has blended the portraits of three powerful men into oneImage: Juni Kriswanto/AFP

blocks.text: Donald Trump's visit to UN headquarters in New York in September 2025 was rife with symbolism.

As the US president stepped onto the escalator in the lobby ahead of his address, it stopped working. Then, the teleprompter failed during his speech, prompting the former TV star to tell the assembled heads of state and government, half-jokingly: "These are the two things I got from the United Nations: A bad escalator and a bad teleprompter."

The United Nations is the central institution of the post-World War II order, shaped in part by the United States and based on multilateralism and the balancing of interests. When the UN was founded in 1945, its goal was to prevent wars. Its mandate later expanded to include countless other areas, such as global health, development and climate protection.
Today, more than 80 years later, the UN's institutions, above all the Security Council, are widely considered to be in need of an overhaul, much like the UN headquarters itself.

blocks.caption: Has Trump exposed the UN's shortcomings to the world — or is he largely responsible for their destruction?Image: Kylie Cooper/REUTERS

blocks.text: The broken escalator incident was apparently triggered accidentally by Trump's own camera operator, the UN has said, rejecting responsibility for the incident. And beyond this symbolic moment, views are split over whether Trump, with his sometimes isolationist America First ideology, is above all a symptom of the crumbling multilateral world order or a destructive wrecking ball.
Far beyond escalators and teleprompters, politicians and analysts around the world are debating the question: Is multilateralism coming to an end — and if so, what comes next?
A new world order in five years or continued disorder?

Finnish President Alexander Stubb, one of the few heads of state to hold a doctorate in international relations, argues that the world is currently experiencing a power vacuum from which a new world order will likely emerge over the next five years.
Can democracy survive the rise of extreme wealth?

Other experts expect a longer period of adjustment. "It is time to acknowledge that the old order really has disappeared and to plot a new approach to geopolitics. This moment does not constitute a short interregnum between a US-led order and a Chinese-led one," Mark Leonard, director of the European Council on Foreign Relations think tank, recently wrote in an essay in Foreign Affairs magazine.

"For some time, the world will be without any order at all, swept by fragmentation, contagion, and strangulation or the temptation to weaponize a wide variety of geographic, economic, and technological chokepoints."
An era of reform gridlock

"That framework of multilateralism, which is connected with the world after World War II [...] and a golden period of then the United Nations, I would say that it's all over," said Teresa Nogueira Pinto, a globalization expert specializing in Africa at Lusofona University in Lisbon.

"It's not working," she added. "We can see that in the peacekeeping and peacebuilding missions, most of them, they have been a failure, and then we see that the UN is desperately in need of a reform."

Speaking with DW, Pinto cited the UN Security Council as an example, stressing that it doesn't represent the world in 2026. "But who would join? India, Pakistan, Nigeria, Ethiopia — I mean, it's very, very hard to even imagine a reform."

Johannes Thimm, head of the Americas Research Group at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP) in Berlin, takes a different view. "I do not agree that this era is already completely over," he said. "International law is very diverse and also includes a great deal that you don't even notice in the daily relations between states, diplomatic conventions, treaties and so on. And there is still quite a lot there that you don't really notice because it isn't particularly spectacular."

But he added that there is no doubt that international law has increasingly been violated in recent times, for example, through wars of aggression in Ukraine and Iran. Meanwhile, violations of international humanitarian law, as in Gaza, also pose a challenge to the multilateral order.

blocks.caption: The International Court of Justice has repeatedly ordered Israel not to block the delivery of humanitarian aid during its war against Hamas in Gaza. But hundreds of Palestinians in the coastal enclave are estimated to have died of starvationImage: Stringer/REUTERS

blocks.text: Thimm pointed out US withdrawals from dozens of international organizations and treaties as another factor undermining the stability of multilateralism. These include the World Health Organization, the Paris climate agreement, the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Just recently, the US government further stepped up its pressure on the International Criminal Court, which it has criticized.

"If the still most powerful state acts this way," Thimm said, "then that poses a threat to the system as a whole. So, I would say, a greater threat than when Russia, for example, wages a war of aggression."
Old alliances fray, new ones emerge

Trump frequently invokes the Monroe Doctrine of 1823, which defined the Western Hemisphere as an exclusive sphere of influence for Washington. Applied to the present day, this could mean that the rest of the world is no longer dominated by the United States but by other major and middle powers: that's to say a multipolar world order following the departure of the US as the dominant power.

For many countries, this upheaval carries the risk of losing influence. For others, however, it can also be an incentive to reposition themselves and secure their place through alliances of their own in a multipolar world no longer dominated by the West. It is no coincidence, for example, that the BRICS alliance of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa has also gained in importance and taken on new members. It is increasingly seeking to establish a confident counterweight to the Western-dominated international financial architecture.
What is BRICS and what does it want?

"Many African countries are realizing that the previous models were not so advantageous for them, and especially for growth and sustainable growth," said Pinto. "They are taking advantage of this, and I would say also that this is very connected to the comeback of geopolitics. For a period we thought that geopolitics was history, but it's not."

The world is also reorganizing itself in terms of security policy. Within NATO, there are fears of a further US withdrawal or even a military attack from within should Trump continue to pursue hi sclaims to Greenland, which is administered by Denmark. In the Indo-Pacific region, and especially in the Middle East, US allies are questioning the reliability of American security guarantees and looking for new alliances.

In early August, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and nuclear-armed Pakistan launched the Mecca Defense Pact, with NATO-style mutual defense guarantees. The agreement, as well as the European coalition of the willing to support Ukraine, are seen as examples of the smaller, more agile formats that are sometimes referred to as "minilateralism."

In many cases, military and diplomatic efforts are being considered together. "A world without rules only helps the strong," said SWP expert Thimm. "Everyone else, whether they are moderately strong or weak, gets crushed. And that is why Europe, which I would count among the moderately strong, naturally has a strong interest in preserving some kind of order."

blocks.caption: The New Development Bank in Shanghai is intended, in line with the BRICS countries' aims, to provide a counterweight to Western institutions such as the World Bank and the International Monetary FundImage: Fang Zhe/Xinhua/IMAGO

blocks.text: Alongside military considerations, many states are also looking for new, broader economic and political partnerships. Pinto expects regional alliances to gain importance and potentially produce better results than mechanisms at the global level. The World Trade Organization, for example, achieved a great deal in the 20th century, she said, but has not functioned for some time now.
"Now, it may be more useful to think about regional approaches such as the African Continental Free Trade Area."

The harmonization of African markets is seen as a promising approach to solving many problems. But further implementation of the free trade area, ratified by almost all African states since 2018, has been rather slow.
Whose interests will a future world order serve?

Pinto said three factors could influence the future distribution of power in a multipolar world: sovereignty, access to resources and, last but not least, demographics. Young, growing societies in Africa and Asia could make themselves indispensable. "India could become a superpower by the end of the century," she said.

Amid the decline of US influence, the growing power of other actors such as China, and other factors including minilateralism and regional alliances — it's still too early to say for sure what kind of world order will emerge from the status quo.
Is the Board of Peace Trump's private UN?

At least in the short term, however, Thimm fears that "the world will become more violent. There will be more wars. The wars will become more brutal. It will be more difficult to organize cooperation. So I don't know what will happen when the next pandemic breaks out. I don't know what will happen when the next global financial crisis breaks out."
Against this backdrop, he pointed out that we still face the climate crisis, a key challenge that can only be solved through collective action.

articles.title: Heavy rains to drench parts of Luzon on Sept. 1
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Heavy rainfall is expected in parts of Luzon from Monday afternoon to Tuesday afternoon due to the southwest monsoon, which is being enhanced by Tropical Depression Pilandok,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Heavy rainfall is expected in parts of Luzon from Monday afternoon to Tuesday afternoon due to the southwest monsoon, which is being enhanced by Tropical Depression Pilandok, the state weather bureau reported.

Based on its 5 p.m. weather advisory, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said heavy to intense rains, or around 100 to 200 millimeters (mm) of rainfall, are expected in Ilocos Sur, La Union, Abra and Benguet.
“Numerous flooding events are likely, especially in areas that are urbanized, low-lying or near rivers. Landslides are likely in moderate to highly susceptible areas,” Pagasa said.
Meanwhile, moderate to heavy rains, or around 50 to 100 mm of rainfall, are expected over the following areas:

items: Ilocos Norte
Pangasinan
Batanes
Apayao
Kalinga
Ifugao
Mountain Province
Nueva Vizcaya
Tarlac
Nueva Ecija
Pampanga
Zambales
Bataan

blocks.text: Under this condition, localized flooding is possible mainly in urbanized, low-lying or riverside areas, and landslides may occur in highly susceptible areas.
“Forecast rainfall may be higher in mountainous and elevated areas,” the weather bureau said, noting that impacts in some areas may be worsened by significant antecedent rainfall.
Pagasa advised the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices in the mentioned areas to take all necessary measures “to protect life and property.”

Pagasa also reported that Tropical Depression Pilandok was forecast to intensify into a tropical storm by Tuesday, Sept. 1, and remain a tropical storm as it moved generally north-northwestward over the Philippine Sea, after staying almost stationary for the next 36 hours.
The tropical depression is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility by Wednesday afternoon or evening. /mcm

articles.title: Weeks of rain leave 15 dead, 3 injured in Bulacan
articles.summary: CITY OF MALOLOS — Weeks of heavy rain left 15 people dead and three injured in flood-stricken Bulacan, which had been placed under a state of calamity on Aug. 20. The Bulacan Provincial Disaster Risk…

blocks.text: CITY OF MALOLOS — Weeks of heavy rain left 15 people dead and three injured in flood-stricken Bulacan, which had been placed under a state of calamity on Aug. 20.

The Bulacan Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) said 86-year-old Gener Arcega Dimacali and 20-year-old Laverine Velasco drowned at the height of heavy rains and flash floods on Aug. 29 in Marilao town.

The heavy downpour that day also caused the death of Jennie Ursabia, 29, in Barangay Tambubong in Bocaue town. The mezzanine of a warehouse storing commodities sold online collapsed, hitting her as floodwaters surged at 3:20 p.m. She was declared dead on arrival at Rogaciano Memorial Medical Hospital in Sta. Maria town.
Christel Rebua, 18, from Barangay Taal, was also struck by warehouse debris and died at a hospital in Sta. Maria, where she was rushed, Manuel Lukban Jr., head of the Bulacan PDRRMO, said on Monday.
Three others—Dazel Anne Arnaiz, 18, and Jonel Barsilon, 28, both from Barangay Tambubong, and Raymond Parman, 25, from Barangay Batia—were injured in the warehouse accident.

In Barangay Anyatam in the municipality of San Ildefonso, 15-year-old Angelo Alcaraz and April Alcaraz, 13, were reported missing on Aug. 23, and their drowned remains were found separately on Aug. 25.
In Barangay San Juan in Hagonoy town on Aug. 23, Olympia Nepomuceno, 74, and Rolando de Leon, 64, were declared dead on arrival after they were both electrocuted.

In Barangay Taliptip in Bulakan town, an unidentified body was found in the river on Aug. 22. The Bulakan Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office said no one had yet claimed the body and that a funeral firm had volunteered to bury it on Aug. 27.

In Sitio Bagumbario, Barangay San Miguel, in Calumpit town, Rhian Joy T. Martinez, 17, died of electrocution on Aug. 19. In the Calumpit barangay of Sto. Niño, Cecilio Lopez, 66, died of drowning on Aug. 22. In Barangay Iba O’ Este, Ran Romy Ortillano, 8, drowned on Aug. 23. His body was found floating in Barangay Masukol in Paombong town on Aug. 25.
In Sta. Maria town, Axel Kurt Mijares, 15, died of drowning on Aug. 20. His body was found at midnight on Aug. 22 along Catmon River in Barangay Kaylawig.

In the City of San Jose del Monte, John Norbert Nipay, 17, drowned on Aug. 10. His body was found and retrieved from Macaiban River in Sta. Maria town on Aug. 12. In a separate drowning incident in the city, the body of Ronjean Justine Alseco, 13, who drowned on Aug. 10, was found in Nagbalon River in Marilao town on Aug. 13.
All 23 towns and cities of Bulacan were affected by floods of up to 6 feet, while landslides plagued the mountainous town of Doña Remedios Trinidad, Lukban said. /mcm

articles.title: WALANG PASOK: Palace suspends in-person classes, work in 15 Luzon areas
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang has suspended in-person work in government offices and face-to-face classes at all levels on Sept. 1 (Tuesday) in 15 provinces in Luzon in anticipation of continued…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang has suspended in-person work in government offices and face-to-face classes at all levels on Sept. 1 (Tuesday) in 15 provinces in Luzon in anticipation of continued heavy rainfall associated with the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat).

Under Memorandum Circular No. 133 issued on Monday by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, by authority of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., directed to implement appropriate alternative work arrangements in the following provinces:

items: Abra
Apayao
Bataan
Batanes
Benguet
Ilocos Norte
Ilocos Sur
Kalinga
La Union
Mountain Province
Nueva Vizcaya
Pampanga
Pangasinan
Tarlac
Zambales

blocks.text: Unless otherwise directed by their respective local chief executives, alternative learning modes for classes and learning continuity measures at all levels in public and private schools shall be implemented in these provinces.

The suspension of in-person work and classes is upon the recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) and due to forecast heavy rainfall brought by habagat, which may result in urban flooding and traffic disruptions in these areas.
Under MC 133, agencies responsible for basic, vital and health services, preparedness and response duties must continue to remain operational.
All other government agencies in the aforementioned regions may implement alternate work arrangements, as may be necessary, to ensure continuity of essential government functions.
Local chief executives of areas in other regions not mentioned in the MC may implement localized cancellation or suspension of classes and work in government offices.
The suspension of work in private companies and offices is left to the discretion of their respective heads. /jpv

articles.title: NLEX operator sorry for heavy traffic, vows for concrete flood barriers
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation, operator of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX), has apologized to motorists who have been stranded in some sections of the expressway,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation, operator of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX), has apologized to motorists who have been stranded in some sections of the expressway, which were rendered impassable because of severe flooding.

The management, it said, understands the public’s frustration, saying it is “deeply sorry” for what motorists, especially those travelling with children, elderly, or individuals needing medical attention, had to go through.

It said NLEX is implementing additional engineering measures in the Tulaoc area, where concrete barriers will be deployed along 300 meters northbound and 300 meters southbound to serve as a temporary flood wall.
Siphoning trucks will also be deployed to remove floodwater, while pumping operations will be intensified once the inflow is contained or significantly reduced.
As it explained in a statement on Monday, Aug. 31, days of continuous heavy rain have flooded the entire town of San Simon, as confirmed by Pampanga Governor Lilia Pineda in a radio interview.
“With surrounding areas underwater, pumping alone cannot keep the expressway clear while floodwater continues to enter the road,” it said.

This was why from the first hours, NLEX issued round-the-clock advisories through its social media channels and 31 Variable Message Signs across NLEX, Subic–Clark–Tarlac Expressway, and the NLEX Connector, alerting motorists to conditions ahead and available alternative routes.

“MacArthur Highway, the principal alternative route, was also heavily flooded, with portions rendered impassable, leaving motorists with very limited options,” it said, pointing out that a counterflow will be established to facilitate the movement of emergency and response equipment to the affected Tulaoc area.

“As a longer-term flood-mitigation measure, NLEX plans to further raise the pavement along the Northbound and Southbound sections in Tulaoc,” said the corporation, explaining that further road-raising works can be implemented once the Tulaoc Bridge has been raised to provide the necessary vertical clearance, subject to the required engineering assessment and works.

It said “our operations, patrol and emergency crews remain deployed 24/7 to assist stranded motorists.” “We will continue to keep the public informed as conditions change and thank NLEX users for their patience and understanding.” /jpv

articles.title: Passengers stranded as strike disrupts flights at Kenya's main airport
articles.summary: Kenya Airways says the strike has caused delays of more than six hours, with some flights cancelled.

blocks.text: Hundreds of passengers were stranded at Kenya's main airport in the capital, Nairobi, as flight disruptions continued for the second day amid a workers' strike.
Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) is a key regional transport hub.
On Sunday, the airports authority and the national carrier, Kenya Airways, warned departing flights may be delayed.
A new round of talks between unions and airport managers was due to take place on Monday, although discussions broke up a day earlier without agreement.
Aviation sector workers are on a nationwide go-slow strike to demand better working conditions and the implementation of a previously agreed deal.
Those hoping to get on a flight have been stuck at JKIA, with some spending the night in and around the check-in areas waiting for news.

Kenya Airways said in its latest update that due to "the industrial action by air traffic control workers", it is experiencing delays of more than six hours, and the flight backlog has forced it to cancel some departures.
It has apologised for the disruption and said passengers who would like to change or reschedule their flights could do so without a penalty.
Flight tracking website Flightradar24 showed a host of delayed, cancelled or diverted flights.

RwandAir said on Monday that it had cancelled two flights due to the ongoing "operational constraints affecting air traffic control services" at the airport. This followed earlier cancellations on Sunday.
Mendel Goldman, who was travelling to a wedding in Florida, told the Reuters news agency that his flight had been cancelled, after several delays.
He said he had been waiting for 12 hours.
"The earliest flight they can get us is only tomorrow night, so we've got to wait.
"We're going to try and make most of it, but in the meantime, I've been here for 12 hours now, waiting in the airport," he said.
William Obino, a 22-year-old traveller told the AFP news agency: "Nothing is happening, updates are reaching us late. It's ruining our itinerary."
The strike comes after a two-day dispute in February over collective bargaining and the use of volunteers at the airport.
Union officials said they took industrial action because concerns remained unresolved.

The main airport in Nairobi is one of the busiest hubs in the region and serves as a key gateway between the continent and the rest of the world. Last year, it handled about nine million passengers, according to the Kenyan authorities.
It has however seen multiple strikes in recent years as workers push for better conditions.

articles.title: EJ Obiena back to golden ways with victory in Germany
articles.summary: EJ Obiena claims his ninth gold medal of the year by ruling the ISTAF Berlin in Germany

blocks.text: EFFORT. The Philippines' Ernest John Obiena in action during the men's pole vault final of the 2026 Weltklasse Zurich in Switzerland.
Denis Balibouse/REUTERS
EJ Obiena claims his ninth gold medal of the year by ruling the ISTAF Berlin in Germany
MANILA, Philippines – Another vault, another gold.
EJ Obiena claimed his ninth gold medal of the year after ruling the ISTAF Berlin at the Olympiastadion in Germany on Sunday, August 30 (Monday, August 31, Manila time).
The Filipino pole vault star cleared 5.82 meters in a single attempt as he rediscovered his winning ways after failing to crack the podium in his last three meets.
Belgium’s Ylio Philtjens placed second with 5.72m, beating France’s Robin Emig for the silver via countback.

With the gold already in the bag, Obiena tried to eclipse his season best of 5.91m he achieved when he topped the Golden Sand in Poland earlier this August by going for 5.97m but to no avail as he exhausted all of his three tries.
Obiena’s recent form has allowed him to climb to No. 12 in the world rankings — two spots above his No. 14 standing in June.

Enjoying a career resurgence, the former world No. 2 is tagged as one of the Philippines’ best bets in the Asian Games, where he is expected to defend the title he won in the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China.
The upcoming Asian Games will be held in Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4. – Rappler.com

articles.title: French high schools rush to put Macron’s phone ban into force
articles.summary:
Unions say ban will take time to enact, while president also wants under-15s social media ban as key legacy

French high schools are rushing to put in place a hurriedly signed off ban on…

blocks.text: French high schools are rushing to put in place a ban on mobile phones this week as Emmanuel Macron pushes for children to spend less time in front of screens.
Education unions warned that banning mobile phone use in lycées – where children are aged 15 to 18 – would be hard to implement quickly.
Macron approved the high school phone ban this month after another measure he had hoped would be a key legacy, his proposed social media ban for under-15s, was knocked back as unconstitutional.
The text of the social media ban is being rewritten in the hope it can be pushed it through before Macron leaves office in May.
France has already banned children from using mobile phones in primary schools and in middle schools, or collèges, which are attended between the ages of 11 and 15.
The government’s focus is now on banning mobile phone use among older teenagers at school from September, as it argues that too much screen time is harming children’s development.
In order to enforce the hurriedly signed-off ban, high schools must amend their rules – a lengthy process – and many schools have said they will struggle to implement the measure swiftly.

“It’s impossible to put this in place from scratch from 1 September,” said Jérôme Fournier, the national secretary of the SE-Unsa trade union. “Schools will need to change their internal regulations and that requires a full consultation process and a vote, and for high school students to be consulted. So we need time for everyone to meet and work on this.”

Fournier said a key challenge was that high school students were often obliged to rely on school smartphone apps to find out even the most basic information for the school day, such as timetables, room changes and homework. “Some even have to use apps on their phones as a badge to enter the canteen to eat lunch or to borrow books from the school library,” he said.
Fournier said high schools often hosted students for higher education courses or apprenticeships, some of whom were aged 20 and needed to use their phones for their work.

He said the key issue for each high school was to decide where exactly to enforce the ban, whether across the whole school, including corridors, or with exceptions such as in the playground. He said teenagers could be tempted to leave the school grounds in order to use their phones on the street outside, which could have implications for security and road safety.

Fournier said students should be consulted on the process rather than being treated as children. “These older teenagers are pre-adults – some in their final school year are going to vote in the upcoming presidential election,” he said.
Macron’s office has said he has no plans to give up on his push to bar under-15s from social media platforms such as TikTok and Snapchat, and the government is working redraft the law.

France’s constitutional council recently struck down the first version of the law after concerns that its definition of social media was not specific enough. This meant a host of sites not generally considered social media but that allowed commentary or communication could be banned, amounting to a “disproportionate restriction” on freedom of expression.
The constitutional council also raised concerns about the privacy implications of putting in place an age-verification system for all users.

Valère Ndior, a law professor at the University of Western Brittany, said it was no surprise to legal experts that the law in its current form had been knocked back, and it would be a challenge to rewrite it. “For the moment, as a legal practitioner, I can’t see how it’s possible to strike a balance between European law and French constitutional law,” he said.

articles.title: Palace orders alternative government work set-up, learning modes in 15 provinces on Sept 1
articles.summary: Alternative work arrangements in government offices and alternative learning modes in public and private schools will be implemented on Tuesday, Sept. 1 due to continued heavy rains. Through…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. (PCO)
Alternative work arrangements in government offices and alternative learning modes in public and private schools will be implemented on Tuesday, Sept. 1 due to continued heavy rains.
Through Memorandum Circular No. 133, President Marcos ordered the alternative government work and class set-up in 15 provinces in Luzon.

The directive covers the provinces of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, Kalinga, Mountain Province, Apayao, Batanes, Nueva Vizcaya, Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, and Bataan.
It was issued upon the recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC).
Agencies involved in the delivery of basic and health services, disaster preparedness and response, and other vital services shall continue their operations and provide the necessary services.

Contract of Service (COS) and Job Order (JO) workers placed under alternative work arrangements will continue to receive their corresponding wages or salaries, subject to applicable rules and regulations, the memorandum stated.

The circular also allows local chief executives to implement localized cancellation or suspension of classes and/or work in government offices in other areas, in accordance with relevant laws, rules and regulations.
The suspension of work or adoption of alternative work arrangements in the private sector, however, will be left to the discretion of management.

articles.title: Pilandok maintains strength; monsoon rain in 3 areas due to ‘habagat’
articles.summary: Tropical Depression Pilandok continues to meander over the Philippine Sea east of extreme Northern Luzon, says PAGASA

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength on Monday afternoon, August 31, while monsoon rain has eased in some areas, with Ilocos Region, Abra, and Benguet bearing the brunt due to the enhanced southwest monsoon.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said in its 5 pm bulletin Monday that Pilandok was located 1,145 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon, moving north northwestward at 10 kilometers per hour with winds of 55 km/h and gustiness of up to 70 km/h.
Two tropical depressions outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) are enhancing the southwest monsoon.

Tropical Depression Saudel (formerly referred to as Obet), located 1,075 km west of extreme Northern Luzon, has winds of 45 km/h and gustiness of up to 75 km/h. PAGASA Weather Specialist Charmagne Varilla said Saudel could still reenter PAR and redevelop into a tropical storm, but it has a low likelihood of making landfall.

The other tropical depression, located 570 km west northwest of Itbayat, Batanes, has winds of 45 km/h and gustiness of up to 60 km/h. According to Varilla, this tropical depression could eventually be absorbed into Saudel’s circulation, or it could have a “looping track” along the northwestern part, enter PAR, then make landfall in Taiwan.

In either scenario, this tropical depression won’t have a direct effect on the country, but it will continue to enhance the southwest monsoon and bring rain to parts of Luzon and the western section of Visayas.

Another low pressure area being monitored outside PAR has a “medium” chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours. It could enter PAR but is less likely to make landfall and will not affect the country.

Meanwhile, Tropical Depression Pilandok may become almost stationary over the Philippine Sea east of extreme Northern Luzon for the next 36 hours before moving generally north northwestward. It is still less likely to make landfall and will remain far from the Philippine landmass.
Pilandok may intensify into a tropical storm by Tuesday, September 1, before it leaves PAR and moves toward southern Japan.

The enhanced southwest monsoon is bringing monsoon rain to Ilocos Region, Abra, and Benguet, and occasional rain to the rest of Cordillera Administrative Region, Batanes, Nueva Vizcaya, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, and Nueva Ecija.

It is also causing scattered rain and thunderstorms in Metro Manila, Calabarzon, the rest of Cagayan Valley, the rest of Central Luzon, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, Aklan, and Antique, and isolated rain showers or thunderstorms in the rest of Luzon, Negros Island Region, and the rest of Western Visayas.

articles.title: Abante issues appeal to VP Duterte supporters in Mindanao as impeachment trial moves forward
articles.summary: Manila 6th district Rep. Bienvenido "Benny" Abante Jr. is asking supporters of impeachment trial respondent Vice President Sara Duterte from Mindanao and elsewhere to judge the actions of the…

blocks.text: Manila 6th district Rep. Bienvenido "Benny" Abante Jr. is asking supporters of impeachment trial respondent Vice President Sara Duterte from Mindanao and elsewhere to judge the actions of the prosecution team based on their constitutional duty.
The impeachment respondent had this to say even as the high-stakes trial against the popular official from Mindanao enters its third month.
The House, which prepared the articles of impeachment against Duterte, earlier formed a team of 26 public and private prosecutors tasked to convict the Vice President.

"Ang pakiusap lamang po namin sa taong bayan ay makinig at manood po sila at sila na ang manghusga on their own kung talagang ginagawa ng prosecution team ang kanilang tungkulin ayon sa Konstitusyon, ayon sa batas,” Abante, an impeachment complaint endorser, said.

(Our only appeal to the public is for them to listen and watch the proceedings and judge for themselves whether the prosecution team is truly performing its duty in accordance with the Constitution and the law.)
He stressed that the House prosecution’s responsibility is to present its case rather than dictate the conclusion that Filipinos or the senator-judges should eventually reach.
“We cannot make the judgment now. Ang gagawin lamang ng prosecution team ay ilahad sa taong bayan lahat ng mga ebidensya,” Abante said.
(We cannot make the judgment now. The only thing the prosecution team will do is present all the evidence to the public.)

He said the defense will likewise get the opportunity to challenge prosecution witnesses, contest documentary evidence and present its own case before the senator-judges determine whether any of the impeachment articles has been proven.
Asked what guarantee he could give Mindanaoans, the veteran lawmaker said:
“Makakaasa po ang taong bayan, kayo man ay sumusuporta sa Vice President o hindi, na maririnig po ninyo rito ay mga ebidensya na inilahad ng prosecution team."
(The public can be assured that whether or not you support the Vice President, what you will hear here are the pieces of evidence presented by the prosecution team.)
Duterte retains deep political support in Mindanao, particularly in Davao City, where she is a former mayor and vice mayor.
For Abante, keeping the proceedings open to public scrutiny gives Filipinos--including those from Duterte’s bailiwick--the opportunity to evaluate the case beyond competing political narratives.
“I hope that ang mga taong bayan po ang makikita nila ang mga ebidensya tungkol dito, and they will actually appreciate all the evidence presented. ‘Yun po ang nais natin,” he said.
(I hope that the public will see the evidence presented in this case and that they will actually appreciate all the evidence presented. That is what we want.)

articles.title: Cayetano to Lacson: Stop the theatrics, let evidence speak
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Monday told Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson to “stop the theatrics” and let evidence speak in the proper forum as the latter continues…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Monday told Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson to “stop the theatrics” and let evidence speak in the proper forum as the latter continues his probe into infrastructure and reclamation projects in Taguig City.

“Senator Lacson has perfected the art of political persecution, which is a combination of demolition jobs, witch hunts, and trial by publicity, disguised as legal prosecution,” Cayetano said in a Facebook post.
“He intimidates and threatens witnesses and agencies, then he himself makes announcements for them,” he added.

Cayetano’s statement came as Lacson on Monday flagged at least P3.713 billion in public funds that he said may have been “wasted” on flood control and multipurpose projects in reclamation areas along Laguna Lake in Taguig City, the political bailiwick of the Cayetanos.

In his post, which emphasized the word “WASTED,” Cayetano said investigations into corruption and flood control should be pursued from investigation to accountability, but warned that the process must be a search for “TRUTH,” rather than a vehicle for “political vendetta.”
“This is where Senator Ping Lacson and the majority of Filipinos fundamentally differ,” Cayetano said.
Obscuring the truth
According to Cayetano, accusations should be met with specific questions on what happened, who was responsible, and what evidence supports the claims.
Cayetano argued that repeatedly raising new allegations and insinuations only confuses the issues and makes the truth harder for Filipinos to see.

“To be fair – if there is evidence against DPWH, Taguig, or against me, then present it. Allow the investigative offices (like The Office of The Ombudsman) to do their job. Stop the theatrics and let the evidence do the talking set In The proper judicial Venue where fairness Is assured,” he said.
“Let the investigating agencies investigate! Let the witnesses testify freely and truthfully. Let the accused answer,” Cayetano added.
He also called for allegations of corruption anywhere in government to be investigated “with exactly the same determination,” regardless of the personalities or political affiliations involved.
Right back at ‘ya

Cayetano then used Lacson’s own “WASTED” framing to argue that public resources and government efforts could themselves be wasted when investigations become political battles rather than disciplined searches for truth.

He said government time spent on political warfare, public funds spent on projects that do not serve Filipinos, investigations turned into “political theater,” and opportunities for meaningful reforms sacrificed for partisan interests all amount to being “WASTED.”

“And ultimately, we risk wasting something far more precious than government money or government time: The sacrifice of those who came before us,” Cayetano wrote further on the same day the country celebrates National Heroes Day.
“Our heroes did not sacrifice so succeeding generations could perfect the politics of accusation. They sacrificed because they believed we could build a nation,” he added.
Cayetano said National Heroes Day should serve as a reminder of the responsibility of Filipinos to build on the freedom, country and future left by those who came before them.
“Let us stop wasting time, opportunities, and the Filipino people’s trust,” he said.
Lacson previously said that his office has turned over to the Ombudsman evidence that he and his office found from their investigation in Taguig.
His probe into the city was fueled by his feud with Cayetano who first alleged that Lacson’s net worth doubled.
Lacson has since fired back, saying he had no budget insertions since he was elected senator, and in turn accused Cayetano of making P6.79-billion insertions in the 2025 General Appropriations Act.
Cayetano has also denied all these allegations and said Taguig had no “ghost” projects.
The Inquirer sought comment from Lacson over Cayetano’s latest post but has yet to receive a response as of posting time. /jpv

articles.title: Morocco not to blame for Ceuta border breach, says Spanish PM
articles.summary:
Pedro Sánchez says two countries are cooperating after mass incursion by 70,000 people into north African enclave

Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has insisted there was no evidence…

blocks.text: Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has insisted there was no evidence to suggest the Moroccan government was behind last month’s massive border crossing into Ceuta.

As many as 141 people are thought to have died trying to enter the Spanish enclave at the end of July. The influx of about 70,000 men, women and children unleashed a political crisis, a humanitarian emergency and reignited tensions over immigration within the EU.
Although the overwhelming majority of the migrants crossed back into Morocco weeks ago, hundreds of people, including minors, are still on the streets of Ceuta, leading to tensions with residents.

Despite speculation that Rabat may have engineered the mass crossing as a means of showing its displeasure at Spain’s rapprochement with Algeria, Sánchez said there was nothing to indicate the involvement of the Moroccan authorities.
“There’s no information from any intelligence agency that raises doubts over the involvement of Moroccan authorities,” he told Cadena Ser radio on Monday.

“Cooperation with Morocco is frankly positive. I’d like to stress that we need to be aware that this crisis can be resolved only through cooperation – and not through a lack of trust in Morocco, which would only further aggravate the already complex situation we have in Ceuta.”

The prime minister once again pointed the finger at “criminal gangs” who had used disinformation to falsely claim that a ruling by Spain’s supreme court meant that no one who entered Ceuta by swimming could be deported back to Morocco.

He also said fake news had been pumped out on social media accounts “associated with Russia, Israel and the international far right that always use migration to attack not just Spain but also Europe”.
Sánchez said that about 1,500 migrants remained in Ceuta, of whom 1,200 are minors, and there would soon be “sufficient capacity” to accommodate all those still in the enclave.

Their continuing presence has led to clashes between some Ceuta residents and police, while some of the migrants have had their belongings burned while sleeping rough on beaches. On Saturday, four Moroccan migrants were arrested for throwing stones at Spanish soldiers.

Spain’s conservative People’s party has accused the government of failing to protect the people of Ceuta. “It did nothing to avoid the invasion on 30 July and it’s doing nothing to stop the public order crisis that’s getting worse every day,” the PP’s leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, said last week.

Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, has described events in Ceuta as “an invasion and an act of war promoted by Morocco and allowed by Sánchez, who is incapable of responding because he is subservient to Morocco”.

articles.title: South African airline defends low-altitude aerial stunt over packed stadium
articles.summary: Airlink says the manoeuvre with two planes in close formation involved careful and precise planning.

blocks.text: "Planning. Precision. Performance," was the airline's message in social media posts, external accompanied by the footage.
In a statement reproduced on a government news site, external, Airlink went into more detail.
"The two aircraft were flown by highly experienced crew, with each comprised of three senior captains operating in the roles of commander, co-pilot and safety/technical officer," the airline said.
It added that the flights were performed with the "approved and rehearsed safety altitude and speed limits for the flypast".
The flight tracking website Flightradar24, external said that according to its analysis "the lead aircraft passed less than 50 feet (15 metres) above the top of the stadium".

Questions have been raised over the risk and potential for disaster involving two planes and a packed stadium, but many South Africans have responded with expressions of national pride that its country's pilots could pull this off.
The low-altitude flyby has become a feature of the build-up to some big matches.
The most notable was when a South African Airways jet flew over a Johannesburg stadium before the start of the 1995 rugby World Cup final which saw South Africa beat New Zealand.

The match, immortalised in the Hollywood film Invictus, was highly symbolic as the country's first black president, Nelson Mandela, donned the jersey of national side, which had been closely associated with the apartheid government and previously excluded players who were not white.

articles.title: Rescuers race to find trapped workers in hydropower plant tunnels after Nepal flooding
articles.summary: Rescuers rushed Monday to reach workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites buried in mud after catastrophic flooding in Nepal and China, as the death toll continued to rise and…

image.caption: A rescuer works at the entrance of a tunnel at Chilime Hydropower Plant as rescue operations continue for people trapped inside following deadly flash floods and a mudslide, in Rasuwa, Nepal. (Ashish Gurung/Reuters)

blocks.text: World

Rescuers rushed Monday to reach workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites buried in mud after catastrophic flooding in Nepal and China, as the death toll continued to rise and increasingly desperate families search for their loved ones.
Multiple foreign teams assisting local rescuers as deaths climb past 900
Hundreds feared trapped in tunnels after Nepal flash floods

The combined deaths in Nepal and China surpassed 900, with more than 4,700 people missing, and a private-sector association representing power companies said at least 900 workers have been unaccounted for from 12 hydropower projects damaged by the floods in Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

Mohan Kumar Dangi, president of the Independent Power Producers' Association, Nepal, or IPPAN, said there's an estimation of at least 500 of the 900 missing workers trapped in the tunnels, although authorities have provided varying numbers and said several foreign teams were assisting Nepali rescuers.

At least one expert said the tunnels offered enough space for people to take refuge and that some workers could have access to oxygen. But others warned that the chances of finding survivors were diminishing.

Dangi said some workers had managed to make contact and call for help when the disaster struck last Wednesday, and some others who managed to flee reported to authorities and relatives that many of their colleagues were still in the tunnels. But he said that, six days after the disaster, fears grew that some might have suffocated.
"We are working in search and rescue of the stranded people from hills, settlements and river areas," said Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal's army spokesman.

Nepal's disaster agency said Monday that 903 deaths had been counted in that country, with 4,247 people, including 592 foreigners, missing. As of Sunday, Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, and Chinese state media said 261 of the missing were foreigners, including over a hundred Nepalis.
Trapped in tunnels

Workers shovelling mud from a flood-ravaged power station in Dhading, Nepal, told The Associated Press that the station is a key node for providing power to over 20,000 people in the region. The workers cleaning the power station said they hope that it is not rebuilt near the river.
Rescue efforts are focused on people trapped in the gigantic tunnels built for controlling the waterflow to produce hydropower.

"The tunnels are built to access hydropower infrastructure and to divert water — an essential step to generate energy. These tunnels are big enough to drive trucks through," said Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria who is currently based in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

"There is enough place for people to take refuge safely inside and from what we understand they have managed to get oxygen to some of those stuck inside and are trying to rescue them now. It's a race for time though as people need food and water."

In the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project, in the hard-hit Rasuwa district, at least 576 were missing, Dangi said, adding that around 300 of them were believed to be trapped inside the project's tunnel. Rescuers have been trying to find survivors for days, working through the rain.
On the Chinese side, rescue and recovery efforts included rebuilding the road leading to Gyirong Port at the border between China and Nepal.

Trucks carried giant rocks as workers worked on repaving a portion of the road, state broadcaster CCTV showed Monday, next to rapidly rushing waters, which have been made more powerful by rains in the past couple of days. The road is now under some two to three metres of water, hampering rescuers' ability to reach the border. The repaving effort was just a little over a kilometre from the border, CCTV said.
Although some rescue teams have managed to reach the border, that represented only a portion of the force.

items: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood
Scientists fear Nepal's disaster is just a glimpse of the carnage climate change could cause

blocks.text: Two days after the disaster, Maraval Nagappan travelled to Nepal to search for his son, who was among the missing. He visited rescue centres and morgues and went as far as 40 kilometres from where his son was believed to have been, but found no sign of him.

His son, Sathya Narayan had been leading a group of 49 Indian devotees who were returning from Mount Kailash — a sacred site in southwestern Tibet. The group has been missing since floodwaters swept through a Chinese immigration complex where they were waiting to cross into Nepal.

Nagappan, who owns the Chennai-based travel company that organized their pilgrimage, and said the group had been expected to complete immigration formalities and leave for Nepal within about two hours. Instead of making the crossing, they were caught in the flood, Nagappan said.

The pilgrimage had begun Aug. 14. "I haven't heard from my son since then. I don't know whether he is alive or dead," he told The Associated Press, but he said he hadn't given up on hearing from his son.

Surveillance footage showed water surging through the immigration complex at the border as people scrambled to escape. Nagappan said some of those seen fleeing were members of his son's group and were identified by the clothes they were wearing.

Wednesday's flash floods started after a glacial collapse high in the Himalayan region. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.
The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

articles.title: Philippines ‘stands out’ in region for cutting all forms of deprivation—ADB
articles.summary: The Philippines stood out in a regional study by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for reducing all three forms of deprivation it tracked, although Filipinos in rural areas remain more likely to face…

blocks.text: The Philippines stood out in a regional study by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for reducing all three forms of deprivation it tracked, although Filipinos in rural areas remain more likely to face hardships than their urban counterparts.

In its “Key Indicators for Asia and the Pacific 2026: Measuring Deprivation at Household and Individual Level” report published on Monday, Aug. 31, the Manila-based multilateral lender examined deprivation among adults aged 25 to 49 across 23 Asia-Pacific economies.

Under the ADB’s approach, deprivation is grouped into three categories: people who are deprived both individually and at the household level; those who live in deprived households but are not personally deprived; and those who experience individual hardships despite living in households considered nonpoor.

Looking at changes over time, the Philippines was among four economies specifically highlighted by the ADB for broad-based progress, with improvements not confined to just one measure but extending across the different dimensions of deprivation it tracked.

“Indonesia, Nepal, the Philippines, and China stand out as examples of economies that have achieved simultaneous declines across all three categories during the respective survey periods,” the ADB said.
The lender said this “aligned improvement” was consistent with broad-based economic growth accompanied by better service delivery that benefited even the most deprived communities.
The report introduced a new way of looking at deprivation that goes beyond measuring poverty at the household level by also examining the circumstances of individual household members.

Individual hardships measured by the ADB include lack of health insurance or internet access, unfavorable employment conditions, limited ownership of a house or land, lack of access to financial services, low educational attainment, as well as limited participation in household financial and health decisions.

The ADB said adding individual-level measures can uncover hardships that conventional household poverty statistics may miss, as people living under the same roof do not necessarily have equal access to opportunities and resources.

In the Philippines, the latest analysis was based on the 2022 demographic and health survey (DHS), covering 15,994 households and 16,627 individuals included in the final sample. For the Philippines, the individual-level portion of the study covered women aged 25 to 49.

The ADB cautioned against using the results to make precise rankings among economies because survey coverage and available indicators differ. In Bangladesh, the Philippines, Tajikistan, and Türkiye, the individual-level data used in the study covered women only, it noted.
Despite the Philippines’ overall improvement, the ADB found that a significant divide remained between rural and urban areas.

The ADB said the Philippines, alongside China, India, and Indonesia, illustrated how sizable rural-urban gaps can persist even in economies where the overall prevalence of deprivation is moderate or low. Across the 23 economies studied, deprivation was higher in rural areas in 21.
“Where rural-urban gaps are wide, investment in rural development is especially critical,” the ADB said.

The ADB’s findings come just weeks after the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) released the country’s first official multidimensional poverty index (MPI), which similarly looks beyond income by measuring overlapping deprivations in education, employment, health and nutrition, as well as housing, water, and sanitation.

Based on preliminary results of the 2024 community-based monitoring system (CBMS), the PSA estimated that 12.4 percent of Filipino households were multidimensionally poor, with an average deprivation intensity of 33.9 percent.

The PSA also estimated that 12.8 percent of Filipinos lived in households classified as multidimensionally poor. This individual headcount, however, remains based on the deprivation status of the household, with people living in the same household assigned the same deprivation score.

This differs from the ADB’s approach, which adds a separate individual-level lens to identify people who may personally experience significant hardships even when the households they live in are considered nonpoor.

Education accounted for the largest share of multidimensional poverty among Filipinos at 40.7 percent, followed by housing, water, and sanitation at 31.3 percent; health and nutrition, 18.5 percent; and employment, 9.5 percent, according to the PSA.
Across the 23 economies covered by the ADB study, about 31 percent of adults aged 25 to 49 were classified as individually deprived despite living in nonpoor households.
About two-fifths of these individuals, equivalent to 12 percent of the overall age group studied, experienced a high to extreme breadth of deprivation.
The ADB also found that individual deprivation was not confined to poor families, with people experiencing individual-level deprivation present across household wealth groups.

While deprivation generally declined over time, the ADB said progress was slowest in reducing the range of hardships faced by individually deprived people living in nonpoor households, indicating that improvements in household economic conditions alone may not be enough to address their needs.

articles.title: House Democrat to launch challenge to Trump’s ‘Lake America’ order – US politics live
articles.summary: Debbie Dingell plans to introduce her ‘Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act’ today following president’s latest escalation in US-Canada trade war

blocks.text: Key events

items: 39m agoHouse Democrat plans to introduce bill to nullify Trump's 'Lake America' executive order

blocks.caption: Robert Tait

blocks.text: Robert Tait
Having reportedly read Victor Hugo’s Les Misérables, in French, during a military tour of duty in Iraq, Jamieson Greer considered himself an unlikely target for accusations of francophobia.

But Donald Trump’s US trade representative, hitherto one of the president’s less high-profile cabinet members, found himself in that uncomfortable position amid the acrimonious collapse of bilateral trade talks with Canada that now threatens to degenerate into an all-out trade war between the two close trading partners whose economies are tightly intertwined.

An apparent pending deal between Washington and Ottawa aimed at avoiding damaging tit-for-tat tariffs broke down at the last minute, with Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, claiming his country had come “under attack” from the US.

Among the multiple and complex points of disagreement was a Canadian accusation that US negotiators had pressed for a weakening of legal protections for the French language, which is most heavily spoken in the province of Quebec.

Canadian provisions include legislation that mandates streaming and online video companies to invest in and promote Canadian content and promote the French language. Carney cast US objections to such regulations as a deal breaker, and said they amounted to “threats to French language and culture”.

For Greer, a fluent French speaker who once served as a Mormon missionary in Belgium, France and Luxembourg, the charge was too much. “I speak French, too,” he told CNBC, dismissing the claims as “a funny, fake story”.
Donald Trump ⁠on Sunday said NBC’s Kristen ‌Welker – host of Meet the Press – should face “rebuke or punishment” from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC).

Welker, during a live segment for a local Washington DC affiliate, described the success record of political candidates whom the president had endorsed as “mixed”. The segment aired prior to Sunday’s edition of Meet the Press.
Trump “is going to loom large over these midterms,” Welker remarked on that live shot. “He, of course, has endorsed a slate of candidates in the primaries. He’s had some mixed results.”
But Welker went on to mention Trump’s endorsement of appointed interim US senator Darline Graham, sister of her late predecessor Lindsey Graham, who was successful in her primary battle.

Nonetheless, the president then took verbal aim at Welker with a social media post deriding her as the “Unpopular ‘Hostess’ of … Meet the Fake Press,” accused her of “purposeful inaccuracy” and warned that she would “be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment”.
The post also said that Trump hoped his appointed FCC chair Brendan Carr – and Carr’s colleagues on the commission – “take this Threat to our Country very seriously”.

Once Meet the Press actually started on Sunday, a guest analyst on the show said “the single most important factor in who the Republican nominee will be in [the presidential election of] 2028 will be who Donald Trump endorses”.
House Democrat plans to introduce bill to nullify Trump's 'Lake America' executive order
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
As House representatives return from the summer recess, one Democrat has already set in motion a plan to nullify Donald Trump’s latest conceited executive order.
The president signed an executive order on Thursday directing the federal government to rename Lake Ontario, making it Lake America, amid his escalating trade war with Canada.

“We have a gulf and we have a lake – now all we need is an ocean. Maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and/or the Pacific,” he told reporters, sitting at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office. “Maybe we’ll change them both.”
But House Democrat Debbie Dingell said she plans to introduce a bill later today to nullify the name change, titled the “Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act”.

blocks.caption: Debbie Dingell Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: “People do not understand how intertwined our two countries are,” Dingell told Politico, adding: “And this is insane, this naming Lake Ontario ‘Lake America.’”

Dingell said she had accrued more than 100 signatures from fellow House Democrats in a letter to the president, urging the Trump administration “to change its diplomatic approach with our closest ally, Canada, and recognize the importance of the United States-Canada relationship”.

“I grew up in a small town called St Clair, and when I got up and looked out my bedroom window every day, I didn’t see America. I saw Canada,” Dingell said. “We lived that close. Canada was as close to us as [the Cannon House Office Building] is to the Capitol.”

Trump’s order directed federal agencies to adopt the name-change on US maps, documents and databases. Google Maps has changed Lake Ontario’s name to Lake America for US users to reflect the president’s executive renaming order.
Meanwhile, the president posted overnight on his Truth Social website:

double quotation markFor many years, the USA has been losing more than 60 Billion Dollars a year with Canada. Why??? Our long ago stolen businesses are now coming back to America in order to avoid paying tariffs. They are lining up, just like the rest of the World!!!
In other developments:

items: Trump and Canada continued a verbal duel on Saturday over the US government’s administrative renaming of Lake Ontario, with the Ontario premier erecting a giant sign saying “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” – and the American president posting a video of him tearing down an avatar of that sign, erecting a replacement saying Lake America, and dancing to YMCA. Rhetoric over the naming of Lake Ontario is the public face of an escalating trade dispute between the US and its northern neighbor involving a 50% US tariff on Canadian steel and retaliatory tariffs from Ottawa.

The White House “border czar,” Tom Homan, denied on Sunday that deporting British far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos just a day after being arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) amounted to preferential treatment. Homan said it was his understanding that Yiannopoulos, 41, had overstayed what he believed to be a visitor visa, had not appeared at an immigration hearing and was issued a final order of removal on 22 July.

Welker, during a live segment for a local Washington, DC, affiliate, described the success record of political candidates whom the president had endorsed as “mixed”. The segment aired prior to Sunday’s edition of Meet the Press.
