That was not my intention.”

articles.title: PNP orders tighter watch on vulnerable roads, bridges amid rains
articles.summary: After one bridge collapsed and another partially gave way in Tarlac City amid heavy rains, the Philippine National Police (PNP) ordered local police units to closely monitor and secure vulnerable…

blocks.text: (PHOTO: PNP FACEBOOK PAGE)

After one bridge collapsed and another partially gave way in Tarlac City amid heavy rains, the Philippine National Police (PNP) ordered local police units to closely monitor and secure vulnerable roads and bridges.
Agana Bridge collapsed on Aug. 29 while it was serving as an alternative route following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge a day earlier.
The PNP said an SUV fell into the river during the Agana Bridge collapse. Four passengers remained missing, while one was rescued.
In a statement, the PNP said its personnel in Tarlac immediately secured the area and joined the search and rescue operations.

“Our personnel immediately responded to the incident, secured the area, coordinated with the other responding agencies, and assisted in the search and rescue operations. Our priority was to ensure public safety and help locate those who remain missing,” PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr. said.

Nartatez said the PNP would strengthen coordination among police commanders, local government units, and disaster response agencies as continuing rains affect roads, bridges, and other vulnerable areas.

“We will remind all police commanders to coordinate closely with their respective local government units and disaster-response agencies, particularly in securing bridges, roads and other areas affected by the continuing rains,” he said.

The PNP said the directive was in line with the orders of President Marcos and Department of the Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla to strengthen public safety measures and ensure a coordinated government response in areas affected by hazards and continuing rains.
Nartatez directed the Tarlac police to maintain security and crowd control around the collapsed bridge and continue participating in the search and rescue operations for the four missing passengers.

“Local police units should prioritize public safety, closely monitor vulnerable areas, immediately secure unsafe roads and bridges, and coordinate with local authorities so that appropriate measures can be taken without delay,” he said.

articles.title: Badenoch to reshuffle shadow cabinet following Patel and Cleverly resignations
articles.summary:
Tory leader expected to install Tom Tugendhat as shadow foreign secretary as Cleverly quits to run for London mayor

Kemi Badenoch is to reshuffle her shadow cabinet on Monday, and is…

blocks.text: Kemi Badenoch is to reshuffle her shadow cabinet on Monday, and is expected to install Tom Tugendhat as shadow foreign secretary to replace Priti Patel.

Tugendhat, a former security minister, was a leadership candidate who had previously declined to join the shadow cabinet. Badenoch is also expected to replace James Cleverly, the shadow communities secretary, who has resigned from the shadow cabinet to run for London mayor.

Patel announced on Sunday night she would be leaving as shadow foreign secretary but said she would take on an “international role” with the party to build ties with other rightwing parties across the world.
The Telegraph reported on Sunday that Tugendhat, who has been outspoken on China and Iran since returning to the backbenches, will be her replacement.

In a statement, she said she wanted to also spend more time in her Essex constituency. “I’m pleased to continue supporting Kemi and the Conservative party in a new role strengthening our relationships with fellow conservatives and centre-right parties around the world,” she said.
“At a time of profound global uncertainty, when our values and freedoms are under threat, conservatives must work more closely together.

“With Labour axing key transport schemes, cancelling plans for a new school, threatening to destroy our countryside, councils and communities and cutting policing, I will be a vocal champion for my constituents in the House of Commons defending their interests and demanding action.”
Badenoch has also sacked Stuart Andrew, the shadow health secretary, who said in a post on X he would be returning to the backbenches.

Other changes will include a replacement for the shadow energy secretary Claire Coutinho, who will soon go on maternity leave with her second child. Coutinho had been widely tipped as Badenoch’s preferred candidate to eventually replace the shadow chancellor Mel Stride, who many Tories have said privately they believe is failing to make the necessary impact.

Badenoch is also expected to find a new role for Julia Lopez, who had shadowed the now abolished science, innovation and technology department. Helen Grant, the shadow solicitor general, has also asked to leave the shadow frontbench.
Cleverly, who announced his run for London mayor on Sunday, denied he had quit the shadow cabinet following a shift to the right under Badenoch’s leadership.
after newsletter promotion
“I am going to put forward a classic Conservative case to be the mayor of London, and it’s about enterprise, it’s about opportunity,” Cleverly told Times Radio.
“That is a classically Conservative vision, and it will run in parallel to and supportive of Kemi’s plans for the country as a whole.”

Cleverly, who lost the Conservative leadership race to Badenoch, is considered a more moderate voice in a party that has moved to the right as support for Nigel Farage’s rightwing Reform UK has grown.
But the appointment of Tugendhat as shadow foreign secretary would bring a key voice from the party’s more centrist One Nation grouping into the fold, though Tugendhat is hawkish on foreign affairs.

articles.summary: Israel said one of its largest ever arms export deals would entail setting up an air defense system for Greece.

image.caption: Included in the deal are elements of Israel's 'David's Sling' air defense system [FILE: Apr 2, 2017]Image: Sebastian Scheiner/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Israel and Greece signed an arms export deal worth around €3 billion (roughly $3.48 billion) on Monday, Israel's Defense Ministry said.
"Israel will build Greece a comprehensive, multi-layered air defense array, drawing entirely on Israeli-made systems," a ministry statement said.
The statement added that the systems would draw on the "extensive operational experience Israel's defense establishment has gained during the war," in seeming reference to the conflict with Iran.
What do we know about Greece's 'Achilles Shield?'

The "Achilles Shield" agreement will see Israel export several systems, including David's Sling and SPYDER, manufactured by Rafael; and BARAK MX, manufactured by Israel Aerospace Industries, the Times of Israel reported.
The deal was signed on Monday at the ministry headquarters in Tel Aviv by Defense Ministry Director General Amir Baram and his Greek counterpart, Ioannis Bouras.
It is part of a larger military modernization program, the Reuters news agency reported, citing officials.

By 2036, Greece plans to spend some €28 billion to build what it calls the "Achilles Shield," an ​anti-ballistic missile, anti-aircraft and anti-drone system. This also includes fighter jet purchases from the US, and warships from France and Italy.
Greece currently uses a mix of US-made Patriot air defense missiles, Russian S-300 systems and other various ​short-range air defences.
Israel and Greece, who share strong economic and diplomatic ties, have been negotiating the deal for around three years, according to the Jerusalem Post.
The two countries operate an air ⁠training center ​in Greece, and hold joint annual military exercises and cooperate on anti-drone systems and cybersecurity.
"This is the largest defense export deal in the history of Israel-Greece relations, and one of the largest in the history of the State of Israel," the Israeli Defense Ministry said.
Greece has a longstanding dispute with Turkey over territorial, maritime, and air sovereignty issues in the Aegean Sea and eastern Mediterranean.
Amid threats from Iran during the ongoing war, Greece recently relocated a Patriot air defense system to the island of Crete, which hosts a large US base at Souda.

articles.title: Pilandok to intensify into tropical storm by Sept. 1
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok is forecast to intensify into a tropical storm by Tuesday, Sept. 1, and remain a tropical storm as it moves toward southern Japan, the state weather…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok is forecast to intensify into a tropical storm by Tuesday, Sept. 1, and remain a tropical storm as it moves toward southern Japan, the state weather bureau said Monday.

In its 5 p.m. bulletin, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Pilandok was located 1,145 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon, moving west-northwestward at 10 kilometers per hour. It had maximum sustained winds of 55 kph near the center and gustiness of up to 70 kph.
No tropical cyclone wind signal is currently hoisted over any part of the country.
Pagasa said Pilandok could remain almost stationary over the Philippine Sea east of extreme Northern Luzon for the next 36 hours before moving generally north-northwestward.
The tropical depression is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by Wednesday afternoon or evening.

“This tropical cyclone is less likely to make landfall over the country and will remain far from the Philippine landmass,” Pagasa said, but noted that the forecast track may still be subject to change.
The agency earlier reported that three other systems were being monitored outside the PAR, with one having a medium chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.

As of its 2 p.m. monitoring, Tropical Depression Saudel, formerly Obet, was about 1,175 kilometers west of extreme Northern Luzon, while another tropical depression was about 570 kilometers west-northwest of Itbayat, Batanes.
A low-pressure area, meanwhile, was about 3,080 kilometers east of southeastern Luzon and had a medium chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours, Pagasa said. /mcm

articles.title: BIR chief highlights fair, simple tax administration at ECCP forum
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A tax administration that is fair, simple, predictable, and partnership-driven — that’s what Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR)…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A tax administration that is fair, simple, predictable, and partnership-driven — that’s what Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) outlined during the European Chamber of Commerce of the Philippines (ECCP) Tax Forum 2026 held on Aug. 13.

“Businesses can operate under demanding rules. What is much harder is operating under uncertain rules, inconsistent interpretations, or unpredictable processes,” Mendoza told the forum participants, which included business leaders and tax professionals.
The four commitments he presented at the forum are supported by the BIR Dares reform and legacy agenda, which stands for:

items: D – digital and data transformation: upgrading online systems, data-driven auditing, and digital assistance tools, such as Chatbot Revie
A – audit reform and accountability: restricting audits to a strict “one Letter of Authority per taxpayer per year” policy and implementing an “audit-the-auditors” system
R – revenue collection and base protection: intensifying enforcement and tracking down tax evasion or fake transactions
E – employee empowerment and welfare promotion: supporting personnel to build high standards of professionalism
S – service excellence and stakeholder engagement: improving taxpayer services and transparency

blocks.text: As a BIR statement on Monday put it, the BIR is pursuing those reforms to achieve these goals:

items: make compliance easier, through digitalization to reduce processing time
make audits more consistent and accountable
ensure that enforcement will focus on genuine compliance risks

blocks.text: Mendoza stressed the importance of sustaining private sector engagement to shape reforms that respond to actual business conditions and operational concerns.

“The private sector sees things that government sometimes does not. You experience our regulations in actual business operations. You know where processes work. You know where they create bottlenecks. You know where requirements overlap,” Mendoza said.
“We will listen. We will improve. We will enforce the law fairly. And we will continue making it easier for taxpayers to do the right thing,” added.

The ECCP Tax Forum — “From Preparation to Protection: Navigating Tax Compliance in a Changing Landscape” — included sessions focusing on tax compliance, regulatory developments, digitalization, audits, dispute resolution, and other issues affecting businesses operating in the Philippines.

Among the BIR officials present were BIR Deputy Commissioners Larry M. Barcelo and Marissa O. Cabreros, Assistant Commissioners Raquel Cristina V. Baltazar and Mariza R. Uy, and Collection Programs Division Chief Glenn Alde. /atm

articles.title: PNP-HPG files complaint vs 2 Customs officers in Bulacan warehouse raid
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A complaint has been filed against two personnel of the Bureau of Customs (BOC) who were present in the warehouse in Bulacan that was raided for allegedly containing “smuggled”…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A complaint has been filed against two personnel of the Bureau of Customs (BOC) who were present in the warehouse in Bulacan that was raided for allegedly containing “smuggled” cigarette products.

The seven-page complaint, filed before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor in Malolos City, Bulacan, stated that alleged middleman Jesus Froilan Acebes Carpiso identified two BOC personnel as among those present at the warehouse when the entrapment operation was conducted, according to his sworn affidavit.

Filed by the Philippine National Police-Highway Patrol Group (PNP-HPG) on Friday, Aug. 28, the complaint asked the prosecutor’s office to admit Carpiso’s sworn statement, along with other supporting documentary and/or electronic evidence subsequently obtained, and consider these as integral parts of the records of the case.

It also stated that the two BOC personnel, along with another individual, should be included in the preliminary investigation and the determination of probable cause, with “appropriate subpoenas” issued against them.

The PNP-HPG complainants said the complaint should be resolved based on the totality of the evidence and that the existence or absence of probable cause should be determined individually for each respondent.
In his sworn affidavit, Carpiso stated that the two personnel were present at the Bulacan warehouse when the Regional Highway Patrol Unit-National Capital Region conducted the raid.

He identified the two BOC personnel as the individuals who allegedly received payment in exchange for 225 boxes of allegedly smuggled Red Carnival cigarettes during the entrapment, or buy-bust, operation on Aug. 19.
Carpiso allegedly served as the middleman who facilitated the sale of the smuggled cigarettes.
In an interview with Bilyonaryo News Channel on Aug. 25, BOC Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno claimed that he had no knowledge of individuals identified by the aliases “Joy” and “Alex.”
However, a BOC memorandum dated Aug. 20 indicated that the two were among those who prepared an incident report concerning the Bulacan raid.

Earlier, Nepomuceno said the BOC will file a complaint with the National Police Commission against members of the PNP-HPG who allegedly accosted customs personnel destroying smuggled cigarettes seized in operations.
“If our personnel are in the wrong, then we will find out,” he said.

articles.title: [Newsstand] The strongest argument for determining two-thirds impeachment vote
articles.summary: Dean Mel Sta.Maria’s reasoning makes eminent sense—and does not need 16 votes in the Senate to become the rule

blocks.text: How many votes are needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte on any of the four articles of impeachment? Over two days last week, Dean Mel Sta. Maria revisited the issue. He had already spoken on the matter before, and had made a strong argument for considering the conviction threshold not as static (a fixed number of 16 senators) but as variable (because of the “two-thirds” language of the Constitution).

Inspired by an insight of Ateneo Law School constitutional law professor Leo Camacho, Sta. Maria focused on the significance of a qualifying phrase in the constitutional provision on impeachment. To this writer, who has worked for decades in the trenches of the English language, the qualification seems to me to be the very crux of the matter.
The pertinent provision is Article XI, Section 3 (6) of the 1987 Constitution, which in its entirely reads as follows:

“The Senate shall have the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment. When sitting for that purpose, the Senators shall be on oath or affirmation. When the President of the Philippines is on trial, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall preside, but shall not vote. No person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate.”

The qualifying phrase is the opening clause of the second sentence: “When sitting for that purpose” — that is, when the Senate transforms itself into an impeachment court. This, Sta. Maria argues, is the key.
Listen to him:

“When we examine Section 3 (6) [of] Article Xl, the first sentence describes the forum where the impeachment trial will occur: THE SENATE. Then the second sentence provides the transformation process. It says that when senators take their role in the impeachment court as judges, they shall take their ‘oath or affirmation.’ This oath or affirmation is the prerequisite ‘while sitting for that purpose,’ meaning while participating as judges in the impeachment court. ‘Sitting’ easily connotes presence.

“The law is therefore clear. A senator cannot be transformed into a judge without taking his oath or affirmation. These two are the sustaining elements during the duration of the proceedings that shall allow them to be judges. Without the oath or affirmation, they are senators as legislators but not judges in the impeachment court.”

The number of votes needed to convict Duterte, or indeed any impeachable official, is one of three threshold issues the presiding officer of the impeachment court, Senator Chiz Escudero, addressed on July 6, the first day of the impeachment trial and the day he was elected to preside. (READ: What’s the legal basis for Escudero’s 16-vote threshold in impeachment trial?)

“On the first issue, the Constitution provides that no person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate. With 24 members of the Senate, a literal interpretation of this means that conviction requires the affirmative vote of at least 16 senator-judges.”

Senator-judges who disagree, Escudero said, can run to the Supreme Court. “This is the prevailing law today, and whether we agree with it or not, we must abide by it. However, those who disagree are not without recourse, because this is without prejudice to the right of any party who holds a different view to seek judicial relief.”

On the second day of the trial, Senator Ping Lacson asked whether Escudero’s reading of this threshold issue was, as the Journal phrased it, “a personal legal opinion or a ruling of the Impeachment Court.” Escudero said it was a ruling of “the Chair” (and therefore of the court); since it was unchallenged, it is in effect.
This literal interpretation remains the ruling of the impeachment court, though a person with legal standing can still raise it to the Supreme Court.

But, as Sta. Maria’s analysis makes clear, it is a literal but incomplete interpretation. In the Constitution’s own language, the phrase “all the Members of the Senate” has already been qualified by “senators [who] shall be on oath or affirmation.” And senators take that oath or make that affirmation only “when [the Senate is] sitting for that purpose” of conducting an impeachment trial.

It does not make sense to include senators who are not on oath or affirmation as among “all the Members of the Senate” who will decide on the impeachment case. I use “sense” in its ordinary-language meaning, which is how I and many millions of Filipinos read and understood the provisions of the Constitution when ratifying it in 1987. (I was teaching in Cagayan de Oro then, and took part in workshops and forums discussing the draft charter.)

To non-lawyers like me, Sta. Maria’s legal analysis is immediately clarifying. The Senate needs to convert itself into an impeachment court before it can hear an impeachment case; senators elected as legislators need to undergo a process that will transform them into judges. That process of transformation happens when the Senate sits for the specific purpose of hearing the impeachment case; senators become senator-judges when they take an oath or make an affirmation.

Why should senators who failed to do either — because they were sick, or in detention, or in hiding — be considered as senator-judges? In the particular context of Article XI, Sec. 3 (6), “all the Members of the Senate” must refer to senators who are judges by oath or affirmation.

In a comment he posted as a reply to Sta. Maria, the former Supreme Court justice and member of the 1986 Constitutional Commission, the formidable Adolf Azcuna, suggested another reading. “You could also say that the reason it says two-thirds of all the members of the Senate is to exclude the Chief Justice from the computation.”

He was referring to the express provision that, when it is the president of the Philippines who is on trial, it must be the chief justice of the Supreme Court who will serve as presiding officer of the impeachment court. But, to me (again, as a heavy user of the English language, not as a lawyer), this reading seems superfluous, because the language of our Constitution (in contrast to the language of the US Constitution, where our impeachment conventions come from) very specifically provides that, “When the President of the Philippines is on trial, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall preside, but shall not vote.”
If the chief justice cannot vote, why would he or she be included in “the computation”?

I think ordinary-language interpretation is important because that’s how fundamental laws should be read: as intelligible to ordinary citizens. Unlike ordinary laws passed by Congress, a constitution needs to be ratified by a majority of the people (only a few of whom are lawyers) before it can take effect.
The same dynamic applies in the Senate; a majority of senators are non-lawyers.

Presiding Officer Escudero skipped a pivotal step when he said “any party who holds a different view” can petition the Supreme Court. Why file a petition when the senator-judges can decide among themselves to settle the issue?

The Senate’s Rules of Impeachment allow “a Member of the Senate” to ask for a “formal vote” regarding “questions of evidence,” with the vote to be decided (since the standard is not defined in the rules) by simple majority. The very same rules were amended to allow the election of a presiding officer who is not the Senate president, again by simple majority. And the impeachment court elected Escudero as presiding officer by a vote of 12 to 8.

Instead of running to the Supreme Court, senator-judges would be well within their rights to call for a vote in the impeachment court to decide the issue of the conviction threshold. First, relying on the Supreme Court to decide definitively on such a basic standard — how many votes are needed to convict an impeached official — is to dilute “the sole power” given by the Constitution to the Senate “to try and decide all cases of impeachment.”
Second, questioning the ruling of the chair is expressly provided for in the Rules of Impeachment.
Third, the issue can be decided at a strategic stage in the trial, to minimize the possibility of Supreme Court interference.

And, fourth, the fact that three senators are unable to serve as senator-judges is a matter of extreme relevance. They remain senators until their term ends or unless they are expelled from the Senate; but because they are not in a position to take the oath or make the affirmation, they are not senator-judges. You don’t need 16 votes in the Senate to recognize that — just a simple majority. – Rappler.com
Veteran journalist John Nery is a Rappler columnist. He anchors Rappler’s special coverage of the Duterte impeachment trial and, every Wednesday, hosts In the Public Square with John Nery.

articles.title: Inside the sea cucumber smuggling boom
articles.summary: A quiet multimillion‑dollar black market is exploding across the Indian Ocean, driven by one unlikely animal: the sea cucumber.

image.caption: Sea cucumbers are neither cucumbers nor fish, but invertebrate marine animals with a skin or hard coveringImage: oceansasia.org

blocks.text: When it comes to smuggling, squishy sea blobs that spend their lives eating and pooping are probably not what comes to mind. But a group of lumpen creatures known as sea cucumbers are at the center of a $200 million (€175 million) black market trade.

Known alternately and misleadingly as sea cucumbers or sand fish, they are actually neither cucumbers nor fish, but echinoderms. In other words, invertebrate marine animals with a skin or a hard covering.

Found in abundance around the Andaman Islands — the easternmost landmass of the Indian territory— local biologist Sangamesh Uday says they are so ecologically important that without them the intertidal zone "wouldn't be an ecosystem, it would just be broken rocks."

blocks.caption: Sea cucumbers are crucial for the local ecosystem, says local biologist  Uday Image: Parinmnpa/Dreamstime/IMAGO

blocks.text: The 1500 or so species of sea cucumber around the world are great marine recyclers. They eat organic material including bacteria and microalgae, break it down, and excrete clean oxygenated sand. This keeps vital nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorous in circulation and suppresses coral diseases.

It also boosts ocean alkalinity levels which helps to slow down acidification — which is becoming a huge issue as rising levels of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere cause oceans to warm. In short, it's hard to overstate the environmental importance of these innocuous looking lumps.
Why are they being smuggled?

To their detriment, sea cucumbers are also considered a delicacy, especially in China and Southeast Asia. Yet historical records show their trade between Indonesian fishers and Chinese traders even 800 years ago.

They are used in soups, served as pickled sides or turned into traditional medicine. And though there is some scientific evidence that the Omega-3 they contain is a useful antioxidant and anti-inflammatory, they're mostly popular because they're quite phallic — and therefore considered an aphrodisiac.

blocks.caption: Sea cucumbers are considered a delicacy, used in soups or used as traditional medicineImage: oceansasia.org

blocks.text: Since the 1980s, commercial sea cucumber harvesting has expanded globally — with better access as well as higher incomes and demand in East Asia acting as the main drivers. Though many countries have outlawed the practice, some like Sri Lanka and Madagascar do allow fishing and aquaculture. Of the existing sea cucumber fisheries, 70% have become overexploited globally.

The combination of the increasing demand and legal complexities, has drawn the attention of minor and major mafias. Some of the largest Mexican cartels and even the Japanese Yakuza have been reported as diversifying their portfolios and using sea cucumbers and other related sea creatures to keep the money flowing.
These illicit groups enter every aspect of the supply chain — from extorting fishermen to the final smuggling of illegally-caught cucumbers across borders.

They exploit weak environmental regulations and a lack of official knowledge around rules and species. Sea cucumbers are sometimes marked as legal fish consignments or smuggled into countries that do allow trade in the species.
Leading expert on sea cucumber crime, Teale Phelps Bondaroff, says awareness is critical in dealing with the issue.
"While many law enforcement officers may be on the lookout for drugs, weapons, or well-known wildlife contraband like ivory, rhino horns, or shark fins, sea cucumbers may slip past," he told DW.
Poachers from overseas drawn to the Andaman Islands
The Indian government began regulating sea cucumbers in the 1980s and introduced a blanket ban on fishing them in 2001, when it saw the impact of the illicit trade on local populations.

Since then, India has become the country with the strongest protections for the species. Anyone who catches one faces a seven-year jail term — the same sentence handed down for poaching a tiger or elephant.

As a result, sea cucumbers close to the Andaman Islands have generally thrived. In the ocean around Myanmar, around 50km (30 miles) further north, it's a different picture. Civil war in the country has severely impacted local livelihoods and local black-market agents are using the instability to offer comparatively higher sums for a boatload of illegally caught sea cucumbers. And as their numbers in local waters dwindle, poachers head south.
It is no easy game, however. They have to dodge the Indian coast guard, navy, police, evade local fishermen and even dense populations of crocodiles.
Inside the $200 million black market for... sea cucumbers?!

They survive on fish, freediving using hookah pipes to breathe, and spend months rationing their diesel to ensure they have enough to make it back home — evading the Myanmar authorities and pirates looking to try and steal their catch.

Many poachers are caught by the regional Andaman and Nicobar police, who are being specifically trained to comb the mangrove islands to find them. At least 50 people have been arrested in the past year, some as young as 16 and some in their 60s. And some who have come back for the second or third time — at risk of being incarcerated again, after completing full sentences.
Is there a way to stop the illegal trade?
Despite the efforts of the Indian authorities, the number of poachers coming in, year after year, has stayed stable.

Bondaroff sees a need to sound the alarm at a global level. Other similar trades, like that of shark fins, have been slowed thanks to increased awareness about its cruelty and impact on the ecosystem — making it less socially acceptable.
"The solution must include educating consumers about the harms of unsustainable and illegal sea cucumber extraction and tackling seafood fraud."

blocks.caption: Poachers often hide on mangrove islands in the Andamans, making it hard to catch themImage: Dheeraj Aithal/DW

blocks.text: Other suggestions include India opening up small areas of its waters where sea cucumbers can be legally fished. Or introducing community-based aquaculture that is easier to regulate and would also benefit local fishers.
But Bondaroff says tackling the problem also requires cooperation and a deep understanding of the issue.
"This means liaising and information sharing between governments and law enforcement agencies," he said. "And working together to address the complex financial crimes that enable sea cucumber crime."
This report was supported by the Pulitzer Center.

articles.title: From playing Serena Williams on screen to following in her footsteps
articles.summary: Having played a young Serena Williams on the big screen, teenager Thea Frodin is ready to follow in the American great's footsteps at the US Open.

blocks.text: Thea Frodin once played a young Serena Williams on the big screen. Now, the teenager is ready to follow in the American great's footsteps at the US Open.
Five years ago, Frodin was chosen as a tennis-playing body double for the actress cast as her childhood idol in the Oscar-nominated film 'King Richard'.
That involved the then 12-year-old American working alongside actor Will Smith as he portrayed Richard Williams, the father of sisters Serena and Venus.
"Being able to play the role of somebody that I looked up to for my whole life was super special," Frodin told the WTA website., external
"I was honoured. She was one of the players that I looked up to most, just when I was starting to play.
"She's such an inspiration to me."
Now, Frodin will make her main-draw singles debut at her home Grand Slam, where Serena and Venus will this year team up in the doubles.
To make the occasion even more special, she has been drawn against world number two Elena Rybakina, a two-time major winner and the reigning Australian Open champion.
"I'm trying to stay in the moment as much as possible," said Frodin.
"This is a huge opportunity for me to enjoy the moment, have fun and see what I can do.
"The atmosphere, how loud the crowd will be, I feel like I fit well in that environment."
It has not taken long for Frodin to secure her maiden appearance at the sport's highest level.

The 17-year-old earned a wildcard into this year's US Open women's singles competition - just as Venus Williams has done - by winning the United States Tennis Association' (USTA) Girls' 18s National Championships.
It comes in a year where Frodin reached the semi-finals of the Australian Open girls' singles - her best result as a junior at a major.

She also made her qualifying debut on the WTA Tour as a wildcard in Miami, and pushed former world number 35 Viktorija Golubic in a three-set loss in her first meeting with a player ranked inside the top-100.
But on Tuesday, she will walk out for the biggest match of her life.
"To be standing here right now and actually getting a chance to play in the main draw, it means everything," said Frodin.
"[Rybakina] is number two for a reason, so I'm expecting a battle. Hopefully, I can bring out my best level against her."
And, while she has never met the Williams sisters, Frodin is hoping that can change this fortnight.
"Hopefully, if I get a chance to hit with them or just meet them, anything, I'll take it," Frodin added.
"That would be incredible. That would be a dream."

articles.title: MARINA to resume processing of seafarer' SIDs, SRBs on Sept. 1 after cyberattack
articles.summary: The Maritime Authority Industry (MARINA) on Monday announced that it will resume the processing of Seafarer's Identity Document (SID) and Seafarer's Record Book (SRB) on September 1 following the…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 5:45pm

The Maritime Authority Industry (MARINA) on Monday announced that it will resume the processing of Seafarer's Identity Document (SID) and Seafarer's Record Book (SRB) on September 1 following the recent security breach on their system.

MARINA Administrator Sonia Malaluan confirmed the security breach happened last August 13. Hence, they had to issue certifications for the meantime seafarers who are bound to travel with expired SIDs.

"Kailangan namin i-stop ang processing ng SID at SRB. So meaning, the whole system, we have to put it down para masigurado na hindi na lumala habang hindi pa alam kung ano talaga ang nangyari...After several hours, at the end of August 13, it seems medyo nahirapan agad-agad ibalik ang sistema," she said in a press conference.

(We needed to stop the processing of the SID and SRB. Meaning, we had to take down the whole system to ensure it wouldn't get worse while we still didn't know what actually happened... After several hours, at the end of August 13, it seemed quite difficult to restore the system immediately.)
"Ang MARINA naman, we implemented measure na yung mga aalis nating seafarers ay makaalis, so we issued a certification. Ito po ay mga expired SID," Malaluan added.
(On MARINA's end, we implemented measures so that our departing seafarers could still leave, so we issued a certification. These are for those with expired SIDs.)
MARINA said they conducted tests on their system over the weekend, which showed successful results.

"Sa ngayon po, mayroon kaming successful testing nitong Sabado,at patuloy pa rin po today. Pero nakakapag-print na po kami ng mga SIDs, SRBs, pero this will be under our very controlled environment muna. Hindi po lahatan," said Malaluan.

(As of now, we had a successful test this Saturday, and it's still ongoing today. But we are now able to print SIDs and SRBs, though this will be under our very controlled environment for now. It won't be for everyone yet.)
The MARINA official added that the processing of SIDs and SRBs will be done in its central office for now.

"We can assure by tomorrow, stop na po namin yung certification. Uunahin po natin bigyan ng SIDs, SRDs lahat ng papaalis na. ‘Yung testing po natin ay dito muna sa Central Office. So concentrated muna kami dito sa Manila," said Malaluan.

(We can assure that by tomorrow, we will stop issuing certifications. We will prioritize giving SIDs and SRBs to all those who are about to depart. Our testing for now is here at the Central Office. So we are concentrated here in Manila for the time being.)
"Patuloy ang restoration of the entire system. We are taking slowly but carefully to make sure na ang security natin ay hindi na ulit mako-compromise," she added.
(The restoration of the entire system is ongoing. We are taking it slowly but carefully to make sure that our security will not be compromised again.) —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Peso remains Asia’s ‘weakest link’ despite hawkish BSP stance—MUFG
articles.summary: The Philippine peso remains Asia’s “weakest link” as markets remain largely unconvinced that the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) hawkish policy stance can sufficiently contain inflation without…

blocks.text: The Philippine peso remains Asia’s “weakest link” as markets remain largely unconvinced that the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) hawkish policy stance can sufficiently contain inflation without further weakening economic growth, according to Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) Bank Ltd.

The Tokyo-based financial giant noted that the peso has continued to lose ground despite the BSP’s recent rate hikes, with the currency falling to successive record lows against the United States (US) dollar last week.

“[BSP] Governor [Eli M.] Remolona [Jr.] has signaled willingness to tighten policy further as inflation risks remain elevated, but markets continue to focus on the difficult balance between containing inflation and preserving growth,” MUFG Global Markets Research senior currency analyst Lloyd Chan said in a commentary on Monday, Aug. 31.

Last week, the peso sank to a record low against the US dollar, making it Asia’s worst-performing currency over the past week as soaring energy import costs and a widening trade deficit offset recent central bank rate hikes.

MUFG earlier noted that the peso’s underperformance stemmed from persistent pressure on the nation’s external account. The peso closed at ₱62.265 per dollar on Friday, Aug. 28, sinking past its previous historic low of ₱61.888 set just a day earlier.

According to the Japanese lender, the peso fell one percent in the previous week, extending its broader decline, with the currency down 1.6 percent since the start of August, 1.4 percent this quarter, and 5.8 percent so far this year.
For its part, the BSP raised its benchmark policy rate by 25 basis points (bps) to five percent, marking its third consecutive hike aimed at reining in sticky inflation.

Headline inflation slowed to a three-month low of 6.2 percent in July from 6.4 percent in June, down from its peak of 7.2 percent in April. Core inflation—which excludes volatile food and energy items—eased to 4.2 percent from 4.4 percent.
Even with higher interest rates, the peso’s decline accelerated after government data showed July imports jumped 59.7 percent, blowing out the trade deficit to roughly $6 billion.

Widening imbalances and elevated commodity prices are expected to keep the BSP cautious, with MUFG saying persistent inflation, a wider external deficit, and peso weakness could prompt further rate hikes, but at a slower pace.

Meanwhile, economic growth has been experiencing a prolonged slump amid governance issues tied to “ghost” flood control projects. Philippine gross domestic product (GDP) growth averaged 2.6 percent in the first half, dragged by the post-pandemic low of 2.3 percent in the second quarter.

Looking ahead, MUFG forecasts the peso to recover to ₱61.75 per dollar this quarter, strengthen to ₱61.50 in the fourth quarter, reach ₱61 in the first quarter of 2027, and move into the mid-₱60 range by the second quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Ailing Djokovic 'despised' every moment of US Open defeat
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic has exited in the first round of a Grand Slam for the first time in over two decades. Could time– or an unknown health condition be catching up with the Serbian tennis legend?

image.caption: Novak Djokovic was in obvious discomfort for much of his match against Mariano NavoneImage: John Angelillo/UPI Photo/Newscom/picture alliance

blocks.text: Former world No.1 Novak Djokovic's US Open has ended with this earliest Grand Slam exit in two decades – as he fell to Mariano Navone 7-6 (7/5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 on Sunday.
The defeat scuppered the Serbian tennis legend's latest bid for a 25th Grand Slam title – and ended a streak of 78 Grand Slam first-round victories, which began at the 2006 French Open.
Considering the obvious discomfort the 39-year-old Djokovic began feeling early in the match, it was truly impressive that he managed to take Navone, 25, the distance.
After battling through more than four and a half hours in the Arthur Ashe Arena, Djokovic gracefully congratulated his opponent.
"I don't want to take too much out of his win. Congrats to him. He's a nice guy, a fighter," Djokovic said of the 25-year-old Argentine, currently 48th in the men's rankings.
"It's unbelievable," Navone said after triumphing in his first meeting with his childhood idol.
"It was a tough match, a battle. Playing against Novak the first time in the biggest stage we have in the world of tennis right now… I mean, it's crazy."
I 'despised' every minute
Throughout most of the match, Djokovic looked physically spent, repeatedly throwing up into a courtside bucket and regularly doubling over in pain.
Unsurprisingly, Djokovic said he had "despised" every moment of the ordeal at Flushing Meadows.
"I think it was obvious that it was an awful feeling on the court for me," he said.
"It's something that I've been carrying, unfortunately, pretty much every match this year. You know, vomiting, throwing up, a serious issue there.
"Then my whole body, you know, starts to collapse, basically cramping and pain. Yeah, the back just gave up in the end and shoulder, and I couldn't close it out?"
Long-term 'health issue'

Following his last tournament, in Cincinnati two weeks ago, where Djokovic threw up into a towel, first revealed that he had been struggling with a "health issue" that affects him in hot, humid conditions for "many years."

Despite the unspecified medical condition, he says he has been suffering from; Djokovic reached the final of the Australian Open in January and the semifinals of Wimbledon in June. However, he said following his exit in New York that he's now simply not physically capable of going deep into tournaments.
This mystery ailment, coupled with his age, will have many asking whether Djokovic, who remarkably still sits at No. 5 in the men's rankings, could be approaching the end.
Perhaps more alarming than the ailment itself is the fact that he simply doesn't know how to correct the problem. Still, he appears determined to battle on – at least for now.
"Can the issue be fixed? I don't know," he said.
"I'm trying, man. I'm trying. Let's see."

articles.title: Filipino trio opens Nomura Cup campaign in China
articles.summary: A Philippine squad armed to the veritable teeth plunges into action in the 31st Nomura Cup on Sept. 1, having the confidence to go up against some of the best countries in the world as it tries to…

blocks.text: A Philippine squad armed to the veritable teeth plunges into action in the 31st Nomura Cup on Sept. 1, having the confidence to go up against some of the best countries in the world as it tries to win the prestigious event for the first time at Bayhood No. 9 International Golf Club in China.

Three of the best amateurs in the land, two of them recent winners of national titles and the third the runner-up on both events, are upbeat heading into the first round of what is also known as the Asia-Pacific Amateur Team championship over a course the Filipinos on Monday described as "challenging but fair."

"The course is pretty challenging, but it will be a fun one," Shinichi Suzuki, who won the PH Match Play championship two weeks ago, said after the team's official practice round. "I like our chances this week because anyone (on the team) can play well on this course.
"We just have to give it our best and let God do His will."

The Philippines will be coming off a forgettable hosting of the event a few years back, finishing out of the top 10 at the Masters of Manila Southwoods in 2022 before Vietnam bucked the odds with a trio that ruled the event on home soil.
But with this trio that also counts Strokeplay champion Jet Hernandez and Rolando Bregente, this Philippine squad certainly looks formidable on paper.

"I think if we commit to our targets and (be able to) fire at the right spots, we'll be fine," the 21-year-old Hernandez said as he fulfills another tour of duty with the national squad before returning to the United States later in the week. "The greens are a little tricky. But we will get used to it as the week goes on."

Vietnam is the defending champion, surprising the talented field at Vinpearl Golf Haiphong. But the Vietnamese will be with just one of the three players that gave their country its first Nomura Cup, as Ho Anh Huy breaks in a duo that takes over from Nguyen Anh Minh and Le Khanh Hung, who both have collegiate commitments in the United States.

"We have a pretty good chance because the course is tough and I have good teammates," the 24-year-old Bregente said with a slight laugh. "But seriously, it's us against the course and it's a formidable challenger. But we like our chances."

articles.title: House leaders: Time for Poa to shed light on DepEd's confidential fund spending
articles.summary: “Now that we are before an impeachment court, this is the proper forum for him [Poa] to shed light on this,” House Deputy Speaker Paolo Ortega V of La Union said.

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 5:31pm
Lawyer Michael Poa cannot claim ignorance on how the Department of Education's confidential funds were spent during Vice President Sara Duterte's time as Education chief, House leaders said Monday.
Poa, a member of Duterte's defense team at her impeachment trial at the Senate, was an undersecretary at DepEd as well as the department's spokesperson at the time.

“He’s a central figure here,” House Deputy Speaker Paolo Ortega V of La Union said in an online press conference on Monday, ahead of Poa’s scheduled testimony as a hostile witness for the prosecution before the Senate impeachment court on September 1, Tuesday.

Poa told lawmakers during the 2024 House good government and public accountability panel inquiry that he asked then-DepEd Undersecretary Nolasco Mempin to issue military certifications to justify DepEd’s use of its confidential funds for a Youth Leadership Seminar.

Mempin, however, said in the same inquiry that while he and other members of his team indeed issued certifications to Poa, they did not know that these would be used for the liquidation of the DepEd’s confidential funds.
“Now that we are before an impeachment court, this is the proper forum for him [Poa] to shed light on this,” Ortega said.
“Ngayon nasa impeachment court tayo and I believe na ito po ’yung proper forum para po mabigyang-linaw ’yung mga tanong [I believe this is the proper forum to clarify the questionable issues].”
House good government and public accountability vice chairperson Benny Abante of Manila, for his part, said that Poa is an accountable official just like the Vice President.
“Atty. Poa has accountability here. He cannot wash his hands off the disposal of confidential funds,” he said.

In a statement on his upcoming testimony, Poa said, "I welcome the opportunity to testify on the extent of my participation in the subject matter, and perhaps even shed some light on what really transpired during those CGGPA hearings conducted by the House of Representatives."

The House prosecution panel is still presenting evidence on Article 1 of its impeachment case against the Vice President alleging misuse, misappropriation and irregular liquidation of confidential funds, including P112.5 million from DepEd. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: UP Diliman student council calls for academic leniency amid bad weather
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The University of the Philippines Diliman University Student Council has called for academic leniency as students continue to face difficulties brought about by inclement…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The University of the Philippines Diliman University Student Council has called for academic leniency as students continue to face difficulties brought about by inclement weather.

In a letter addressed to the Office of the Chancellor and the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs, the council said many students, particularly those from outside Metro Manila, are experiencing difficulties returning to campus due to flooding and unsafe travel conditions.

“Students from flood-prone areas and affected provinces may remain stranded and unable to report to classes as regular university operations resume. These circumstances may also make it difficult for students to finish or focus on their academic requirements,” it said.

The council called on faculty members and academic units to consider extending deadlines for academic requirements affected by weather-related class suspensions and disruptions, giving students reasonable additional time to complete them.
It also urged faculty members and academic units to excuse students who are unable to attend classes or participate in academic activities due to the weather.

The council said students affected by unsafe travel conditions, transportation disruptions, connectivity issues and other weather-related circumstances should not be penalized for their absences, with appropriate alternative arrangements provided when necessary.

“The USC emphasizes that the resumption of classes does not immediately resolve the difficulties experienced by students affected by the recent weather disturbances,” it said, calling for reasonable consideration and flexibility for students affected by circumstances beyond their control. /mcm

articles.title: San Beda out to defend NCAA crown
articles.summary: Despite losing several of its key players, reigning champion San Beda University remains unfazed ahead of its title defense in the NCAA Season 102 men’s basketball tournament which fires off Sunday,…

blocks.text: Despite losing several of its key players, reigning champion San Beda University remains unfazed ahead of its title defense in the NCAA Season 102 men’s basketball tournament which fires off Sunday, Sept. 13, at Mall of Asia Arena in Pasay City.

Still under the guidance of head coach Yuri Escueta, the Red Lions welcome seven new players who will try to fill the void with the departures of Yukien Andrada, Bryan Sajonia, Nygel Gonzales, Joe Celzo, and Agjanti Miller.

“Together with holdovers and new players namin, hopefully, they can step up and ma-fill ‘yong void dahil sa mga nawalang key players namin from last season,” said Escueta during this season’s press conference Monday, Aug. 31.
“We are expecting a tough challenge. It’s hard to go back-to-back if you lose key players for different reasons… of course, ganun pa rin ‘yong goal namin, to win the championship again,” he added.

Andrada, Sajonia, and Celzo jumped to the professional ranks in the PBA, while Gonzales suffered a season-ending ACL injury. Miller, on the other hand, has decided to transfer from San Beda to De La Salle University which was reminiscent of what Jacob Cortez did in Season 99.
Escueta admitted that the Red Lions expect a tougher climb this season.

“Just like last year, we’re going to take it one game at a time, and will focus lang muna on ourselves,” Escueta continued. “Tignan natin kung papaano maglalaro ‘tong mga holdovers natin pati mga bago. We’ll try our best na ‘yon nga, ma-defend ‘tong title.”
Jomel Puno is fulfilling his promise of playing his final year as he spearheads San Beda, which is bracketed in Group A alongside Benilde, Jose Rizal University, Lyceum, and Mapua.
Group B, meanwhile, is composed of Arellano, Emilio Aguinaldo College, San Sebastian, Perpetual, and last year’s bridesmaid Letran.
The grand old league uses the same format from last edition with the top three teams per group advancing to the quarterfinals and the remaining teams relegated to play-in games.

All basketball games for this year’s edition will air live and free on Cignal platforms via the ONE Sports Youtube Channel and the CignalPlay app. Select games will also air on Mondays and Thursdays on the RPTV Channel. A dedicated channel to NCAA Content will also be launched in NCAA NXT channel 264 HD on Cignal prior to the opening.

articles.title: Ortonio: OVP used P88M confi funds for safehouses, incentives, travelling
articles.summary: The office of Vice President Sara Duterte spent P48 million of its confidential funds in 130 days for rental of safe houses and P40 million for incentives and travelling expenses, OVP Assistant…

blocks.text: The office of Vice President Sara Duterte spent P48 million of its confidential funds in 130 days for rental of safe houses and P40 million for incentives and travelling expenses, OVP Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio said.

Ortonio made the confirmation during the direct examination of private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia who confronted Ortonio with accomplishment reports that the OVP submitted to state auditors on how the former spent its confidential funds.
He said this was how the P48 million for rental of safe houses was spent:

items: P16 million from December 21 to December 31, 2022 (11 days)
P16 million from February 6 to March 29, 2023 (52 days)
P16 million from April 25 to June 30, 2023 (67 days)

blocks.text: Divinagracia also asked Ortonio to confirm if the P16 million was a constant amount regardless of the days covered, to which Ortonio replied, “Yes, based on the report.”
Aside from P48 million in rental of safe houses, Ortonio also confirmed the OVP spent P40 million of its confidential fund for incentives and travelling expenses, broken down to the following:

items: P10 million within 11 days covering 132 areas in December 2022
P10 million within 52 days covering 127 areas from February to March 2023
P10 million within 67 days covering 111 areas from April to June 2023
P10 million within 79 days covering 122 areas from July to September 2023

blocks.text: These prompted Divinagracia to ask if the amount was P10 million regardless of the number of areas covered, to which Ortonio replied, “Yes, based on the document.”
“The amount did not change,” he added.

Ortonio also said the last tranche of the P10 million spent during the third quarter of 2023 has been labeled transportation expenses by the OVP since the Commission on Audit (COA) already informed the OVP that the prior P30 million worth of confidential fund disbursements used for incentives and travelling expenses are not allowed under the 2015 Joint Circular governing the use of confidential funds.

Asked by Divinagracia if he was able to encounter contracts involving van rentals and trucking services since these were the answers provided by the OVP to state auditors to justify the incentives and travelling expenses, Ortonio said “I do not have any document.”
Zero receipts
The expenses are on top of the P122 million in confidential funds paid to informants supposedly to buy food and medicines, which has been flagged by Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo.

Under the 2015 Joint Circular governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds, confidential funds should only be disbursed by the head of agency or the special disbursing officer to the final recipient.

The OVP’s then special disbursing officer (SDO) Gina Acosta, however, testified that she disbursed OVP’s P500 million worth of confidential funds to OVP Security Officer Colonel Dante Lachica, who did another set of disbursements to end users who are the informants and agents.

OVP officials Acosta and Ortonio testified that Lachica submitted acknowledgment receipts in liquidating its P500 million confidential fund expenses, including those with unusual and funny names, and that these purchases did not have official receipts or disbursement vouchers.

“The explanation that was provided to me [by Lachica] was that binigay po ang pera directly doon sa mga informants and agents and the informants and agents na po ;yung bumili ng mga medical and food supplies. So, it's the acknowledgement receipt which is the proof of the release of the funds to the informants or the agents,” Ortonio said when asked by Divinagracia on official receipts.
“Wala po silang nabigay na (They did not give) official receipts, Ma'am, but there were acknowledgement receipts, Ma'am, that were provided,” Ortonio added.

Further, Divinagracia underscored that Ortonio was the one responding to at least four of the state auditors’ queries on how OVP is disbursing its confidential fund even if he has maintained that he does not have personal knowledge of how the confidential fund is being spent.
Divingracia was referring to audit observation memorandum (AOM) that the COA issued to the OVP dated October 19, 2023, November 30, 2023, April 19, 2024, and August 27, 2024.

Ortonio confirmed that these letters were addressed to Acosta and OVP’s resident accountant Julieta Villadelrey, but he was the one who answered these AOMs since it is “usually either the Assistant Chief of Staff or the Chief of Staff who responds on behalf of the agency” for such AOMs.
“Regardless kung may kaalaman, ang chief of staff at assistant chief of staff, ‘yan ang sinasabi mo?” Divinagracia asked.
Ortonio then said, “As representative of the organization, ma'am.”
In addition, Ortonio said that he did not read the protective intelligence operations reports submitted to him by Lachica concerning the use of OVP’s confidential funds.
“As the liaison, I am the designated liaison officer for the confidential funds, Ma'am. And yes, I submitted documents in a sealed envelope,” he said.
“Unfortunately, Ma'am, I was not able to read the reports, ma'am, because these are sealed already, ma'am. I submitted the documents only, ma'am, to the COA,” he added.
Senator Judge Raffy Tulfo earlier said that Ortonio, the third-highest-ranking official of the OVP, supposedly not knowing how the confidential fund was disbursed, defies logic. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: China is concealing scale of flood disaster, say Tibet campaigners
articles.summary:
Rights group claims 300 homes were destroyed in Tibet and number of missing people is ‘far higher’ than Beijing admits

A Tibetan advocacy group says hundreds of homes were destroyed on the…

blocks.text: A Tibetan advocacy group says hundreds of homes were destroyed on the Tibetan side of the border in last week’s deadly floods, raising questions about Beijing’s official account of the scale of the disaster.

Public discussion about the flash floods has been restricted, with security officials in Tibet announcing on Sunday that it had penalised at least 10 people for sharing “false disaster information”. There was no further information on the nature of the penalties.

Chinese authorities say 16 people have been confirmed dead and 546 are missing, including 261 foreign citizens. But the International Campaign for Tibet says its sources believe the number of casualties is significantly higher, with at least 300 homes destroyed.

Tencho Gyatso, the president of the campaign group, told the Guardian: “What is visible in Nepal exposes what is being concealed in Tibet. Four villages – Sale, Serchung, Labi and Rizi – were among the hardest hit, with approximately 300 homes reportedly destroyed and many people still missing.”
She said the “little information that we can gather from the ground” suggested the numbers affected were “far higher” than Chinese officials had reported.

On 26 August, the collapse of a glacier triggered deadly floods along the Nepal-Tibet border, destroying entire villages. The death toll on the Nepal side has passed 900, with more than 4,000 missing. Tourists from India, the US, Britain, Australia and Canada among others remain unaccounted for in the mountainous region that is popular with trekkers and pilgrims.

Advocacy groups say there has been a stark contrast in the amount of information presented on either side of the border. Chinese coverage has been dominated by official state media reports, with few unofficial accounts about the scale of the disaster and its aftermath.

blocks.caption: Nepali soldiers retrieve bodies of people swept away by the flash floods and a mudslide on the Narayani River. Photograph: Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters

blocks.text: Independent verification is extremely difficult in Tibet, where foreign journalists face severe restrictions. Tibetans can face imprisonment for sharing information with journalists and advocacy groups outside China.
Gyatso said: “Officially released glimpses, however important, cannot tell us what is happening across all affected communities.”

Her Tibetan advocacy group said several sources reported that survivors had been moved to Gyirong, which is about 30km (18 miles) from the border crossing that was hit by the flooding. They are said to be under strict management and restricted from communicating freely.

According to a report posted on 27 August on the Tibet Daily, a state-run newspaper, two Tibetans were detained for questioning for posting “rumours” that more than 1,000 people had been swept away close to the border.

Gyatso said: “The Chinese government portrays it like it’s only happening in Nepal and there’s nothing across the border. For any type of crisis, the way China handles it is that there is no crisis. The party is in control.”
Posts relating to the disaster continued to trend on Chinese social media on Monday, with many comments echoing official narratives and supporting rescue efforts.

A Weibo post by Hu Xijin – a prominent Chinese commentator and former chief editor of the state-run Global Times – attracted more than 300 comments and thousands of likes. He accused a small number of voices of seeking to “stir controversy by fabricating baseless claims”.
However, one comment under his post questioned why all the updates were coming from the Nepali side of the border.

blocks.caption: Rescuers use sniffer dogs to search for mudslide victims in Gyirong in Tibet. Photograph: Jigme Dorje/Xinhua/AP

blocks.text: On Sunday, Tibetan public security officials said they had penalised people for sharing misleading information or “disrupting online order” with posts about the disaster.

In one case, a user identified only as Zhang disputed the official death toll, posting: “Clearly thousands of people were swept away, yet the authorities reported only three deaths and 265 people missing.”
Another user named Zhou said: “In this wave of mudslides, one entire village was wiped out. It was definitely more than a thousand [deaths].”
Maya Wang of Human Rights Watch said: “The instinct of the Chinese government is always to kind of control and to ensure the narrative which is to portray itself as a very efficient government.
“There have been questions raised over how the development of the valleys in an ecologically fragile and geologically fragile area may have related to this disaster.”

Human rights groups say that Beijing maintains tight controls over movement, religion and information in Tibet. Tibetan groups in exile have long been critical of large-scale development in the region, which they consider geologically fragile.
A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said ⁠on Monday that the ⁠release of ⁠information about the floods and mudslide near its ⁠border with Nepal was transparent and timely.

“Malicious smear campaigns ‌and hype using the disaster situation does not align with popular sentiment,” said Guo Jiakun, ‌in response to allegations that China censored videos of the disaster and understated the number of missing people.
When asked about allegations ‌that China ignored warnings from scientists over hydropower construction, he said: “We ⁠firmly oppose such baseless and malicious speculation.”
Additional reporting by Yu-chen Li in Taipei

articles.title: Palace on flood control probe: Let the Ombudsman do its job
articles.summary: Malacañang on Monday said the public should just let the Office of the Ombudsman continue its investigation into the anomalous flood control projects and not rush things, as demanded by many, as…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 5:18pm

Malacañang on Monday said the public should just let the Office of the Ombudsman continue its investigation into the anomalous flood control projects and not rush things, as demanded by many, as parts of the country suffer from severe flooding due to persistent rains.

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said the Office of the Ombudsman is an independent constitutional body and has its own mandate, separate from the executive, legislative, and judicial branches of the government.

“Nadidinig naman po natin ang mga report, mga salita, ang mga mensahe ni Ombudsman Boying Remulla, kung paano sila nagtatrabaho at paano nila inaaral ang mga naipasa na mga dokumento sa kanilang opisina,” she said in a video statement.
(We’re seeing the reports and the statements of Ombudsman Boying Remulla, how they work and how they study the documents that have been submitted to their office.)
“Batid natin ang hirap na mag-aral ng gabundok na mga files, at random naman din natin na nais din nilang mapabilis lahat ang mga kasong ini-imbestigahan,” she added.
(We understand the difficulty of studying numerous files, and we know that they also want to expedite all the cases being investigated.)
Castro, however, explained it would not be wise to rush the investigation as it may lead to cases getting dismissed due to lack of evidence.

“Mahirap madaliin ang kaso tapos hilaw. Sisihin sila kapag na-dismiss ang kaso dahil kulang sa ebidensya. So, hayaan po natin magtrabaho ang Ombudsman dahil alam po nila ang kanilang responsibilidad,” she said.

(It’s difficult to rush cases that are still raw. The Ombudsman will be blamed if the cases are dismissed because of lack of evidence. So, let’s just let the Ombudsman work because they know what their responsibility is.)
Nevertheless, she maintained that the Ombudsman’s flood control investigation is in accordance with the law. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Mendoza vows to fix ‘unpredictable’ tax rules for local businesses
articles.summary: The head of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) vowed to streamline tax enforcement and eliminate regulatory uncertainty for businesses, framing predictable rules as crucial to improving the…

blocks.text: The head of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) vowed to streamline tax enforcement and eliminate regulatory uncertainty for businesses, framing predictable rules as crucial to improving the Philippines’ overall investment climate.

Speaking at the European Chamber of Commerce of the Philippines Tax Forum, BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza outlined a reform strategy built around fairness, simplicity, predictability, and partnership. The effort will be anchored by the tax agency’s reform framework, known as the BIR DARES agenda.

Mendoza stressed that inconsistent rules pose a far greater challenge to private enterprise than strict regulations, noting that unpredictable administrative processes create friction for companies operating in the country.
The tax chief said the bureau aims to refine audit procedures, reduce bureaucratic discretion, and focus enforcement specifically on genuine compliance risks rather than routine operations.

Digital transformation will play a central role in the overhaul, according to the commissioner. The BIR plans to automate core services to trim processing times, cut unnecessary paperwork, and increase transparency across taxpayer transactions.

Beyond internal upgrades, Mendoza emphasized the need for sustained collaboration with the private sector. Engaging with businesses, he said, allows regulators to identify operational bottlenecks and overlapping requirements that may not be apparent to public officials. Tax certainty and regulatory consistency remain central to maintaining foreign and local investor confidence.

The conference brought together senior corporate executives, tax specialists, and government officials to navigate regulatory shifts, digital compliance, and dispute resolution. Presenting alongside Mendoza were key BIR executives, including Deputy Commissioners Larry M. Barcelo and Marissa O. Cabreros, Assistant Commissioners Raquel Cristina V. Baltazar and Mariza R. Uy, and Collection Programs Division Chief Glenn Alde.
Discussions centered on policy changes impacting commercial operations, including preliminary implementation steps for the Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax under global minimum tax standards.

articles.title: Davison delivers 30-point effort, lifts High Speed Hitters past Thais
articles.summary: Games Tuesday 1:30 p.m. – PLDT vs Nxled 4 p.m. – Farm Fresh vs EST Cola 6:30 p.m. – Creamline vs Ho Chi Minh Savi Davison fired 30 points to spearhead PLDT’s title-retention bid in the PVL…

blocks.text: Games Tuesday
1:30 p.m. – PLDT vs Nxled
4 p.m. – Farm Fresh vs EST Cola
6:30 p.m. – Creamline vs Ho Chi Minh

Savi Davison fired 30 points to spearhead PLDT’s title-retention bid in the PVL Invitational, as the High Speed Hitters shook off a third-set stumble with a decisive fourth-set surge to defeat EST Cola of Thailand, 25-23, 25-15, 26-28, 25-14, Monday, Aug. 31, at the Araneta Coliseum.

For all her brilliance, the Fil-Canadian admitted the defending champions came into the weeklong tournament virtually unprepared. But when the opening serve was fired, PLDT showed it had enough firepower – and adaptability – to rise to the challenge.

“I think we were unprepared coming into this game, but we knew we needed to adapt. Thailand is always gonna be a strong force in volleyball, so I’m pretty glad that we were able to kind of fire from every angle and get it done in four sets,” said Davison.
And fire from every angle they did.

The high-leaping ace was relentless from the opening set, powering PLDT’s attack while making her presence felt at the net with five blocks. She also came through with several crucial digs, repeatedly keeping rallies alive and giving the High Speed Hitters opportunities to turn defense into points.
Davison found a perfect partner in the middle in Mika Reyes, who added six blocks for 16 points, as the two combined to give PLDT a formidable presence at the net.
Their chemistry proved particularly crucial in the fourth set.

After Reyes broke a 12-all count with a quick attack, Davison turned an out-of-system play into a crucial point before adding two more to push PLDT ahead, 16-12. Reyes followed with another hit, while Davison preserved a spectacular one-handed save by Kath Arado that eventually led to another point as the High Speed Hitters pulled away, 20-13.
From there, PLDT shifted into cruise control.

EST Cola, already forced to dig deep after skipper and top scorer Aekpatchaya Kantima went down with an ankle injury in Set 2, could not summon another comeback. The Thais had stunned PLDT by taking the third set, 28-26, after saving a match point and surviving a nerve-racking extension, but the High Speed Hitters quickly slammed the door shut in the fourth.

EST Cola’s third-set escape briefly raised the prospect of a long, bruising battle. Instead, PLDT regained its composure and finished the match in one hour and 47 minutes – avoiding the physical toll of a five-setter with both teams facing another game Tuesday.

Jovie Prado, Kim Dy and Majoy Baron provided ample support with nine, eight and seven points, respectively, underscoring the depth that carried PLDT to a breakthrough two-title campaign last year, including its triumph in the PVL On Tour.
Arado finished with 26 excellent digs and 12 receptions, while Prado also shone in defense with 21 digs and 13 receptions.

For EST Cola, the loss did little to diminish its impressive showing against the defending champions. The Thais showed enough grit and resilience to threaten PLDT even after losing Hantima, fighting back to steal the third set and keeping the fourth close before the High Speed Hitters finally pulled away.

Nirarach Srikuta led the Thai side with 14 points, including the clutch hits that kept EST Cola alive in the third, while Nannaphat Moonjakham added 12. Hantima finished with eight points before her injury, while Papatchaya Phontham and Supawadee Panwilai chipped in six apiece.
PLDT now turns its attention to Nxled at 1:30 p.m. Tuesday, while EST Cola seeks to bounce back against Farm Fresh at 4 p.m.
In a compressed tournament where every victory – and every ounce of energy – can prove decisive, the High Speed Hitters got the result they wanted without having to go the distance.

PLDT dominated EST Cola across the board, outscoring the Thai squad in attacks (60-42) and blocks (14-11) with setter Kim Fajardo finishing with 29 excellent sets, eight more than counterpart Natnicha Saelao. The High Speed Hitters also targeted EST Cola’s shaky reception to fire off six service aces while giving up just two, further capitalizing with 25 points off opponent errors compared to the 21 they conceded.

EST Cola squandered a pair of four-point leads in Set 3, but the Thais refused to fold. From 15-17 down, they clawed their way back behind crisp, efficient hitting and near-stifling defense, then showed remarkable poise and nerve in a bone-crunching endgame to foil PLDT’s sweep bid and force another set.

The Thais appeared headed for another collapse when they trailed, 21-23, but PLDT handed them a lifeline with back-to-back miscues – a service error and a net violation – that allowed EST Cola to draw level. What followed was a gripping extension filled with thunderous attacks, desperate digs and spectacular saves, with both teams repeatedly staring down the possibility of defeat.
EST Cola saved a match point, only to squander two set points of its own. After PLDT forced another tie at 26 on an EST Cola service error, the Thais finally seized the moment.

Srikuta uncorked a difficult down-the-line winner to cap a heart-stopping rally that featured a furious exchange of power hits and remarkable defensive plays. She then followed it with a perfectly placed ace, sending the EST Cola bench into wild celebration and leaving the PLDT side stunned.
From the brink of a sweep, the Thais had suddenly breathed life into the match, turning a seemingly one-sided affair into a potential comeback battle.
But the High Speed Hitters slammed the door shut, snuffing out any hopes of a full-blown resurgence with a decisive run midway in the fourth.

PLDT and EST Cola traded blows early in the opening set before the High Speed Hitters established control at the net, anchored by Reyes and Baron with explosive support from Davison and Dy. Arado and Prado also kept the play clean, allowing PLDT to capitalize on the Thais' offensive errors and surge to a commanding 23-17 lead.

Refusing to fold, EST Cola mounted a furious late-game rally from the brink of defeat at 19-24. Ignited by a Hantima spike, the Thais saved four consecutive set points. They stuffed Dy’s set-clinching bid, seized on a Davison error, and scored on a Moonjakham thunderbolt to cap a heart-stopping rally of digs and blocks, trimming the deficit to 23-24.
The thrilling comeback ended in anti-climactic heartbreak, however, as Hantima sent her next serve long, handing PLDT the breathless first-set victory.
