articles.title: Filipinos spent so much on streaming, apps that taxes hit ₱17 billion—BIR
articles.summary: Tax collections from foreign digital service providers reached ₱17.5 billion in the first six months of the year, driven by higher consumer adoption and improved compliance among global technology…

blocks.text: Charlito Martin R. Mendoza

Tax collections from foreign digital service providers reached ₱17.5 billion in the first six months of the year, driven by higher consumer adoption and improved compliance among global technology platforms.

Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza told the Manila Bulletin that revenues collected by the government’s main tax agency from non-resident digital service providers (DSPs) have seen “encouraging” growth on the back of robust compliance.

Collections from foreign DSPs surged more than threefold during the first semester compared to the ₱6.6 billion logged in the initial six months of the value-added tax (VAT) on digital services program.
The government began collecting the 12-percent consumption levy on DSPs in June 2025, covering both business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) transactions.
It bears noting that the first-half collection already accounts for three-fourths of the national government’s full-year target of ₱23.1 billion.
Mendoza said the overwhelming expansion in collections from this segment is an “encouraging sign that implementation is gaining traction.”

Between B2B and B2C, Mendoza noted that the latter emerged as the “slightly bigger” contributor, though B2B transactions still made a substantial showing. “This means the growth is broad-based and reflects increasing digital activity from both individual consumers and businesses,” Mendoza said.
Major global platforms registered with the BIR include Meta, Google Asia, Netflix, Disney, Canva, Spotify, LinkedIn, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Valve.
While substantial, Mendoza noted that the expansion in tax haul was an anticipated development “as compliance improves and more digital transactions are properly captured.”

For the BIR, this trend implies that the digital VAT law is proving effective. “It is helping level the playing field between local and foreign digital service providers, improving tax compliance, and ensuring that the growing digital economy contributes its fair share to government revenues and, ultimately, to public services for our people,” Mendoza said.

However, the BIR chief believes it is still “too early” to make a definitive projection for the full year, responding to a query on whether the medium-term program necessitates upward revisions due to the robust first-half haul.
Mendoza also demurred on betting whether the first-semester figure would double by year-end to reach roughly ₱35 billion.
He explained that fourth-quarter collections are due in January 2027, deferring the complete tally of the current fiscal year's returns.

Of the government's tax reform measures, only the VAT on digital services brought in additional revenues. Meanwhile, the Capital Markets Efficiency Promotion Act (CMEPA) and the CREATE MORE Act reduced revenues by ₱2.3 billion and ₱342 million, respectively.

Revenue losses from CMEPA are expected to more than double to ₱4.9 billion in 2026, before dropping by 5.5 percent to ₱4.6 billion in 2027. Incurred losses from lowering corporate income taxes (CIT) under the CREATE MORE Act are projected to nearly triple to ₱981 million this year and swell further by 68.2 percent to ₱1.7 billion next year.

VAT collections from digital services form part of the BIR's overall tax collection, which stood at ₱1.63 trillion, boosted by higher returns from corporate income tax, personal income tax, VAT, other percentage taxes, and miscellaneous taxes.
More recently, the BIR collected ₱1.99 trillion—up 5.3 percent from a year earlier—as improved taxpayer services helped strengthen compliance and boost receipts.

articles.title: Tommy Koh, Runa Khan, Bo Kyi win 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Singaporean diplomat and academic Tommy Koh, Bangladeshi social entrepreneur Runa Khan, and Myanmar human rights activist Bo Kyi are the recipients of the 68th Ramon Magsaysay…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Singaporean diplomat and academic Tommy Koh, Bangladeshi social entrepreneur Runa Khan, and Myanmar human rights activist Bo Kyi are the recipients of the 68th Ramon Magsaysay Awards, Asia’s premier prize and highest honor.
They were recognized for their remarkable contributions to Asia at a ceremony on Monday.
The ceremony coincided with the 119th birth anniversary of Ramon Magsaysay, the Philippines’ seventh president, whose legacy the awards honor.

Koh, a law professor at the National University of Singapore, was recognized for his leadership in international diplomacy and his efforts to mentor a new generation of advocates for justice and human dignity worldwide.
In 1978, he chaired a pivotal negotiating committee of the Third United Nations Conference on the Law of the Sea.
As president of the conference in 1982, he led more than 150 countries to adopt the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (Unclos).
The Unclos is the international treaty that provides the overarching legal framework for ocean spaces, maritime activities, and resources.
Khan, a founder of the grassroots development organization Friendship, was honored for her deep compassion for Bangladesh’s poorest communities.
For over two decades, Khan has led Friendship in broadening its efforts in healthcare, education, climate adaptation, livelihoods, disaster preparedness, and inclusive citizenship.
Kyi, a former political prisoner, was recognized for his lifelong commitment to truth, accountability, and justice, through his work on issues related to human rights in Myanmar.

He also co-founded the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an organization that documents political arrests and detentions while providing support to political detainees and their families.

blocks.caption: Singapore’s Tommy Koh, Bangladesh’s Runa Khan, and Myanmar’s Bo Kyi are the recipients of the 68th Ramon Magsaysay Awards, considered Asia’s most premier prize and highest honor. (Photo by Andrea Gregorio)

blocks.text: “Through their examples, we see that the leadership values embodied by President Ramon Magsaysay remain as urgent and vital today as ever, especially in a world where the need for principles action and moral clarity has never been greater,” said Ramon Magsaysay Awards Foundation (RMAF) chairman Edgar Chua.
This year’s theme is “A World for All,” a call to build an inclusive future where dignity is upheld and everyone can thrive.

“At a time when the world continues to confront uncertainty, division, and increasingly complex challenges, this year’s theme, A World for All, invites us to reflect on the kind of world we want to build together,” said RMAF president Susanna Afan.
The 2026 Ramon Magsaysay awardees will receive a medallion featuring President Ramon Magsaysay’s likeness, a citation certificate, and a cash prize. /dl

articles.title: Marcos’ contributions merit honorary PLM law degree, says Palace
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Palace press officer Claire Castro on Monday pushed back against critics of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s honorary Doctor of Laws degree from Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Palace press officer Claire Castro on Monday pushed back against critics of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s honorary Doctor of Laws degree from Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM), saying he deserved the recognition for his contributions to the country.

The statement came after the conferment drew flak from students, professors, and Kabataan Party-list Representative Renee Co. The lawmaker called the recognition inappropriate amid allegations of corruption involving the Marcos administration and the President’s family.

“Ang mga tumutuligsa rito ay mga taong kung hindi man mapagmataas ay mga kumakalaban sa Pangulo, the usual obstructionists at destabilizers, o yung mga sumasakay lang sa nakikita sa social media, pero hindi nauunawaan ang totoong issue,” Castro said in a video statement.

(Those criticizing the decision are either people who are arrogant, those who oppose the President—the usual obstructionists and destabilizers—or those simply jumping on the social media bandwagon without understanding the real issue.)
Castro said the critics do not fully understand what honoris causa means and proceeded to explain why Marcos deserved the recognition.
“Ito ay isang pagkilala o parangal para sa taong mataas ang naabot na posisyon. May mga mahalagang naiambag sa komunidad o mga nagawa para sa bansa,” Castro said.
(This is a recognition or honor given to a person who has attained a distinguished position and has made significant contributions to the community or the country.)

“Huwag natin kalimutan ang pagtindig pa lamang ng ating Pangulo, Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. sa karapatan natin sa West Philippine Sea, ang pagpaputol ng 300-meter floating barrier na inilagay ng China Coast Guard sa Scarborough Shoal noong September 2023 para harangin ang ating mga mangingisda na makapasok at makapangisda sa traditional fishing lagoon ay isang gawain ng isang matapat na leader,” she also said.

(Let us not forget President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s firm stand in defending our rights in the West Philippine Sea. His decision to have the 300-meter floating barrier installed by the China Coast Guard at Scarborough Shoal cut and removed in September 2023—intended to prevent our fishermen from entering and fishing in their traditional fishing grounds—was an act befitting a principled and steadfast leader.)
Castro also cited Marcos’ respect for every human life and due process, and his efforts to prevent the abuse of power.
Additionally, she highlighted the President’s push for investigations into corruption allegations in the government and his efforts to ensure sufficient fuel supplies during the Middle East crisis.

“Pati na ang supply ng fertilizer para hindi maapektuhan ang ating mga magsasaka. Ang masagip ang isang kababayan mula sa death row, sentensyang pinataw ng ibang bansa. Pagsagip sa 17 OFW sa Qatar sa kasong illegal assembly at sa 24 Filipinos na nakadetained sa Eastern Siberia sa Russia. Ito ay nagawa ng Pangulo dahil sa maganda niyang relasyon sa leaders ng Qatar at Russia,” she said.

(This also includes ensuring the supply of fertilizer so that our farmers would not be adversely affected. The President also succeeded in saving a Filipino from the death penalty imposed by a foreign country, as well as securing the release of 17 OFWs in Qatar who were facing charges of illegal assembly and 24 Filipinos detained in Eastern Siberia, Russia. These were made possible, in part, by the President’s good relations with the leaders of Qatar and Russia.)
Castro slams Co
The Palace official said Co’s objection to Marcos’ honorary degree supposedly reflected the lawmaker’s “weakness” and alleged goal of undermining the administration.

“Yan marahil ang kanilang goal, laging maging negatibo sa administrasyon. Ngunit ang pamimintas na ito sa ginawa ng PLM sa pagbibigay ng Honoris Causa sa pinakamatas na lider na bansa ay pagpapakita lamang ni Congressman Co ng kanyang kahinaan,” the Palace official said.

(That may well be their goal—to always portray the administration in a negative light. But this criticism of PLM’s decision to confer an honorary degree, honoris causa, on the country’s highest-ranking leader only exposes Congressman Co’s own shortcomings.)

“Ang mga nabanggit ko ng mga nagawa ng Pangulo ay hindi pa marahil na gagawa ni Congressman Rene Co. Definitely, wala pa siya nasasagip na buhay mula sa isang siguradong may death penalty,” she continued.
(The accomplishments of the President that I have mentioned are things Congressman Rene Co has likely yet to achieve. Definitely, he has not yet saved a life from certain execution.)
Castro said the insults, disparaging remarks, and belittling comments made by Co only showed what the lawmaker had learned and how far that education had taken him.

“Sa aking pagkakaalam, hindi itinuturo sa law schools ang maging arugante at huwag niyang idamay ang lahat ng abugado dahil alam naming mga abugado na ang pagmamata ng kapwa, panimira ng walang basihan, ay hindi gawain ng matino at mahusay na abugado,” she said.

(As far as I know, law schools do not teach students to be arrogant. He should not drag all lawyers into this, because we lawyers know that belittling others and making baseless accusations are not the actions of a sensible and competent lawyer.)
PLM conferred on Marcos an honorary degree of Doctor of Laws, Honoris Causa, during its 58th Commencement Exercises on Aug. 27.

However, students questioned the university administration’s decision to confer the award on Marcos, saying they were not consulted. They also warned that the recognition could be seen as an endorsement of an administration facing questions over good governance.

They also cited PLM’s history, invoking the memory of Liliosa Hilao, a PLM student journalist who was the first reported student activist to die in detention during martial law under the Marcos Sr. dictatorship. /mr

articles.title: 22 Filipino seafarers return home after Black Sea missile attack
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Twenty-two Filipino seafarers arrived in Manila on Aug. 30 after being repatriated from Ukraine following a missile attack on their vessel while it was docked at Chornomorsk…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Twenty-two Filipino seafarers arrived in Manila on Aug. 30 after being repatriated from Ukraine following a missile attack on their vessel while it was docked at Chornomorsk Port in the Black Sea region.
The crew was aboard the Liberia-flagged bulk carrier M/V Antonia S when the vessel was hit by a missile on Aug. 19, according to the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW).

The agency said local authorities evacuated the crew to a designated shelter within Chornomorsk Port after the attack. They stayed there while arrangements were made for temporary accommodation and their return to the Philippines.

The seafarers arrived at Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3 aboard Turkish Airlines Flight TK084 and received medical assistance from the Manila International Airport Authority medical team. They were also given financial assistance through the DMW AKSYON Fund under the government’s UPLIFT initiative.

DMW Officer-in-Charge Assistant Secretary for Sea-Based OFW Concerns Augusto B. San Diego III reminded the seafarers to exercise their rights, including refusing to sail when conditions pose a serious threat to their safety.
He also asked them to remember Filipino seafarers still working in areas affected by armed conflict.

“Include in your prayers our fellow Filipino seafarers who continue to sail in areas affected by war. Above all, let us pray that the war will end and that the violence that continues to put the lives of our seafarers at risk will stop,” San Diego said.

The ship’s Filipino captain also thanked a foreign security officer aboard the vessel whose warning of the incoming attack gave the crew time to move to the upper deck and take precautionary measures before the missile struck.
The returning seafarers will undergo medical and psychological assessments arranged by their licensed manning agency.

The DMW also reminded licensed manning agencies and their accredited principals to monitor the welfare of Filipino seafarers, observe safety precautions and follow protocols for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. /mr

Organisers say world must revive its spiritual relationship with food as climate crisis and conflict disrupt food security

Mending the broken food system under the threat of climate-driven…

blocks.text: Mending the broken food system under the threat of climate-driven weather extremes will require more than economic fixes and intensive agriculture, according to the organisers of a pioneering summit this week, who say the world must revive its spiritual relationship with food.

Delegates from more than 60 countries and the UN will gather for the next five days in Paro in the tiny Himalayan nation of Bhutan for the world’s first “conscious food summit”, which will bring together governments and farmers, mindfulness experts and yoga therapists.

Tshering Tobgay, Bhutan’s prime minister, said: “Food lies at the intersection of many of the defining challenges of our time – hunger, poor nutrition, poverty, climate change, biodiversity loss, and increasingly food security is also being disrupted by conflict and geopolitical instability. Our central message is simple: transforming our food systems requires both inner and outer change.”

Conscious eating is at the heart of these talks, which will promote regenerative practices and Indigenous knowledge. “Consciousness can cultivate compassion, empathy, resilience, creativity and a stronger connection with nature,” Tobgay said in an interview with the Guardian. “This does not mean choosing spirituality over science. It means recognising that our values and mindsets influence how science, policy, finance and technology are used.”

blocks.caption: Tshering Tobgay: ‘Food systems are ultimately shaped by human choices.’ Photograph: Mike Bowers/The Guardian

blocks.text: The impacts of the climate crisis have been brought home close to Bhutan’s borders with the disaster in its near neighbour Nepal last week where a glacial collapse led to floods and landslides that killed hundreds.

This year and next as the “super El Niño” hits, the World Food Programme has warned that 50 million people could be pushed close to starvation. Food shortages and higher prices for staples are likely around the world. It follows a summer in the northern hemisphere in which harvests have been devastated by drought, intense heat and wildfires.

Jerry Spooner, of Regenerative Vanua, a Pacific NGO, said the threats would push global food systems to their limit. “As we face the growing impacts of climate change, a potential super El Niño, biodiversity loss and increasing global instability, it is becoming clear that our food systems are not resilient enough for the challenges ahead,” he said. “The opportunity in Bhutan is to move beyond discussing how we produce more food and instead focus on how we build food systems that regenerate ecosystems, strengthen communities, celebrate culture and improve our collective resilience.”

blocks.caption: Cows searching for food in a pasture in Tecoluca, El Salvador, where the lack of rainfall has reduced the availability of grass and other forage for livestock. Photograph: Marvin Recinos/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Tobgay said people must articulate the values they wanted to see reflected in the way food is produced and consumed, instead of relying on businesses and governments to shape food choices. “Food systems are ultimately shaped by human choices, institutions, incentives, relationships and values,” he said. “So we must address root causes as well as symptoms.”
Farmers and rural people were often at the mercy of markets and global forces. “Too often, policies are developed for these groups rather than with them,” Tobgay said.
after newsletter promotion

The summit will focus not on bombastic political speeches and promises but on fostering inner change, with the help of “spiritual masters” such as mindfulness practitioners. Food had become a commodity on world markets and was treated carelessly as a result, leading to waste and unhealthy eating, and those attitudes must be reversed, Tobgay said.

“Outer change is agriculture, markets, finance, public policy and consumption,” he said. “Consciousness has value only if it influences our decisions and changes how we act. For example, a conscious approach to production would care for both the land and the farmer. It would regenerate soils, not deplete them. It would protect water. It would reduce pollution and deforestation and recognise the dignity and wellbeing of the people who produce the food that sustain us.”

Tobgay begins each day at 5am with a bowl of porridge and a banana, eaten sitting by a small stream that runs near his house. “I listen to the birds that are up and about by that time, I listen to the stream and the water,” he said.

Anyone could try conscious eating, he added. Many cultures have a tradition before meals of reflecting on the food, its provenance and preparation, and giving thanks. Reviving such practices would take almost no time but could, he hopes, be one of the first steps to a revolution in the way we treat the planet and each other.

articles.title: Honorary degree given to Marcos for his contributions, Palace says
articles.summary: Malacañang has defended President Marcos for receiving honoris causa amid criticisms, saying it was given to him in recognition of his contrubutions as the higest-ranking official in the country.…

blocks.text: Malacañang has defended President Marcos for receiving honoris causa amid criticisms, saying it was given to him in recognition of his contrubutions as the higest-ranking official in the country.
Last week, Marcos received honoris causa, the highest honorary degree of the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila, when he graced the university's 58th commencement exercises.
The feat has since drawn criticism.

Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro clarified that the honorary degree is not earned through traditional academic studies, attending law school, or passing the bar examinations.

"Ang titulong honoris causa ay isang honorary degree. Ito ay isang pagkilala o parangal para sa taong mataas ang naabot na posisyon. May mga mahalagang naiambag sa komunidad o mga nagawa para sa bansa (The title honoris causa is an honorary degree. It is a form of recognition or distinction given to a person who has attained a high position, made significant contributions to the community, or accomplished something of importance for the country)," Castro said on Monday, Aug. 31.

"At hindi ito nakukuha sa pamamagitan ng tradisyonal na pag-aaral, pagpasok sa law school, o pagpasa sa bar examinations (It is not earned through traditional academic studies, attending law school, or passing the bar examinations)," Castro explained.
The Palace official stressed that perhaps many "do not fully understand the term honoris causa."
She also alleged that some of those criticizing the President for receiving the honorary degree are "obstructionists at destabilizers."

"Ang mga tumutuligsa rito ay mga taong kung hindi man mapagmataas ay mga kumakalaban sa Pangulo, the usual obstructionists at destabilizers, o yung mga sumasakay lang sa nakikita sa social media, pero hindi nauunawaan ang totoong issue (Those criticizing it are people who, if not being arrogant, are either opposed to the President, the usual obstructionists and destabilizers, or simply jumping on the bandwagon based on what they see on social media without understanding the real issue)," Castro said.
With this, the Palace spokesperson underscored the need to clarify it to prevent people from being misled.

"Mahalagang malinawan ibang kababayan natin na naloloko ng iba gamit ang fake news o ng pagiging mapagmataas lamang (It is important to clarify this for our fellow Filipinos who may be misled by others through fake news or simply because of arrogance)," Castro said.
Castro cited several actions Marcos has taken during his presidency that make him worthy of the recognition.

"Huwag natin kalimutan ang pagtindig pa lamang ng ating Pangulong, Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. sa karapatan natin sa West Philippine Sea (Let us not forget how our President, Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., has stood up for our rights in the West Philippine Sea)," Castro said.

"Ang pagpaputol ng 300-meter floating barrier na inilagay ng China Coast Guard sa Scarborough Shoal noong September 2023 para harangin ang ating mangingisda na makapasok at makapangisda sa traditional fishing lagoon ay isang gawain ng isang matapat na leader (The removal of the 300-meter floating barrier installed by the China Coast Guard at Scarborough Shoal in September 2023 to prevent our fishermen from entering and fishing in their traditional fishing lagoon was an act of a steadfast leader)," Castro added.
She also cited Marcos' move to initiate investigations into corruption allegations and his response to the fuel crisis caused by the conflict in the Middle East.
Castro further mentioned the actions taken for distressed and displaced overseas Filipino workers in Qatar and Russia.

articles.title: DA moves to stop solar projects from encroaching on farmland
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture (DA) is proposing a geofencing program to protect agricultural land from rapidly expanding solar power projects in a bid to strengthen the country’s food security.…

blocks.text: Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr.
The Department of Agriculture (DA) is proposing a geofencing program to protect agricultural land from rapidly expanding solar power projects in a bid to strengthen the country’s food security.

Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said his agency is pushing to geofence around three million hectares of flat agricultural land, particularly rice-producing areas, to prevent them from being converted into solar farms.
Geofencing creates digital geographic boundaries around priority agricultural areas, offering renewable energy (RE) developers a clear guide on where projects should not be located.

“We need energy security, but it cannot come at the cost of food security. The country must be able to keep the lights on without putting at risk the land that keeps food on Filipino tables,” Tiu Laurel said in a statement on Monday, Aug. 31.
He noted that the plan aims to identify up to 2,000 flat rice lands for geofencing, ensuring they remain dedicated to agricultural production.
The DA added that this list of priority lands will be cross-checked against existing and awarded energy projects to prevent overlaps.

Tiu Laurel said the initiative was proposed during a recent meeting with Department of Energy (DOE) Secretary Sharon Garin to address the balance between the country’s solar capacity expansion and food production.
Additionally, the DA is lobbying for a program that would allow farmers and fisherfolk to directly benefit from the ongoing RE transition through lower electricity costs.

Under this proposal, RE suppliers under the Green Energy Auction, Green Energy Option, and the Retail Competition and Open Access framework could connect directly with qualified agricultural end-users.
Potential beneficiaries include farms, fishponds, irrigation systems, post-harvest facilities, rice mills, cold storage plants, slaughterhouses, and other food production operations.
The DOE is currently examining how RE suppliers and distribution utilities can participate in the proposed initiative.

In the meantime, the DA and DOE are working to develop a farm-to-energy framework alongside the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) to explore further ways organized agricultural groups can benefit from RE.

“The framework will help proponents under the agricultural energy category lower electricity costs, generate savings, and strengthen incomes across the sector,” said Agriculture Undersecretary Roger Navarro.
The DA announced it will sign a memorandum of agreement with the DOE in October to formalize the partnership and expedite the development of the recommended programs.

“Our goal now, for both the DOE and the DA, is to ensure that both of these pressing needs of Filipinos are addressed in a way that benefits the country without sacrificing one for the other,” Tiu Laurel said.

articles.title: Palace on Habagat floods: 'No holidays for President'
articles.summary: Malacañang on Monday said that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos and concerned agencies are continuously responding to areas affected by the severe flooding due to the heavy rains brought by the…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 4:30pm

Malacañang on Monday said that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos and concerned agencies are continuously responding to areas affected by the severe flooding due to the heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat).
In a video message, Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro said that there is no holiday for the President amid the situation. August 31 is National Heroes’ Day in the Philippines.

“Minomonitor ng Pangulo ang lagay ng panahon. Sa paglakas muli ng ulan itong gabi ng Biyernes at Sabado, ang mga miyembro ng gabinete ay muling nag-update sa Pangulo at inutos ng Pangulo na dapat na lahat ng apektadong lugar at apektadong mga residente, siguraduhin hindi magugutom at kumpleto pati ang non-food kits,” she said.

(The President is monitoring the weather situation. As the rains intensified again on Friday night and Saturday, Cabinet members provided the President with updates, and he directed that all affected areas and residents be ensured of food supplies and non-food kits.)

“Sa mga ganitong klaseng sitwasyon, hindi kailangang utusan pa ng Pangulo ang mga nasabing miyembro ng gabinete dahil alam nila kung ano ang nais ng Pangulo, mabilis na aksyon. Walang holiday-holiday sa Pangulo,” she added.

(In situations like this, the President does not need to issue specific orders to the concerned Cabinet members because they already know what he wants, which is swift action. For the President, there are no holidays.)

Castro said Marcos is set to lead a response meeting in Central Luzon and Metro Manila within the day, along with officials from the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), and Department of Budget and Management (DBM) to get flood updates.

Over the weekend, the President was criticized on social media following the circulation of videos showing him singing at First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos’ birthday celebration despite the inclement weather.
Stolen equipment
Castro likewise lamented the incident where pumping station equipment was reportedly stolen in Metro Manila, which resulted in several pumping stations failing to operate amid the heavy rains.
She said the President and concerned agencies have been doing everything possible to alleviate the flooding problem in the country, but such pilfering discredits the government’s efforts.

“Dahil sa mga ninakaw na mahahalagang piyesa ng pumping stations hindi sila gagana. Gagastos tayo ulit para sa mga replacement na ito. Paano kung walang makuha agad na replacement? Hindi agad maiaayos ang mga ito na magdudulot na naman ng mabagal na paghupa ng baha,” she said.

(Due to the stolen parts of the pumping stations, they will not work. We will spend more money on these replacements. What if we do not get replacements immediately? These cannot be repaired immediately, which will cause the flood waters to slowly subside again.)
“Huwag tayo maging makasarili. Buhay, kalusugan, at ari-arian ang maaapektuhan dahil sa mga pagnanakaw na ito. Huwag ninyong isabotahe ang mga proyekto ng Pangulo. Magtulungan po tayo,” she added.
(Let’s not be selfish. Lives, health, and livelihood will be affected because of these thefts. Do not sabotage the President’s projects. Let’s help one another.)
The Palace official thus issued a stern warning against those “sabotaging” the government’s flood control projects.

“Sa lahat ng mga gumagawang pananabotahe na ito, kayo po ay hahabulin ng batas. Papanagutin po namin kayo dahil buhay at kabuhayan ang maaaring maapektuhan ng inyong mga makasariling gawain,” she emphasized.
(For all those who are sabotaging these projects, the law will run after you. We will hold you accountable because your selfish actions affect lives of people and their livelihoods.) —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Lacson: P3.7B 'wasted' on 'illegal' Taguig reclamation projects
articles.summary: The feud between Senators Panfilo Lacson and Alan Peter Cayetano over allegedly illegal reclamation projects on the Taguig side of Laguna Lake has continued, with Lacson claiming that at least P3.713…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 4:24pm

The feud between Senators Panfilo Lacson and Alan Peter Cayetano over allegedly illegal reclamation projects on the Taguig side of Laguna Lake has continued, with Lacson claiming that at least P3.713 billion in public funds has been wasted on related projects.
In a post on X, Lacson said his team would submit its latest findings on the alleged anomalous projects to the Office of the Ombudsman’s fact-finding team for appropriate action.

“Based on official records and our investigation, the total cost of identified completed, ongoing (and suspended) DPWH flood control and multi-purpose projects along the ‘illegal’ Laguna Lakeshore reclamation areas in Taguig City has so far reached P3.713 billion,” he said.

“These do not include other anomalous slope protection and flood mitigation projects along Taguig River involving double appropriations and ‘ghost’ projects using recycled photographs in different ‘completed’ projects, for billing purposes,” he added.
Lacson said four parcels of allegedly illegally reclaimed land in Taguig City were initially identified as covered by “fraudulently” issued land titles.
He said the details of the four parcels were as follows:

items: one covered by an administrative patent, involving 9,204 square meters under an Original Certificate of Title (OCT);
one covered through judicial/ordinary land registration processing, involving 5,000 square meters under an OCT;
one covered by a homestead patent, involving 181,077 square meters under a Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT); and
one involving 193,027 square meters under a TCT.

blocks.text: According to Lacson, the top five contractors involved in projects worth a combined P2.372 billion were:

items: Dahl Construction: P858.22 million covering five solo projects worth P571.5 million and four joint ventures totaling P286.7 million;
J.C. Uyecio: P483.1 million covering four joint ventures;
Toughbuilt: P434.2 million covering three solo projects;
Topnotch: P329.9 million covering two joint ventures with Core Check and one with Beam Team; and
GR Fervidal: P266.6 million covering five solo multi-purpose building projects.

blocks.text: For his part, Senate Minority Leader Cayetano appeared to downplay Lacson’s claims, saying the government could even “gain” if allegations that properties along Laguna Lake in Taguig City were illegally titled are proven true.
He referred to a newspaper report claiming that 181,000 square meters, or 18 hectares, of land had been “illegally titled.”

"Sa isang banda po, nagho-hope din kami na totoo iyon. Bakit? Kasi kung totoong ilegal iyon, sa gobyerno iyon [mapupunta]. Edi may 18 hectares tayo ngayon para sa gobyerno,” he said at an event on Sunday.
(On the one hand, we also hope that it is true. Why? Because if it is really illegal, it will go to the government. Then the government would have 18 hectares of land.)
Cayetano also welcomed the investigation into the land titles, saying his wife, Taguig City Mayor Lani Cayetano, also wanted the properties examined.
He likewise continued to deny allegations that he was involved in land grabbing, particularly those involving The Lakeshore Tent.

“Iyon ang pinapalabas na illegal reclamation at pinapalabas na kinakamkam ko rin daw po ‘yung iba para sa aking sarili. Pero ang blessing po ay marami kasing gumagamit at alam naman po na hindi amin iyon,” Cayetano said.

(That is being portrayed as illegal reclamation, and they are alleging that I also grabbed other areas for myself. But the blessing is that many people use it, and they know that it does not belong to us.)— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: DPWH, DepEd hold bulk of unused cash use despite improving gov’t spending efficiency in July
articles.summary: Government departments and special purpose funds (SPFs) slightly improved their spending efficiency by end-July 2026, but unused cash authority remained concentrated in public works and education.…

blocks.text: Government departments and special purpose funds (SPFs) slightly improved their spending efficiency by end-July 2026, but unused cash authority remained concentrated in public works and education.

The latest Department of Budget and Management (DBM) data showed that the overall utilization rate for notices of cash allocation (NCAs) stood at 94.6 percent as of end-July 2026, a 0.6-percentage-point (ppt) increase from the 94 percent recorded in July 2025.

Total NCA releases rose to ₱3.13 trillion, roughly 4.7 percent higher than the ₱2.99 trillion recorded a year ago. Of the total, ₱2.96 trillion was utilized, leaving ₱169.9 billion in unused cash authority as of end-July, down from ₱178.2 billion a year ago.

Under the government’s accounting framework, these notices act as the primary disbursement authority, allowing agencies to pay for contracted works and services. High utilization typically suggests more efficient procurement and administrative implementation of national programs.
Despite the overall national improvement, several major departments saw significant declines in their cash utilization rates.

Cash utilization by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) dropped from 94 percent in July 2025 to 86.2 percent in July 2026, leaving ₱44.2 billion in unused cash—the largest among departments. This came alongside a massive cut in its total NCA releases, which fell from ₱610 billion to ₱320.1 billion.

Similarly, the Department of Education (DepEd) saw its utilization rate dip from 97 percent to 93.1 percent, leaving ₱35.3 billion unused—more than triple the ₱10.7 billion recorded a year ago. The Department of Transportation’s (DOTr) cash utilization also fell from 92 percent to 85.7 percent, leaving ₱7 billion unused.

Other agencies reporting declines were the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), which dropped from 86 percent to 72 percent; the Office of the President (OP), from 89 percent to 69.4 percent; and the Civil Service Commission (CSC), from 92 percent to 73.3 percent.

Further, the Department of Finance’s (DOF) utilization rate fell from 96 percent to 90 percent, leaving ₱1.5 billion unused. This decline came alongside a massive reduction in total releases to the department, which plummeted from ₱50.8 billion to ₱15 billion.

In contrast, several departments and agencies showed notable resilience and improved efficiency. For one, the Department of National Defense (DND) saw a solid improvement, with its utilization rate rising to 98.4 percent from 93 percent a year ago.

Other agencies that posted improved utilization rates included the Department of Agriculture (DA), which rose to 79.4 percent from 72 percent; the Office of the Ombudsman, which increased to 96.5 percent from 93 percent; and the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), which inched up to 91.4 percent from 91 percent.
Under SPFs, allocations to local government units (ALGU) achieved a 100-percent utilization rate, up from 99 percent.

However, some agencies that previously reported solid performance lost ground. The Judiciary saw its utilization rate drop to 91.8 percent, while the Commission on Elections (Comelec) fell to 76.9 percent.

articles.title: Prolonged flooding puts Calasiao, Dagupan residents on edge
articles.summary: CALASIAO, PANGASINAN — Prolonged flooding brought out by the raging rains from the southwest monsoon, or "habagat", has disrupted daily life in parts of Calasiao and Dagupan City, with some residents…

blocks.text: CALASIAO, PANGASINAN — Prolonged flooding brought out by the raging rains from the southwest monsoon, or "habagat", has disrupted daily life in parts of Calasiao and Dagupan City, with some residents reportedly dealing with floodwaters for nearly a month.
In Calasiao, residents have resorted to riding "kuliglig", a farm machinery, locally used form of transportation, to get through flooded roads and reach their destinations.
Floodwaters in some communities have reportedly reached waist level, forcing residents to find alternative ways to move around and, in some cases, seek safer ground.
The persistent flooding has also resulted in prolonged class suspensions in affected areas, disrupting the education of students for weeks.
In Dagupan City, the flooding is at times aggravated by high tide, which can slow the drainage of floodwaters in low-lying communities.

The prolonged inundation has also prompted residents to raise questions about the effectiveness of existing flood-control measures, including road-widening and road-elevation projects, in addressing recurring flooding.
Residents say the current situation is among the most prolonged flooding episodes they have experienced in recent memory.
While claims that the flooding is the worst or longest since 1972 .: for many residents, the water has stayed far too long.

articles.summary: US targets Iran’s Larak Island in first exchange of fire in more than a month, sparking reprisals against US forces in Jordan and UAE

blocks.text: US and Iran trade strikes for first time in a month
Welcome to our live coverage as hostilities between the US and Iran flared again for the first time in a month, with American strikes on Iran prompting retaliation from Tehran.

A supertanker caught ⁠fire and was brought to a complete ⁠halt after ⁠hitting two naval mines in ⁠the southern strait of Hormuz, Iran state ⁠TV reported on Monday, ​citing ‌a statement ‌from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

The IRGC said the tanker had been attempting to pass through the waterway illegally. It ‌did not identify the vessel or provide information ​about its crew. It warned that other ships violating ⁠its security rules would face ​the ​same fate and ​said compliance with ​its regulations ‌for ​passage ​through the strait was mandatory.

On Sunday, the US said it carried out airstrikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the strait, with an American official saying the IRGC was preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the narrow waterway.

The IRGC said on Monday it attacked two US military airbases with ballistic missiles in Washington-allied Jordan, causing “heavy damage”, state media reported. Jordan’s army said it had intercepted eight missiles, without stating their origin.

Iran said later it had targeted US military personnel at an airbase in the United Arab Emirates. Donald Trump later claimed on social media that Iran’s energy hub of Kharg Island was “being blown to smithereens”.
In other developments:

items: Iran’s supreme leader called the US and Israel enemies of all Islamic nations. In a written message issued six months on from the start of the war, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei also urged rulers of Muslim nations to “know your real enemy, understand its plans and confront it”, the official Irna news agency reported.

Israel’s Shin Bet security agency says it urgently evacuated prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s oldest son from the US due to a threat against him. In a brief statement the Associated Press obtained on Sunday, the Shin Bet confirmed there had been a “significant threat” to Yair Netanyahu, without elaborating.
US treasury secretary Scott Bessent will step up efforts to isolate Iran economically as he hosts G20 counterparts this week, a US official has said.

Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian is due to take part in a summit starting on Monday of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a regional bloc that seeks to be a counter-influence to the west. Russia’s Vladimir Putin is expected to hold separate bilateral talks with Pezeshkian and China’s Xi Jinping, among other leaders, a Kremlin spokesperson said.

articles.title: Arm cache unearthed in Quezon
articles.summary: LOPEZ, Quezon- An arm cache belonging to the New People’s Army (NPA) was unearthed by government forces in Barangay Santa Rosa on Friday, Aug. 28, in this town. According to the report of the 201st…

blocks.text: LOPEZ, Quezon- An arm cache belonging to the New People’s Army (NPA) was unearthed by government forces in Barangay Santa Rosa on Friday, Aug. 28, in this town.

According to the report of the 201st Infantry Brigade, the combined forces of the 85th Infantry Battalion, the 417th Quezon Police Mobile Force Company, and the Lopez Municipal Police Station discovered the arms cache following information given by a former rebel.

The location of the arms cache was revealed by a rebel returnee who disclosed that following an armed encounter between the government forces and the NPA rebels in Barangay Cogorin, this town, on April 23, 2025. The rebel withdrew toward Barangay Santa Rosa and buried assorted firearms and other war materiel belonging to the detached squad of the dismantled Platun Reymark.

Recovered from the cache were an improvised explosive device (IED), an improvised hand grenade, a .45-caliber pistol, a .38-caliber pistol, a magazine, and live ammunition, two copies of “Piling Mga Sulating Militar ni Mao Zedong,” and medical supplies.

Army Maj. General Arsenio Sadural, commander of the 2nd Infantry Division, said the recovery reflects the continuing effort to consolidate government gains against the remaining communist armed groups in Southern Tagalog.

“The dismantling of an armed group does not end with the neutralization of its manpower. We must also account for the weapons, explosives, logistics, and other resources it leaves behind to ensure they can no longer be retrieved and used to rebuild its capabilities,” Sadural said.
He also encouraged remaining NPA members to consider the experience of former rebels who are now helping communities move away from armed conflict.

“Those who have chosen to return to the folds of the law are showing that there is a meaningful role for them in building peace. We continue to call on those who remain in the armed movement to come home and take the same opportunity to begin again,” Sadural added.

The 2nd Division continues to work closely with its partners in the security sector, local government units, former rebels, and communities to locate remaining war materiel and prevent the remnants of dismantled NPA units from rebuilding their capabilities in Southern Tagalog.

articles.title: Algeria president seeks death penalty for arsonists after deadly forest fires
articles.summary: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune says he is not ruling out foul play after 100 wildfires were recorded.

blocks.text: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has said he wants to reinstate the death penalty for arsonists, following a wave of forest fires that have killed at least 12 people.

The president ordered the justice ministry to introduce changes to the criminal law introducing capital punishment for arsonists. Capital punishment remains in the country's penal code for some offences, but no execution has been carried out since 1993.
More than 100 wildfires have been recorded in recent days in the north-east of the country, most of which have been extinguished.
On Saturday, Tebboune said he did not rule out foul play.
The Algerian president said necessary investigations would be carried out especially in view of the intensity of the fires.
On Sunday, he gave a 15 September deadline for amendments to provide for the death sentence for anyone convicted of intentionally starting a fire in forested areas.
Under the current law, deliberately starting forest fires is punishable by up to 30 years in prison, or life imprisonment in certain cases.
Deadly blazes swept through large swathes of northern Algeria last week, causing widespread destruction, injuring dozens and displacing thousands of people.
The fires erupted amid an intense heatwave in northern Africa, with Algeria and Tunisia particularly affected.

Algerian civil authorities were on Sunday afternoon still battling to battle some of the fires, with the Algerian Press Service noting that 18 out 19 fires that had broken out in the previous 24 hours had been extinguished
The Algerian president ordered that compensation be paid to the families who have been affected, as well as repairs to damaged homes and essential services.
He said there would be investigations into the extent of the damage and losses caused by the fires.
While Algeria regularly experiences forest fires around the summer months, climate change has exacerbated the intensity and severity of recent wildfires in the country.

articles.title: Body found in Muntinlupa identified
articles.summary: The body of a man who was pulled out from a drainage ditch in Muntinlupa last Aug. 27 was identified by his former live-in partner. The Muntinlupa police previously stated that the body of the man…

blocks.text: The body of a man who was pulled out from a drainage ditch in Muntinlupa last Aug. 27 was identified by his former live-in partner.
The Muntinlupa police previously stated that the body of the man was discovered by a resident through an underground drainage opening under a bridge between Barangays Alabang and Bayanan.
Personnel from the Muntinlupa City Fire Station’s Katarungan Fire Station needed to smash a hole on a sidewalk along the National Road in Barangay Bayanan to retrieve the body.
Following the discovery, investigators made efforts to identify the body. Last Aug. 30, they interviewed J. Flores, 38, a scavenger.
She claimed that she was a former live-in partner of the dead man who she identified as Efren Pineda Jr., 37, a scavenger.
The police also identified Flores’ acquaintance, R. Valdez, 38, also a scavenger. She told the police that she gave clothes to Pineda consisting of a yellow green polo shirt and dark blue pants.
Together with the police, Flores and Valdez went to Our Lady of Loreto Funeral Homes in Taguig City to identify the body.

According to the police, the two women positively identified the body even though it was in an advanced stage of decomposition based on his clothes, which were the ones Valdez gave to him. Flores also identified the body through a bump in the right upper forehead.
Flores said Pineda engaged in scavenging activities in Bayanan, telling the police that he would frequently go underneath the creek and in the drainage canal.
She said she had an argument with Pineda last Aug. 2, the last time she saw Pineda alive. After this, she said, he went to the underground drainage canal where his body was later discovered.
The Muntinlupa police are exerting efforts to locate Pineda’s family and relatives

articles.title: P12.2M in presidential aid released to 61 Bacolod villages
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - This highly-urbanized city has released P12.2 million in financial assistance under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s "Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” (BBM) program to 61 barangays for…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY - This highly-urbanized city has released P12.2 million in financial assistance under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s "Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” (BBM) program to 61
barangays for their socio-civic projects.

Bacolod City Mayor Greg Gasataya, in coordination with the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and the Office of the President, led the distribution of checks to representatives of all barangays during a recent ceremonial turnover at the Bacolod City Government Center (BCGC) lobby.

Each barangay received a total allocation of P200,000, which included P100,000 for five Presidential Scholars, and P100,000 for a community development project identified by the barangay. Each scholar received P20,000 in educational assistance.
Gasataya thanked the President and the national government for extending the program to all barangays, acknowledging the urgency and necessity of this program.
He said this is the first time the national government has equally provided the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) to all barangays, regardless of population and size.

Gasataya also thanked barangay officials for their cooperation in completing the requirements necessary for the release of the funds, emphasizing that the program is intended to directly benefit their constituents.
He required all barangay captains to submit signed certifications attesting that none of their selected scholars are family members or relatives of any incumbent barangay official.
“This is to ensure that those who will benefit from the scholarship program are the ones who need it most,” the mayor stressed.
DILG City Director Christian Nagaynay emphasized that accountability and transparency remain central to the program’s implementation.

He noted that barangays are required to publicly post information on the distribution of assistance, including aid provided to scholars, and submit a fund utilization report every 30 days for the community projects they implement.

The city government reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with barangay officials and national government agencies to ensure that the funds are utilized properly, efficiently, and transparently.

Woman confesses to pretending son had cancer to raise money
A German woman on trial in Giessen, north of Frankfurt in Hesse, has confessed to pretending her young son had cancer to raise money online.
Her lawyer said in court that she accepted and admitted to the allegations "without any reservation" and regretted what had happened.
She's accused of obtaining a total of €358,000 (roughly $415,000 at current exchange rates) in donations between September 2021 and October 2024. The boy was aged 5 to 8 during this time period.
The woman is alleged to have come up with the idea after a dermatological examination revealed an issue that turned out to be benign and require no further treatment.
She then allegedly claimed that her son was suffering from malignant melanoma and urgently required expensive specialist treatment in the US, claims she also made to the media and online.
Prosecutor Kai Karges said that hundreds of individuals and charities responded to the calls, and said that the child also believed he had cancer.
The fraud was uncovered when the boy's pediatrician saw the calls for donations on social media and alerted child protection services. He has since been taken into care.

articles.title: Marcos allies say OP's P4.5B proposed confi, intel fund for 2027 justified
articles.summary: House good government and public accountability panel vice chairperson Benny Abante on Monday defended President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr."s proposed P4.5 billion confidential and intelligence…

blocks.text: House good government and public accountability panel vice chairperson Benny Abante on Monday defended President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr.’s proposed P4.5 billion confidential and intelligence fund (CIF) for 2027.

“I think we have to remember that the President is also the commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces. Therefore, he has all the right to have a confidential fund,” Abante said during an online press conference.
“Having said that, the President really needs CIF,” he added.
The Office of the President’s P4.5 billion proposed CIF for 2027 is the same level as this year.
Of the P4.5 billion, P2.25 billion accounts for confidential funds while another P2.25 billion is for intelligence funds.

The 2015 Joint Circular governing the use of CIF defines confidential expenses as those expenses pertaining/related to surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.

The same 2015 guidelines, on the other hand, define intelligence expenses as those related to intelligence information gathering activities of uniformed and military personnel, and intelligence practitioners that have a direct impact on national security.
Overall, the Marcos administration proposed a P10.77 billion worth of CIF for 2027, down from this year’s P11.8 billion allocation.
Of the proposed amount, P4.368 billion is for confidential funds and P6.405 billion for intelligence funds.
Abante, however, noted that such CIF must be properly accounted for.
Deputy Speaker and La Union Rep. Paolo Ortega V agreed.
“Importante kung merong nailaan o naibigay na pondo, dapat tama po ’yung paggamit, tama ’yung pinuntahan, at tama po ’yung proseso na sinusunod,” Ortega said.
(The fund should be used appropriately, meaning accountability process must be followed to the letter.)

Senate finance panel chairperson JV Ejercito earlier said that the CIF should be limited to agencies whose mandates involve law enforcement, intelligence and national security, and that the OP falls squarely within that justification.
Ejercito even said that the President, by the virtue of his position, will be subjected to threats.

One of the allegations of the House prosecution team in its impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte is alleged betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution for apparently threatening to kill President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and then-Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez via a hitman if she herself was killed.
Abante, however, stressed that presidential confidential funds must still be properly used and accounted for.
“Kinakailangan po nating malaman lamang paano gagamitin ’yan, saan gagamitin ’yan,” he said.
(We need to know where these funds will be used for.)
Deputy Speaker and La Union Rep. Paolo Ortega V agreed, saying the key is ensuring that confidential funds are properly spent and established processes are followed.
(If there is an allocation for such, it is very important to ensure that it is disbursed appropriately and in accordance with accountability processes.)
Abolish CIF

But for opposition lawmaker Alliance of Concerned Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio of and Gabriela party-list Sarah Elago, the confidential fund spending of Vice President Sara Duterte which was marred with unusual recipient names should already prompt the abolition of the CIF allocation.

"That is why we have always called for the CIF abolition. The budget should not have confidential allocations. It should be transparent, and there are other ways to ensure that security concerns are addressed," Tinio said.

"Nobody should be exempted from accountability, especially the Office of the President. We should abolish CIF and realign the fund for basic services such as health, education, housing agriculture, among others," Elago added. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Corals in decline globally, nearly half a century of data shows
articles.summary: New research highlights the declines in living corals in reefs around the world, showing the unprecedented twin-danger of human-caused climate change and an expected record El Niño.

image.caption: The painstaking work of underwater surveys, seen here in southern Thailand in 2024, is helping catalog the declines in hard coral cover around the world. Data shows the 'window of recovery' for reefs is getting shorter, says lead author Manuel González Rivero. (Lillian Swuanrumpha/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: The proportion of the world's reefs with living, stony stalks of hard corals is down significantly, according to a new global report on these vital ecosystems.

And as these reefs stare down a potentially record-breaking El Niño peak just months away, new research suggests the naturally-occurring warming phenomenon might be more intense than it used to be — a trend captured in coral skeletons.

The Status of Coral Reefs of the World 2025 says marine heatwaves and global bleaching events have taken a repetitive toll on the world's corals. This climate change-fuelled heat stress has driven hard coral coverage globally to roughly 25 per cent.

"Coral cover around the world used to be above 30 or 40 per cent back in the '80s," said Manuel González Rivero, lead author with the Australian Institute of Marine Science and global co-ordinator of the Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network.

But he adds that the main takeaway is "not only that we're seeing a loss in coral cover, but that the window of recovery is getting shorter and shorter," given extreme ocean heat events have been occurring more frequently.
Which is why the rate of recent coral cover decline relative to previous decades is also worrying at 9.5 per cent.

"This decline … is showing that we're losing big chunks of coral from the majority of the world's coral reefs — and it's associated with climate change,” said Emily Darling, director of Coral Reefs at the Wildlife Conservation Society, who was not involved in the report.
Windows closing

This status report is the seventh by the Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network, using data from close to 37,000 reef sites. Hard coral cover shows a clear downward trend of loss and recovery stretching back to 1980.
The declines, notably, come after a global bleaching event, or GBE — where hotter ocean temperatures cause corals to expel the symbiotic microscopic algae inside, turning them a ghostly white.

While bleaching itself is not a death sentence, it leaves the corals weak and susceptible to disease and death, starting a domino effect for all the microorganisms and larger marine species that depend on them as a source of food and shelter.
Corals can recover, if given time. However, of the four recorded GBEs, three have happened in just the last 15 years — with the latest only recently declared over.

"Corals have had nine months, just over a year, to try to recover," said Darling, "and now they're facing down the strongest 'super' El Niño on record and the hottest ocean temperatures ever recorded."
The lack of a decent recovery window means even resilient species, which Darling's recent research focused on, are getting hit repeatedly.
Good news about coral reefs and their climate resilience
Uneven declines

Of the 10 regions monitored in this report, Rivero says, the declines are seen in four — Australia, the eastern Pacific, the Caribbean and the area from the Persian Gulf out to the Arabian Sea. Other regions are stable, if not growing.

Corals in growth areas, however, are not immune to the added heat of the oceans. As humans burn fossil fuels, oceans absorb 90 per cent of the excess heat trapped by those greenhouse gases, leading to more intense and frequent marine heatwaves.

In the western Indian Ocean, which saw a significant increase in coral cover, the report notes "data sparsity prior to 1998 and uneven monitoring efforts" can "limit the accuracy of estimates of hard coral cover," adding that it and other regions may have actually experienced a decline.

Darling says confidence in the data has improved, because the number of people doing the diving, measuring and counting has gone up. But she also echoes the report's call for sustained funding and standardizing monitoring methods in order to better understand the global picture of reefs.
"There's still hope for increasing resilience to coral reefs," Darling said, but warned that ocean temperatures are getting hotter.
"And we are slowly boiling corals to death."
LISTEN | Repetitive strain on our oceans:
Quirks and Quarks15:12Climate change is making marine heat waves more frequent and intense – and that's changing life in the ocean
Action on a global and regional level

While the report's data brings the decline of corals into focus, the calls to action are also clear. Given reefs support an estimated 25 per cent of marine life and contribute to the economy and coastal protection of more than 100 countries, the authors advocate for global and local action.

On a regional level, "second-stage interventions" such as limiting overfishing, pollution and coastal development can "increase the resilience of coral reefs and their likelihood of surviving and recovering from extreme events," according to the report.
But on a global level, Rivero says, we need to stop emitting greenhouse gases by burning fossil fuels.

"Climate change is driving the warming of the oceans and that warming of oceans is driving the decline that we've seen on coral reefs. There's no doubt about it," Rivero told CBC News from Townsville, Australia.
El Niño may be getting worse

The current danger is more heat ahead with El Niño gaining strength on top of a baseline raised by climate change. But new research published in Science says recent El Niño events have been stronger — and corals themselves are a calendar of proof.

"Corals can live for decades to centuries, and in the chemistry of their skeleton, they preserve a history of the conditions that they grow under," said Julia Cole, paleoclimatologist and chair of the department of earth and environmental sciences at the University of Michigan.
"In warm conditions, corals are building their skeleton with a different chemistry than during cold conditions."

items: Oceans dangerously acidic from carbon emissions, report warns
El Niño is here, and it’s already looking like it could be 'mind-blowing'

blocks.text: By studying the geochemistry of corals in the Galápagos — what Cole refers to as the heart of El Niño country — the study was able to go effectively back in time. It found evidence of stronger El Niño events in the last 40 years compared to a time before 1850.

Cole cautions that El Niño is complex and this is not predictive of future events, but there is a shift in the last few decades as the world has gotten warmer from the burning of fossil fuels. For corals, that's not good news.
"It really adds to this urgency and also a deep concern.... If this is where we are now, where are we going in the next 10 years?" Darling told CBC News.
"Because we know that a lot of this warming is committed and even if we turn things around today we still have a ways to go before the ecological systems on our planet start to respond to that."

articles.title: Weather tracker: Warm Yellow Sea strengthens storms in South Korea
articles.summary:
More than 200mm of rain forecast in parts of South Korea, while parts of southern Europe to be 10C above average

South Korea’s prime minister, Han Seong-sook, met officials to prepare for…

blocks.text: South Korea’s prime minister, Han Seong-sook, met officials to prepare for heavy rain expected this week, with rainfall totals across central and northern parts of the country forecast to exceed 200mm in some areas.

South Korea was battered by heavy rainfall earlier this month and some areas were particularly hard hit. Over the weekend further thunderstorms pushed into the region and these are expected to cause disruption through Monday. This heavy rain is caused by a series of severe thunderstorms that developed over the Yellow Sea, on the western side of South Korea, and will slowly push eastwards on Monday before easing on Tuesday. These storms have been strengthened by the very warm Yellow Sea, which now has a surface temperature of 29C, 4C above the climatological average.

Thailand is also under a warning for heavy to very heavy rain as the country passes the middle of its monsoon season, which runs from May to October. In the Philippines, the province of Tarlac has been placed under a state of calamity due to prolonged heavy rain in August.

Nearby in the north Pacific, which has had an active typhoon and tropical storm season so far and will continue to do so this week, several tropical systems have the potential to develop. Last week, Typhoon Bang-lang and Tropical Storm Etau developed very close to each other in the north-west Pacific and both travelled northwards, although neither made landfall. Another two systems near the Philippines and China have a medium to high chance of developing into a tropical cyclone. For this to happen, wind speeds need to reach 39mph (63km/h). Across in the eastern north Pacific, Karina has developed into a category 1 hurricane and is expected to head just to the north of Hawaii but is not forecast to make landfall. Tropical Storm Lowell is expected to strengthen into a hurricane on Tuesday before passing just to the south of Hawaii.

As Europe reaches the end of its record-breaking meteorological summer, the hot weather is showing no signs of easing off for the start of September. The heat is expected to intensify again later this week across central and southern parts of Europe, with temperatures rising to 10C above the climatological average. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, temperatures could reach about 40C by the weekend, falling just shy of the country’s all-time temperature record of 43.1C, set in 2007.

articles.title: DSWD releases 2.3 million food packs to families hit by floods, landslides
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) has released about 2.3 million family food packs to families affected by successive storms and flooding, while maintaining millions more in…

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) has released about 2.3 million family food packs to families affected by successive storms and flooding, while maintaining millions more in reserve as the southwest monsoon or “habagat” continues to affect parts of the country.
DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian said the 2.3 million food packs released over the past several weeks represent one of the largest relief distributions in the agency’s history.
“That is one of the largest releases of family food packs in our history because we are talking about almost four weeks and 2.3 million food packs,” he added.
Gatchalian said the DSWD would continue distributing and replenishing its relief supplies as more communities deal with the effects of recent weather disturbances.
DSWD currently has 3,586,913 family food packs, 301,570 ready-to-eat food packs, and 282,931 non-food items prepositioned in strategic locations nationwide.

The relief supplies are being used to augment assistance for communities affected by Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, as well as recent flooding in Central Luzon and parts of the National Capital Region (NCR).
DSWD field offices remain in coordination with local government units (LGUs) to monitor weather developments, assess emergency situations, and respond to requests for additional relief supplies.
“The ones distributing to the beneficiaries or victims are the local government units because, remember, they are the first responders. We only provide augmentation,” Gatchalian said.

“As far as we know, we have complied with all the requests we have received from local government units. But some local government units are already asking for a second or third round, and rightfully so, because this disaster has gone on for quite some time,” he added.
Repacking hubs and supply chains nationwide continue to operate to replenish prepositioned relief supplies and ensure that resources remain available for communities affected by disasters.

articles.title: Historical, mordern heroes honored in Zambo celebration of National Heroes Day
articles.summary: ZAMBOANGA CITY- Zamboanga city joined the nation in commemorating National Heroes’ Day through a program held at Plaza Rizal on Monday, August 31. The program, which started with a flag raising…

blocks.text: (Photo courtesy of Zamboanga City PIO)
ZAMBOANGA CITY- Zamboanga city joined the nation in commemorating National Heroes’ Day through a program held at Plaza Rizal on Monday, August 31.

The program, which started with a flag raising ceremony, was participated in by officials and members of the security sector, government officials and personnel, Boy Scouts of the Philippines and academic institutions.
During the program, officials honored both historic and modern day heroes as both offer their lives in service to the public.
Mayor Khymer Olaso honored historical heroes and said that their heroism lives on through the modern heroes of today.
"The true meaning of heroism is the willingness to serve others without expecting anything in return. We must do more for our city and continue to rise above every challenge, "Olaso said.

Meanwhile, WestMinCom Deputy Commander BGen. Bayani Curaming, Deputy Commander for Internal Defense Operations said that heroism and courage from our national heroes continue to live on in the present time.
Curaming lauded active-duty members in the security sector and civil servants who risk personal comfort to serve the public.
"Let us show the nation that bravery born in August 1896 lives on in Zamboanga City," Curaming urged.

articles.title: Malacañang defends Marcos' honorary degree from PLM
articles.summary: Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Monday hit back at those questioning the honorary Doctor of Laws degree recently conferred by the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) on…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 3:27pm

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Monday hit back at those questioning the honorary Doctor of Laws degree recently conferred by the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) on President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr.

In a video message, Castro explained that “honoris causa” is an honorary degree bestowed upon a person who has attained a high-ranking position or has made significant contributions to a community or the nation.

“Marami kasi ang hindi nakakaunawa marahil ng katagang honoris causa. Ang mga tumutuligsa rito ay mga taong kung hindi man mapagmataas, ay mga kumakalaban sa Pangulo---the usual obstructionists at destabilizers, o ‘yung mga sumasakay lang sa nakikita sa social media, pero hindi nauunawaan ang totoong issue,” she said.

(Many perhaps don’t understand the term honoris causa. Those who criticize it are either arrogant people or those who oppose the President—the usual obstructionists and destabilizers, or simply those who jump on what they see on social media without understanding the real issue.)

“Ang titulong honoris causa ay isang honorary degree. Ito ay isang pagkilala o parangal para sa taong mataas ang naabot na posisyon, may mga mahahalagang naiambag sa komunidad o mga nagawa para sa bansa,” she added.

(The title honoris causa is an honorary degree. It is a form of recognition or an award bestowed upon an individual who has attained a high-ranking position and made significant contributions to the community or the nation.)
The Palace official emphasized that the honorary degree is not achieved through traditional education, by entering law school, or passing the Bar examinations.
She also underscored the need to clarify the matter for individuals being misled by others through fake news or sheer arrogance.
Marcos received the highest honorary degree conferred by the PLM---a Doctor of Laws, Honoris Causa---during the institution’s 58th commencement exercises on Thursday, August 27.
The President said he accepted the honor “with gratitude, mindful of the responsibility that comes with it.”
According to Castro, Filipinos should not forget the actions done by the President to be granted such a distinction, most especially maintaining the country’s rights in the West Philippine Sea.

“Ang pagpaputol ng 300-meter floating barrier na inilagay ng China Coast Guard sa Scarborough Shoal noong September 2023 para harangin ang ating mangingisda na makapasok at makapangisda sa traditional fishing lagoon ay isang gawain ng isang matapat na leader,” she said.

(Ordering the removal of the 300-meter floating barrier installed by the Chinese Coast Guard at the Scarborough Shoal in September 2023 to block our fishermen from entering and fishing in the traditional fishing lagoon was an act of a good leader.)
Castro said that Marcos also respects human life and due process, and fights against the abuse of power. She pointed out that he even initiated investigations into corruption issues.
She also said the President has ensured the country would not run out of fuel supplies amid the Middle East crisis, and also secured fertilizer supplies to protect farmers.

“Ang masagip ang isang kababayan mula sa death row, sentensyang pinataw ng ibang bansa; pagsagip sa 17 OFW sa Qatar sa kasong illegal assembly, at sa 24 Filipinos na nakadetained sa Eastern Siberia sa Russia. Ito ay nagawa ng Pangulo dahil sa maganda niyang relasyon sa leaders ng Qatar at Russia,” she added.

(The President saved a fellow Filipino from death row—a sentence imposed by a foreign nation, and rescued 17 OFWs in Qatar facing illegal assembly charges, as well as 24 Filipinos detained in Eastern Siberia, Russia.
